title: Camera profile wizard: build, check and choose per-model, per-style profiles from your own photos (GUI for calibrate)
author: radialmonster
body:
`lightcraft-cli calibrate` builds a camera profile from your own photos. It pools colour pairs from each raw and its embedded camera JPEG, and writes `<model>.json` to the camera-profiles folder, where it replaces the built-in profile for that model. Only people comfortable with a terminal can use it today, and many users don't know camera profiles exist (see #1281). A guided GUI flow would open it up to everyone.

## What exists today (main)

- `lightcraft-cli calibrate [--max N] [--out DIR] FOLDERS/FILES…`
- At most 300 files by default, spread evenly over the folders given, and at most 4000 pairs per photo.
- At least 5 usable photos per model.
- It writes to the camera-profiles folder unless `--out` is given.
- It runs in parallel and reports per model on stderr.
- Profiles are read once per process, and a local profile replaces the built-in one.

## Proposal

A camera profile wizard that builds one profile per camera model **and picture style** from the user's photos. It checks each profile on held-out photos before installing it, installs it without a restart, and lets each photo use the profile that matches the style it was shot with.

### 1. Read the picture style from every raw

title: Windows 11: dragging the window across monitors with different display scales makes it balloon and jump (winit 0.30.13 mixed-DPI drag)
author: msaulc
body:
## Summary

LightCraft locks winit 0.30.13 without a winit patch, so it should have the Windows 11 mixed-DPI drag bug found in GridCraft (storytold/gridcraft#760, fix in storytold/gridcraft#761). Dragging the window across the boundary between monitors with different display scales makes it flip between the two scales and grow by their ratio.

**Expected effect in LightCraft:** the window balloons and jumps during the drag. Past 8192 px the surface fails to configure; LightCraft's window device logs wgpu errors instead of crashing, but the window can't render at that size.

This comes from reading LightCraft's code at its current `main`, not from a run of LightCraft. GridCraft, on the same stack, was reproduced and fixed on hardware.

## What happens (measured in GridCraft)

Windows 11 24H2, a 3440×1440 monitor at 100 % next to a 3840×2400 panel at 250 %. Dragging the window from the 250 % panel toward the top edge of the 100 % monitor, client size per step: 3600×2250 → 1440×900 → 3600×2250 → **9048×5757**. GridCraft then crashed in wgpu's `Surface::configure`: `Requested was (9048, 5757), maximum extent for either dimension is 8192`.

## Cause

- **winit 0.30.13's `WM_DPICHANGED` handling during a live drag** (rust-windowing/winit#4041, #4600). winit replaces the rect Windows suggests with its own and nudges it back onto the monitor being left, which triggers another DPI change. winit master fixed this in 488c036a (#4341), but only for 0.31; eframe 0.36 needs 0.30.
- **Surface size limit:** LightCraft's window device requests exactly 8192 px (`apps/lightcraft/src/window_gpu.rs`) and logs uncaptured errors.

## Fix used in GridCraft (storytold/gridcraft#761)

1. Pin winit to the single commit of rust-windowing/winit#4694, its 0.30.x backport (+21/−34 lines on top of v0.30.13), with no vendored copy:
   ```toml
   [patch.crates-io]
   winit = { git = "https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit", rev = "39c4009c41e5977d779cf8a365792c8153ca77c5" }
   ```

## Symptom

#1028: on a Sony ILCE-6400 photo of sunlit wet rock, small reflections ("sparkles") look green in a full-size LightCraft export, where the camera's JPEG shows them near white. The clipped centres themselves render white; the colour is in the unclipped pixels around them: in a 900×400 crop, 17 % of the bright output pixels are green or cyan (and 12 % yellow), and none of them has a clipped channel. The reporter's photo was shared for testing only, so it is described here in numbers.

It is not specific to clipping. On a public sample it shows as thin yellow and green outlines along sharp white edges.

## Public repro (CC0)

raw.pixls.us, Sony ILCE-6400, DSC00475.ARW (id 3151, "14bit compressed", sha256 `339e7d83e030b31509ff201d4130a9bcede9945a12b07ec6a48a8b02cd499802`): https://raw.pixls.us/data/Sony/ILCE-6400/DSC00475.ARW

```
lightcraft-cli render DSC00475.ARW -o out.png
```

Look at the white ferry's superstructure and mast against the sky at 1:1, around x 3880-4180, y 1640-1750 of the 6000×4000 export: yellow and cyan 1-px outlines on the white edges. Nothing in that window is clipped (green peaks at 0.73 of white; in the whole ferry region 5 of 487,500 green samples reach the clip). Over the ferry (x 3300-4800, y 1550-2200), of the pixels within 2 px of near-white pixels (every channel >= 200), main 701f78ea renders 10.4 % yellow and 1.3 % green (mean a\* -3.8, C\* 14.0); with the mosaic white-balanced before the demosaic, 1.6 % and 0.0 % (a\* +0.3, C\* 9.7).

title: High ISO: single outlier photosites survive noise reduction as coloured dots
author: PiMinusMax
body:
### Summary

At high ISO, single photosites in the raw mosaic read far above their neighbours. Demosaicing turns each one into a saturated dot of 1–3 px, mostly red on this sensor. Neither colour nor luminance noise reduction removes these dots. With the colour NR of #815 and the luminance NR of #1129 they get *more* visible, because the noise around them goes away and the dot stays. Main 0.7.1 shows the same dots.

Example: Sony α77 II (ILCA-77M2), ISO 8000, 1/30 s, a garden at night. An automatic search finds **367** isolated red dots in the grass of one 24 MP frame.

![Red dots in grass](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PiMinusMax/lightcraft/0184fcf155cc8c8d062fd12d89c8d07ae6f3dd33/outlier_dots_a77_iso8000.png)
*Fig. 1: the seven strongest dots, 24 × 24 px crops at 6×. Main 0.7.1 at the raw defaults (Color 25), then the #815/#1129 prototype without NR, with Color 25, with Color 25 + Luminance 50, and with the mosaic outlier filter proposed below. Main's Color 25 leaves the colour noise almost as it is (#815).*

### Not fixed hot pixels

These are not the camera's hot pixels at fixed positions. In the two neighbouring frames (same camera, ISO and exposure), only 2 of the 8 strongest positions are raised again. The outliers are random per frame. The ARW carries no defect list for them. DNG opcodes and Panasonic's marked pixels are already repaired elsewhere.

### Why the noise reductions keep them

- **Colour NR** (#815, joint method with speck brake): the brake removes isolated *colour* specks but leaves points that are also brighter than their surroundings, so stars and small lights are not eaten. These dots are brighter, so they count as light. Colour 25 lowers their red by about a third (median red excess over the 11 × 11 neighbourhood 0.51 → 0.33, linear).
- **Luminance NR** (#1129 prototype): it recognises the brightness spike as an outlier and removes 58 % of it, but it changes Y only and leaves the colour. Afterwards the red-to-brightness ratio of the dots…

title: Feature Request: Native Film Negative Conversion Tool (similar to Negative Lab Pro / Darktable Negadoctor)
author: MatthiasToberer
body:
Currently, LightCraft is an amazing tool for digital RAW files. However, for hybrid analog/digital photographers who scan their own film negatives (using a digital camera or scanner), there is no native way to easily invert and color-correct film negatives. Doing this manually via inverted RGB curves is tedious and rarely yields color-accurate results.

I would love to see a native "Film Conversion" panel or module built directly into LightCraft. Key functionalities should include:
1. A dedicated "Invert" toggle that mathematically reverses the negative image based on the raw data (without breaking the sliders like exposure/contrast, which invert their behavior when using manual curves).
2. A color sampler to click on the unexposed film border (film base) to automatically subtract the orange mask of color negative films.
3. Standard film profiles or simple algorithms to automatically correct balance and dynamic range (similar to how Negative Lab Pro or Darktable's "Negadoctor" module work).

The current alternative is manually flipping the Tone Curve, which makes subsequent editing with the "Light" and "Color" panels extremely unintuitive because all sliders operate in reverse.

title: Feature request: optional macOS system RAW decoder (Core Image CIRAWFilter) as a fallback for preview-only raws
author: bxshi
body:
## Summary

On macOS, offer an **opt-in fallback to Apple's system RAW engine** (Core Image `CIRAWFilter`) for raw files that LightCraft's built-in decoder can only open from their embedded preview.

## Motivation

macOS ships a RAW decoder that Apple keeps up to date for a long list of cameras, and apps like Affinity Photo and Pixelmator Pro / Photomator use it. When LightCraft's decoder doesn't cover a camera or a compression variant yet, the photo falls back to its embedded JPEG, which can't really be edited (lower resolution, baked-in look). A system fallback would fill those gaps while the built-in decoder catches up.

The current example is compressed ORF (#233). Tested on **LightCraft 0.7.1**, macOS, Apple M2 Max:

| File | LightCraft 0.7.1 | macOS system decoder (`sips`) |
|---|---|---|
| Olympus E-P3 `.orf` | preview only, exports at 3200 × 2400 | full 4032 × 3024 |
| Panasonic DC-ZS99 `.rw2` | full 5184 × 3888 ✅ | full 5184 × 3888 |
| Sony ILCE-7RM5 `.arw` | full 9504 × 6336 ✅ | full 9504 × 6336 |

## Proposal

- The built-in decoder stays the default and the only engine on Windows and Linux.
- On macOS, when a raw would otherwise be preview-only, decode it with `CIRAWFilter` instead. Request linear, scene-referred output (no tone curve, no default look) so it goes into the normal pipeline like any other demosaiced raw.
- Show which engine decoded a photo in the Info panel / "preview only" note, and add a preference to turn the fallback off.
- Optionally, a per-photo or per-camera "decode with macOS" override for comparing results.

I understand the project aims to be pure Rust and clean-room. This would only call a system framework the OS already provides, behind a platform flag, without bringing in any third-party decoder code. If that's still out of scope, a short note in the README / docs on why would help users who are wondering about it.

title: Right-to-left languages: what the interface needs before Arabic, Hebrew or Persian can ship
author: nledford
body:
## Summary

#1360 adds Arabic. Trying it locally showed that a right-to-left language needs more than a catalog: text comes out with its words in reverse order, and nothing mirrors. Most of that is in egui and in how the interface is painted, not in #1360. This issue lists what I found, so the work can be split and so a decision can be made on the two large parts (bidi and mirroring) before more translations for Arabic, Hebrew or Persian arrive.

Nothing here affects the languages LightCraft has today.

## How I know

- #1360 at `3195d9db`, merged locally with my open pull requests, stubbed until it compiled (details in [my comment there](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/pull/1360#issuecomment-6135595190)), then headless snapshots of the library, Edit, Info, Settings and Export in Arabic and English.
- egui / epaint 0.36.2 (the version in `Cargo.lock`), read in source.
- Counts below are `git grep` over `crates/ui-egui/src` on `main` at `701f78ea`, tests left out. They size the work; they are not a list of defects.

## Blocking: Arabic cannot be read without these

1. **No bidi reordering in text layout.** epaint shapes each run of one font and places runs left to right in logical order (`epaint-0.36.2/src/text/font.rs:829`, "TODO: heed bidi characters"; `text_layout.rs:1366`). Letters inside an Arabic word join and are ordered correctly. But a space, a digit or a Latin letter falls back to Inter and starts a new run, so the words of every Arabic sentence are drawn first-word-leftmost: "كل الصور" has كل at the left. Punctuation and brackets land on the wrong side for the same reason.
   - Needs: the Unicode bidi algorithm applied before layout (in a text helper of ours, or upstream in egui), with a base direction per language.
2. **No global layout direction.** egui 0.36.2 has `Layout::right_to_left` per `Ui`, and nothing for a whole context; `egui::LayoutDirection` and `Context::set_layout_direction`, which #1360 calls, do not exist.
3. **Much of the interfa…

title: Export writes to any path and silently replaces existing files; no automation root for agents
author: gozzy-nwogbo
body:
**Version:** lightcraft-cli 0.7.1 (release build), also seen on 0.6.0. macOS 27.0.1, Apple Silicon

**What happens**

`app.export` (and the MCP `export` / `render_photo` tools) accepts any destination path, including `..`, and replaces an existing file there without warning. The fix in #93 protects a photo's own original, which still works, but any other file at the destination is overwritten.

**Repro**

```sh
mkdir -p /tmp/lc && echo "precious" > /tmp/lc/victim.jpg
lightcraft-cli run --import any.jpg app.export path=/tmp/lc/victim.jpg
# {"command":"app.export","ok":true,...,"path":"/tmp/lc/victim.jpg"}
```

`victim.jpg` is replaced (its hash changes), exit 0, no warning.

The `conflict` option does not help here: with an explicit `path`, `conflict=unique` and `conflict=skip` both still replace `victim.jpg`.

```sh
lightcraft-cli run --import any.jpg app.export path=/tmp/lc/victim.jpg conflict=skip   # still replaced
```

**Expected**
1. `conflict` applies to an explicit `path` too, so `unique` renames and `skip` leaves the existing file alone. A default that does not overwrite would also be safer.
2. For agent use, the same `--automation-read-root` / `--automation-write-root` confinement that wordcraft, photocraft and vectorcraft offer, so an MCP session can be kept to one folder.

**Related:** #93 (closed). Its description already listed explicit export paths being overwritten unconditionally; the fix covered a photo's own original, so this may be the remaining half of it.

*Found with an automated test harness (Claude Code agents) while evaluating the Craft apps for local agent use. I re-ran the repro above by hand on 0.7.1.*

title: Library on an SMB share: "can't write the new library's snapshot: Operation not supported (os error 45)"
author: youyoulyz
body:
**Environment**
- LightCraft 0.7.1, macOS 15.7.7 (24G720)
- Library directory stored on an SMB share (an smbfs volume mounted from a local NAS)

**Observed**
When opening/importing a library whose directory is on the smbfs volume, the log shows:

```
WARN [main] lightcraft_catalog::journal: catalog: can't write the new library's snapshot: Operation not supported (os error 45)
```

os error 45 is ENOTSUP — smbfs doesn't support the atomic primitive the snapshot write relies on (rename-swap / clonefile are the usual suspects). A leftover `catalog.snap.tmp` (133 bytes) is left in the library directory. The import itself continued, so it's non-fatal — but journal snapshots appear to be silently unavailable on network shares, which degrades recovery, and the only signal is a log WARN.

**Suggestion**
Fall back to write + plain rename when the atomic swap isn't supported, or at least surface/document the limitation for libraries on network volumes.

**Update:** the same library directory also contains a leftover `prefs.json.tmp` (613 B) with no `prefs.json` — either another tmp+swap write that didn't complete, or one not yet flushed while the app is running. Either way it points at the swap step failing on smbfs, not only the snapshot.

Related: #294, #880, #1116

title: Catalog import from an SMB share appears hung: prepare phase full-reads every RAW and the progress counter doesn't advance
author: youyoulyz
body:
**Environment**
- LightCraft 0.7.1, macOS 15.7.7 (24G720), Apple M4
- Sources and library on a local NAS via smbfs (wired 2.5GbE, ~180 MB/s measured with netstat)
- Importing a Lightroom catalog with ~8,725 photos, mostly 40–50 MB DNGs (~390 GB total); add-in-place sources on the same share

**Symptom**
The import dialog showed "14 of 8725" and did not visibly advance for tens of minutes; the app appeared hung (the UI itself stayed responsive).

**What's actually happening**
`sample(1)` of the "hung" process shows it is I/O-bound, not deadlocked: `lightroom_import::spawn_prepare` → `engine::lightroom_job::LightroomJob::prepare` → `engine::import::ImportJob::prepare_files` → `probe_all` spawns 8 workers; each one goes through `engine::files::fs_hooks` → `std::fs::read` reading the **entire** file into memory, then `probe_bytes` (siphash128 over the full contents + metadata extraction). Two workers were parked in `memory::WorkGate::acquire` at the same time. `lsof` taken 10 s apart showed a completely different set of open DNGs each time — files are constantly cycling.

So for this catalog the prepare phase performs one full network read of every RAW (~390 GB ≈ 35+ min at the measured share throughput) before any visible progress.

**Questions / suggestions**
1. Does dedupe fingerprinting require a full-content hash? The README notes network preview reads drop 56.5 MB → 5.9 MB. Could probing fingerprint headers/embedded previews (or a bounded prefix) and only hash full contents when needed?
2. The dialog counter doesn't reflect the scan/probe phase, so on a slow share the import looks frozen for half an hour. Could the dialog expose scan/probe progress separately from import progress?

Happy to collect more diagnostics (fs_usage trace, etc.) on request.

Related: #1407 (journal snapshot write fails on smbfs, seen on the same setup)

title: Sidebar: Local and Folders look alike, but only Folders has Synchronize Folder
author: radialmonster
body:
The sidebar has two folder trees that look the same but do different jobs, and it is hard to tell which one to use.

- **Local** browses every folder on disk. Its right-click menu has Rename Folder, Move Folder To and Show in Explorer.
- **Folders** lists only the folders that hold library photos. Synchronize Folder (find added or missing files) and Remove Disk from Library are only here.

In #1392, the reporter deleted photos in File Explorer and was told to use Synchronize Folder. They right-clicked the folder in Local, the tree they browse in, and the option wasn't there.

Possible fixes, smallest first:
1. When a Local folder holds library photos, its menu also offers Synchronize Folder. The library actions are then available from either tree.
2. One combined tree: every folder on disk, with folders that hold no library photos greyed out, and missing or offline folders marked.

The first is a small change in `panels/left.rs`, since both menus already exist there. The second changes the sidebar's layout, so it is for the maintainer to decide.

title: People view: face pictures render from the raw or a 2,560 px source and aren't kept between launches (slow on large libraries)
author: bitshiftza
body:
**The People view's face pictures load very slowly on a large library, and start over at every launch.**

Measured on a library of 58,796 raws (Sony α1 and A7S III ARW) on an external 5400 rpm hard disk, with 5,048 detected faces: scrolling to a part of the Unnamed faces list not seen yet renders about **4 faces a second**, reading about **17 MiB from the disk per face**, with 60–70 renders queued at once. A stretch already rendered in this session shows instantly, but nothing is kept between launches.

**Why** (`Session::face_job`, `crates/engine/src/media.rs`): each face tile is a full develop render of its photo with the crop replaced by a square around the face. Its source level is chosen so the crop keeps `edge` pixels across ("the smallest that keeps the face sharp, up to the preview"), so a small face in a big photo asks for the Preview level (2,560 px). For a raw whose embedded preview is smaller than that (the A7S III's is 1,616 px), the source becomes the raw itself: the sensor data is read and demosaiced for a ~170 px tile, about 75 % of each 24 MB file. The α1 reads its 8 MB full-size JPEG. The rendered tiles go only to the in-memory render cache.

**Proposal**
1. **Cut faces from the embedded preview.** For a raw, use the largest embedded preview the file carries (read through the planned preview path, #1020) when it gives the tile at least its size across the face, or close to it (a soft limit such as ¾ of the tile edge is invisible at tile size); fall back to the current source only when the preview can't. Never decode a raw just for a face tile.
2. **Keep the tiles.** Store rendered face tiles in the on-disk thumbnail cache (`crates/preview`), keyed like other variants (content hash, develop settings, crop, size, render version), so the second launch shows them without touching the originals.
3. Faces stay exactly as they look today otherwise (the photo's own look, the same square around the face).

title: People view: confirm face suggestions above a selected similarity threshold
author: Th4nat0s
body:
## Problem

The person page in `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/person.rs` shows confirmed faces followed by a **More** grid. `faces.person` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/face_recognize.rs` returns unnamed candidates in descending similarity-score order. The current UI confirms one candidate at a time through `faces.setName`; the separate × control dismisses one candidate for the current session.

When a person has many high-confidence matches, confirming every face individually makes People triage unnecessarily repetitive even though the candidates are already ranked. The selected candidate can provide a natural, user-reviewed threshold: confirm that face and every displayed candidate with an equal or higher score.

This is a UI workflow gap, not a recognition-threshold or model-quality change. LightCraft must continue to name nothing automatically; a batch is applied only after an explicit user action.

## Proposed approach

Add an explicit bulk-confirm action to each candidate tile in the **More** grid:

- Draw an original top-left `↑A` control, meaning “all above”, alongside the existing top-right × and bottom-right confirmation cue. Give it a tooltip that names the person, explains the threshold behavior, and reports the number of faces that will be confirmed.
- Let the `A` key invoke the same action for the currently hovered or keyboard-focused candidate. Scope the key handling to the person page and do not consume it while a text-editing widget has focus.
- Treat the chosen candidate score as the threshold. Include the chosen candidate and all currently shown, non-dismissed **More** candidates whose score is greater than or equal to it. Include score ties even when a tied tile appears later because of the stable photo/index tie-breaker.
- Dispatch the resulting `{photo, index}` list through the existing `faces.nameFaces` command with the current person name. This preserves the command architecture, the 5,000-face validation cap, catalog error handling, and one-step und…

title: People view: rename a named person across the library
author: Th4nat0s
body:
## Problem

The People overview in `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/people.rs` renders each named person as a clickable card, and `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/person.rs` renders the selected name as a non-editable heading. Neither view offers a way to rename the person.

A face can be renamed individually from the loupe through `faces.setName`, and `faces.nameFaces` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/face_recognize.rs` can update an explicit list as one undo step. Those commands do not provide a safe library-wide rename workflow: `faces.nameFaces` accepts at most 5,000 entries, while `faces.person` exposes at most 5,000 confirmed faces. Building the operation from that query could therefore rename only part of a large person without making the truncation obvious.

There is no persistent person entity. `Catalog::people_in` in `crates/catalog/src/query.rs` derives people by trimming each face-region name and grouping it case-insensitively. Renaming one region can consequently split one person into two cards, while changing only capitalization may leave the old spelling visible because the first encountered spelling becomes the displayed name.

Users need an explicit operation that renames every matching face region in the library atomically, including case-only corrections, without editing faces one by one.

## Proposed approach

Add a command such as `faces.renamePerson {from, to, merge?: false}` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/face_recognize.rs` and expose it from both the People card context menu and the person-page header as **Rename Person…**.

The command should:

- Validate `from` as a non-empty person name and validate `to` with the existing face-name rules: trim surrounding whitespace, at most 200 characters, and no control characters.
- Find every in-library face region whose trimmed name matches `from` case-insensitively. Do not obtain the target list through the truncated `faces.person` response.
- Replace all matching spellings with the exact trimmed `to` value, so case-only re…

title: Library: search and filter named people like keywords
author: Th4nat0s
body:
## Problem

Named people are only partially integrated into library search and filtering.

`Filter` in `crates/catalog/src/query.rs` has a single `person: Option<String>` field, and `library.filter {person: ...}` can show photos containing one exact named face. The active value is represented by a removable Person chip in `crates/engine/src/view.rs`. This path is used when the People workflow opens the photos for one person.

The normal **Search Photos** field in `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/topbar.rs` does not search face names. Unqualified tokens in `token_matches` search filenames, title, caption, camera, lens, location, format, and keywords, but omit `Photo::people()`. This differs from the smart-rule field **Any Searchable Text**, which already includes `p.people()` in `crates/catalog/src/rules.rs`.

A fielded `person:` / `who:` token exists, but the query is split with `split_whitespace()` before token evaluation and `has_person` requires an exact full name. `person:Sam` works; `person:Jane Doe` becomes `person:Jane` plus an unrelated `Doe` token and cannot match the person `Jane Doe`. There is no quoted-value parser or autocomplete to make multi-word names usable.

The normal filter bar in `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/filterbar.rs` exposes camera, lens, and keyword pickers only. `FilterValues` in `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs` likewise contains only cameras, lenses, and keywords, even though the existing People cache already provides named people and counts. Users cannot select people from the normal filtering workflow, and the direct `person` field represents only one person.

Advanced smart-album rules already support **People**, **People Count**, nested all/any/none groups, and People inside **Any Searchable Text**. Those capabilities do not replace a discoverable search and filter-bar workflow. The `person` attribute on keyword-list entries is also separate metadata and is not tied to named face regions.

title: Show the camera's focus point (Sony first) and zoom to it
author: bitshiftza
body:
**Show where the camera focused, and zoom to it.**

Most current cameras record the autofocus point in each file's maker notes. Sony bodies record, among others:

| Field (Sony MakerNote) | Example from an ILCE-1 (α1) ARW | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Focus location | `8640 5760 3226 1980` | the image size it is measured in, then the focus centre in pixels |
| Focus frame size | `175x180` | the size of the frame the camera showed |
| Focus mode / AF area mode / AF tracking | `AF-C` / `Animal Eye Tracking` / `Face tracking` | how it focused |

On a sample of α1 files the location matches the subject exactly (drawn on the embedded preview, the box sits on the bird's eye), and varies with spot, zone, wide, tracking and eye-AF shots. In manual focus, or when only the frame centre is reported, there is no real point.

Lightroom Classic doesn't show focus points (photographers use third-party plugins for it), so this goes beyond parity; it's most useful while culling.

**Proposal (first step: Sony)**
- **Read it** from the raw's header at import / probe (the maker notes are in the header, no extra reads), into the photo's metadata as a box normalised to the upright photo plus the AF mode, so it follows rotation and crops. Existing photos get it on the next metadata refresh.
- **Show it:** View ▸ Show Focus Point (with a shortcut) draws the box in Detail, Compare and Survey, like face boxes; the Info panel shows the mode ("AF-C · Wide · Animal Eye").
- **Zoom to it:** the 1:1 zoom key / click zoom centres on the focus point when there is one, so checking sharpness is one keystroke; Compare and Survey can do the same per photo.
- **Missing or meaningless data** (manual focus, a centre-only report, an unknown body) shows nothing rather than a misleading box.
- Commands for the overlay and zoom; the box and mode in the metadata a command / MCP can read.

**Later:** other makers (Fujifilm, Canon, Nikon, OM System, Panasonic record similar data), and a "focus missed?" check that …

title: Mouse wheel scrolls the grid and filmstrip far too little (one notch = 100 points, whatever the view size)
author: MarkusFriedel
body:
**What happens now**

One mouse-wheel notch scrolls the grid and the filmstrip by a fixed 100 points (`theme::WHEEL_LINE_POINTS`, since #1064; 40 before). That suits the side panels, but not the photo views:
- Filmstrip: a cell is 120 points wide, so one notch moves less than one photo.
- Grid: at large thumbnails a row is several hundred points tall, so one notch moves a fraction of a row.

Getting through an album of 1,500 photos (one football match) with the wheel takes hundreds of notches.

**What Lightroom Classic does**

One notch scrolls the grid and the filmstrip by about a third of the visible area: three notches move a photo from one edge to the other. That holds at any window and thumbnail size (checked in both views, also with a smaller window).

**Proposal**

In the grid (both grids) and the filmstrip, a notch scrolls a third of the visible height or width.
- Not snapped to whole rows: if each notch moved exactly N rows, the new photos would land exactly where the old ones were, and the grid would look as if it hadn't moved.
- Jump at once instead of gliding: the glide blurs the photos while they move, which gets in the way when you scan a shoot notch by notch. A step of a third only introduces new photos on 1/3 of the view, so the eye can follow.
- Side panels and dialogs keep 100 points per notch. Trackpads, which report points, scroll as they do now.

I have a PR ready.

title: Build Smart Previews in parallel instead of one photo at a time
author: mattsivak
body:
## Problem

Build Smart Previews works through the selected photos one at a time. `smart_run` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/previews.rs`) loops over the jobs serially and holds the global `SMART_WRITE` mutex across each photo's whole build: decode the original at preview size, choose the scale, sRGB-encode, JPEG-encode at quality 97, then the atomic, synced write. A library-wide build uses one core, while the render and preview pools use them all.

The lock exists only so that Build Smart Previews and the stale-look refresh at opening (`refresh_stale_smart_previews`), which run on separate threads, never write the same proxy file at once. It doesn't need to serialise unrelated photos.

## Proposal

- Narrow the lock: lock per proxy path (or per content hash) instead of process-wide, or take the global lock only around the "is it valid/stale? → write_atomic" check-and-write and not around the decode/encode.
- Run the jobs on a bounded worker pool (rayon or the existing job pool), with a cap that leaves room for interactive renders. Raw decodes at preview size are memory-heavy, so the cap matters.
- Keep the current guarantees: cancel from the activity row, `task.progress` counts (atomic counters already exist), the repaired/refreshed/stale-kept accounting, no partial proxies, and never recreating a missing custom folder.
- Optional: pipeline the decode and the JPEG encode so the two overlap.

## Why not the GPU

Most of the per-photo cost is raw entropy decoding, which is serial bit-stream work and stays on the CPU. Binning, the percentile, the sRGB conversion and the JPEG DCT could run on the GPU, but at ~2560 px they take a few ms on the CPU, and the upload/readback would eat most of that gain. Parallelising across photos should scale with core count; GPU offload wouldn't.

title: Removing a virtual copy keeps the numbered label
author: danielkean
body:
If you create a virtual copy of a file in your library, it adds the '1/2' label to the thumbnail to the original, and then 2/2 to the new virtual copy. However, if you then remove the virtual copy, it doesn't recalculate the labels, so the '1/2' label remains on the original photo even though there's now only one version.

The labels also don't recalculate their numbers when a virtual copy removal happens, for example, if there is the original and then two virtual copies, and you delete the one with the '2/3' label, then the one with '3/3' doesn't get recalculated to be '2/2'.

title: Preview stalls for minutes after a slider drag on a large layered TIFF from an SMB share
author: mattjwood
body:
**Version:** 0.7.1 Linux AppImage (before #1302). Linux Mint 22.3, GeForce MX250. Library on the local disk; original on an SMB share (kernel CIFS, default `cache=strict`).

**File:** 489 MB Photoshop TIFF, 5565×3710, 16-bit, deflate. 375 MB of it is layer data (`ImageSourceData`).

**Steps:** open it in Detail, drag Highlights quickly left and right for a few seconds.

**Result:** the image stops updating for 2–3 minutes. Meanwhile `ui.inspect` shows `loupe.pending: true`, `pendingSlots: ["Thumb(...)"]`, and `workBytes` ≈ 1.4 GB against a `workLimit` of 384 MB. The app keeps reading the file over the network (≈ 2.8 GB read for this one file).

**Measurements:** `lightcraft-cli render --size 1600` takes 3 s from a local copy and 29 s from the share (≈ 850 MB transferred). With the file local, or the share mounted with `cache=loose`, the same drag stays responsive.

**Likely cause:** `tiff_codec::decode` reads the whole file (layers included). Each edit re-queues a thumbnail that decodes the original again, and those decodes hold `work_gate`, so the loupe waits.

**Suggestions:** read only the needed strips/tiles; build the post-edit thumbnail from the loupe's cached source; give the visible view priority at the work gate.

Related: #330, #1302.

_Investigated with help from an AI assistant (Claude); the measurements are from my machine._

title: Preview cache clear and prune traverse symlinked shard directories
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity / confidence:** Medium conditional unintended-deletion risk; high confidence.

Reviewed upstream main at `b3d392b4994ee99dc389890f006600769d0c4ff5`. **Static source-confirmed control flow; scenarios not reproduced.** No product files changed, exploit developed, or destructive testing performed.

## Source evidence
- [`crates/preview/src/disk.rs:121–138`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/b3d392b4994ee99dc389890f006600769d0c4ff5/crates/preview/src/disk.rs#L121-L138): `scan` validates the two-hex shard name then calls `read_dir(sub.path())` without rejecting directory symlinks. Checking child `DirEntry::metadata` does not reject a symlink ancestor.
- [`crates/preview/src/disk.rs:146–170`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/b3d392b4994ee99dc389890f006600769d0c4ff5/crates/preview/src/disk.rs#L146-L170): `prune` and `clear` remove the returned paths.

## Conditions and impact
A validly named cache shard is a symlink to an outside directory containing files matching that shard's cache filename pattern.

Clearing/pruning the cache deletes matching files outside the cache tree. The filename filter limits affected names; this is not indiscriminate deletion of every outside file.

## Recommended remediation
Reject symlink/reparse-point shard entries and keep get/put/delete operations confined to the owned cache directory. For adversarial concurrent replacement, use race-resistant directory-relative operations rather than a separate path check alone.

## Suggested regression tests
Link a valid shard to a disposable outside directory containing matching sentinel names; public clear/prune must preserve them. Include genuine shard cleanup and direct put/get confinement tests.

## Scope / related work
Residual boundary issue after #98: its filename filtering is present, but does not establish directory ownership.

Prepared from a read-only audit; searched existing upstream issue titles and bodies before filing.

title: PEF entropy reader accepts some truncated streams by consuming synthetic zero bits
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity / confidence:** Medium image-integrity risk; high confidence.

Reviewed upstream main at `b3d392b4994ee99dc389890f006600769d0c4ff5`. **Static source evidence; not a runtime reproduction.** No source changes, exploit development or destructive testing.

## Source evidence
- [`crates/raw/src/vendor/pef.rs:73–78`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/b3d392b4994ee99dc389890f006600769d0c4ff5/crates/raw/src/vendor/pef.rs#L73-L78): Refill substitutes zero after the actual source ends.
- [`crates/raw/src/vendor/pef.rs:102–107`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/b3d392b4994ee99dc389890f006600769d0c4ff5/crates/raw/src/vendor/pef.rs#L102-L107): The reader tracks consumed bits, but `overrun()` checks only `pos > src.len() + 8`.
- [`crates/raw/src/vendor/pef.rs:143–167`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/b3d392b4994ee99dc389890f006600769d0c4ff5/crates/raw/src/vendor/pef.rs#L143-L167): Huffman output uses those bits; the permissive overrun check runs once per row before successful return.

## Conditions and impact
A truncated stream ends where its zero-padded lookahead can still decode valid Huffman symbols/additional bits before the refill-position allowance is exceeded.

Missing entropy can become fabricated samples in a successful PEF decode. Padding for lookahead is legitimate; consuming symbols from beyond the actual entropy is not. This is a source-level acceptance defect, not a claim that every truncated PEF is accepted.

## Recommended remediation
Separate padded lookahead from authorized bit consumption. Reject when actual code/additional-bit consumption exceeds available entropy while allowing legal end-of-stream padding.

## Suggested regression tests
Use a small valid Huffman table with a zero-prefix symbol and truncated/empty entropy; require an error when actual bits are absent. Include valid endings that need padded lookahead but consume only real bits.

title: PEF and NEF Huffman predictors use unchecked i32 accumulation
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity / confidence:** Medium reliability risk; high confidence.

Reviewed upstream main at `b3d392b4994ee99dc389890f006600769d0c4ff5`. **Static source evidence; not a runtime reproduction.** No source changes, exploit development or destructive testing.

## Source evidence
- [`crates/raw/src/vendor/pef.rs:152–161`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/b3d392b4994ee99dc389890f006600769d0c4ff5/crates/raw/src/vendor/pef.rs#L152-L161): Both vertical and horizontal predictors use `+= d`; only the emitted sample is clamped.
- [`crates/raw/src/vendor/nefc.rs:280–294`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/b3d392b4994ee99dc389890f006600769d0c4ff5/crates/raw/src/vendor/nefc.rs#L280-L294): Nikon decoding has the same unchecked predictor accumulation and output-only clamping.

## Conditions and impact
A sufficiently long coded sequence of positive or negative differences drives a horizontal/vertical predictor outside i32.

Checked builds panic; unchecked builds wrap predictor state and can produce incorrect intermediate pixels. NEF may eventually reject excessive clipping, but that does not prevent the checked-build panic. No release memory-corruption claim is made.

## Recommended remediation
Use checked predictor addition and return a corruption error on overflow. Validate predictor domain when format rules permit an earlier rejection.

## Suggested regression tests
Exercise positive/negative horizontal and vertical accumulation near the numeric boundary through decoder tests; debug/release must return the same controlled error, with valid coded-stream controls.

No crafted overflow stream was executed.

title: BigTIFF next-IFD offset arithmetic can panic before the truncated-table guard
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity / confidence:** Low–medium reliability risk; high confidence; checked-build impact.

Reviewed upstream main at `b3d392b4994ee99dc389890f006600769d0c4ff5`. **Static source evidence; not a runtime reproduction.** No source changes, exploit development or destructive testing.

## Source evidence
- [`crates/tiff/src/reader.rs:120–133`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/b3d392b4994ee99dc389890f006600769d0c4ff5/crates/tiff/src/reader.rs#L120-L133): The file-controlled u64 entry count is capped to readable entries, permitting a nonempty truncated table.
- [`crates/tiff/src/reader.rs:143–150`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/b3d392b4994ee99dc389890f006600769d0c4ff5/crates/tiff/src/reader.rs#L143-L150): `table + (n as usize).saturating_mul(entry_size)` is computed before checking whether all advertised entries were read.

## Conditions and impact
A BigTIFF advertises an enormous entry count but contains at least one readable entry. Multiplication saturates to usize::MAX, then ordinary addition overflows.

Overflow-checked builds panic. With overflow checks disabled the addition wraps; in this oversized-count case the subsequent branch normally discards the unused position and returns next=0. An arbitrary release read or memory corruption is not established.

## Recommended remediation
Compute next-IFD location only when the full advertised table was read; use checked conversion, multiplication and addition. Return the documented truncation/limit result otherwise.

## Suggested regression tests
A short BigTIFF with an enormous count and one readable entry must not panic under overflow checks; verify ordinary complete and truncated-table behavior.

## Scope / verification limits
This is a narrow arithmetic-order defect, not a claim that every BigTIFF is unsafe.

Existing upstream issue titles/bodies were checked for duplicates before filing.

A relatively small point list can expand into a large retained dab vector and substantial render work. The newer single-segment/nonfinite guards reduce risk but do not enforce a whole-stroke/render budget.

Apply a total budget during interpolation, clip irrelevant segments before densifying, and bound retained dabs/work across strokes. A postconstruction len check cannot serve as an allocation guard.

Full-quality renders arrive faster than JPEG encoding/cache I/O completes, particularly on a slow or stalled filesystem.

Use a bounded worker pool and queue/byte budget; coalesce obsolete/same-key jobs and drop optional cache writes under pressure. Retain generation-based invalidation.

author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity / confidence:** Medium availability risk; high confidence; enabled local control interface.

Reviewed upstream main at `b3d392b4994ee99dc389890f006600769d0c4ff5`. **Static source evidence; not runtime reproduction.** No product edits, exploits or destructive testing.

## Source evidence
- [`crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs:182–189`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/b3d392b4994ee99dc389890f006600769d0c4ff5/crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs#L182-L189): push_drag loops over caller-supplied u64 steps and pushes an event per step.

## Conditions and impact
A control client supplies excessive count/steps in an otherwise small valid request.

The UI thread can freeze generating events or exhaust memory. Transport request-byte limits do not constrain generated event count. Exposure is the enabled loopback control channel, not a demonstrated Internet-accessible endpoint.

## Recommended remediation
Validate conservative per-request count/step maxima before injecting events and enforce an aggregate pending-event budget. Reject invalid/excessive values without partially mutating the queue.

## Suggested regression tests
Exercise public control methods at and above limits; assert prompt parameter errors, unchanged queue on rejection, and bounded accepted event counts.

No oversized control request was sent during the read-only audit.

Reviewed upstream main at `b3d392b4994ee99dc389890f006600769d0c4ff5`. **Static source evidence; not runtime reproduction.** No product edits, exploits or destructive testing.

## Source evidence
- [`crates/mcp/src/backend.rs:75–80`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/b3d392b4994ee99dc389890f006600769d0c4ff5/crates/mcp/src/backend.rs#L75-L80): roundtrip writes/flushed the request before reading the reply; response EOF is an I/O error.
- [`crates/mcp/src/backend.rs:91–100`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/b3d392b4994ee99dc389890f006600769d0c4ff5/crates/mcp/src/backend.rs#L91-L100): Remote::call reconnects and resends the identical request after any roundtrip I/O error.

## Conditions and impact
The application executes a mutating command, but the TCP reply is lost/connection closes before MCP receives it.

The command can execute twice: e.g. a toggle/undo applies again. Request IDs provide response correlation but no server-side deduplication. An error after possible delivery is not evidence that the mutation did not happen.

## Recommended remediation
Retry automatically only when non-delivery is known or the method is safely idempotent; otherwise report unknown outcome. Alternatively implement well-defined server-side idempotency and result replay for mutation requests.

## Suggested regression tests
A controlled server records the mutation then drops the response; after reconnect, assert no second mutation execution. Separately verify safe retry when connection fails before sending.

## Scope / verification limits
No live mutation or network fault was executed. Existing cancellation of not-yet-started control requests does not deduplicate already-executed requests.

Existing upstream issue titles/bodies were checked for duplicates before filing.

title: MCP output failure can hang shutdown while the input reader remains blocked
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity / confidence:** Medium reliability/resource-leak risk; high confidence.

Reviewed upstream main at `b3d392b4994ee99dc389890f006600769d0c4ff5`. **Static source evidence; not runtime reproduction.** No product edits, exploits or destructive testing.

## Source evidence
- [`crates/mcp/src/progress.rs:35–51`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/b3d392b4994ee99dc389890f006600769d0c4ff5/crates/mcp/src/progress.rs#L35-L51): Independent writer exits on Write error; reader can block indefinitely in input.lines().
- [`crates/mcp/src/progress.rs:61–78`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/b3d392b4994ee99dc389890f006600769d0c4ff5/crates/mcp/src/progress.rs#L61-L78): Serving waits on the inbox without observing writer failure, and shutdown joins the blocked reader.

## Conditions and impact
The output pipe fails while the peer keeps input open and stops supplying complete lines. Even if another request reveals the disconnected output channel, reader.join still requires input progress/EOF.

The server may not return the output error or terminate promptly, leaving a hung process/thread rather than an actionable failure.

## Recommended remediation
Propagate writer failure to the serving loop and provide interruptible input/shutdown. Merely signalling the main loop is insufficient if scoped-thread shutdown still waits on a noninterruptible read.

## Suggested regression tests
Use controlled blocking input and failing output; require prompt error/termination without input EOF, both while idle and during progress notifications. Keep normal EOF handling.

## Scope / verification limits
The poisoned-lock test covers a different failure mode. No pipe/process failure reproduction was run.

Existing upstream issue titles/bodies were checked for duplicates before filing.

title: file.findMissing wait=true returns successful null when the search fails or times out
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity / confidence:** Medium automation-correctness risk; high confidence.

Reviewed upstream main at `b3d392b4994ee99dc389890f006600769d0c4ff5`. **Static source evidence; not runtime reproduction.** No product edits, exploits or destructive testing.

## Source evidence
- [`crates/ui-egui/src/menus.rs:1403–1439`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/b3d392b4994ee99dc389890f006600769d0c4ff5/crates/ui-egui/src/menus.rs#L1403-L1439): Completion errors are only toasted; last_find_missing is filled only on success. The wait result is ignored and absence becomes Ok(null).
- [`crates/ui-egui/src/tasks.rs:95–107`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/b3d392b4994ee99dc389890f006600769d0c4ff5/crates/ui-egui/src/tasks.rs#L95-L107): wait explicitly returns false on timeout.

## Conditions and impact
Invoke file.findMissing with wait=true and a folder that fails validation/search, or a search that exceeds the wait deadline.

Automation sees successful null instead of an actionable error. After timeout the task may still apply results later, so success does not imply completion.

## Recommended remediation
Store/return a typed task result, propagate work errors, inspect timeout status, and explicitly report whether timed-out work continues or is cancelled.

## Suggested regression tests
Public command tests: non-directory path returns error, successful search returns structured results, delayed work returns timeout rather than successful null and has documented continuation behavior.

## Scope / verification limits
Source trace only; no ten-minute wait or filesystem mutation test was performed.

Existing upstream issue titles/bodies were checked for duplicates before filing.

title: SAM weight loading checks the expected tensor shape only after allocating and transferring it
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity / confidence:** Medium model-loading reliability risk; high confidence.

Reviewed upstream main at `b3d392b4994ee99dc389890f006600769d0c4ff5`. **Static source evidence; not runtime reproduction.** No product edits, exploits or destructive testing.

## Source evidence
- [`crates/segment/src/weights.rs:80–91`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/b3d392b4994ee99dc389890f006600769d0c4ff5/crates/segment/src/weights.rs#L80-L91): read allocates raw bytes and a float tensor from the stored shape.
- [`crates/segment/src/weights.rs:99–109`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/b3d392b4994ee99dc389890f006600769d0c4ff5/crates/segment/src/weights.rs#L99-L109): Backend::get calls get_unchecked before comparing the requested shape; get_unchecked can also convert dtype/transfer to device.

## Conditions and impact
A manually supplied model has a required tensor with an oversized wrong shape but internally consistent offsets/length and file-backed data.

The loader can consume substantial RAM/VRAM before reporting a shape mismatch already knowable from the header. Current file-bound/shape-byte checks exist; this is not a tiny truncated-file bypass. Official downloaded weights are hash-pinned.

## Recommended remediation
Compare the stored entry shape with the requested shape before read/allocation/conversion/device transfer. Apply model/tensor budgets and fallible allocation where appropriate, including unchecked reads.

## Suggested regression tests
Use valid stored tensor metadata with a deliberately mismatched expected shape and bounded read/allocation instrumentation; require failure before tensor data read/device transfer. Keep correct-shape controls.

## Scope / verification limits
Manual model loading is the relevant input boundary. Existing outside-file tests do not cover expected-shape validation ordering.

Existing upstream issue titles/bodies were checked for duplicates before filing.

**Severity / confidence:** Medium inference-correctness risk; high confidence.

title: Downloader DNS resolution and multiple address attempts escape the connect deadline
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity / confidence:** Medium availability/cancellation risk; high confidence.

Reviewed upstream main at `b3d392b4994ee99dc389890f006600769d0c4ff5`. **Static source evidence; not runtime reproduction.** No product edits, exploits or destructive testing.

## Source evidence
- [`crates/fetch/src/http.rs:182–193`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/b3d392b4994ee99dc389890f006600769d0c4ff5/crates/fetch/src/http.rs#L182-L193): Blocking to_socket_addrs runs before cancellation checks; each subsequent address receives the full connect timeout rather than remaining overall time.

## Conditions and impact
Platform DNS resolution stalls, or resolution returns several unreachable addresses. The user cancels while resolution is blocked.

The configured connect timeout does not bound resolution/total attempts, and cancellation cannot promptly stop the wait. Downloads run on worker threads; a direct UI-thread freeze is not established.

## Recommended remediation
Bound DNS concurrency and the caller wait, observe cancellation, and use a monotonic overall connection deadline across resolution and address attempts. Avoid replacing the bug with unbounded detached resolver threads.

## Suggested regression tests
Inject a stalled resolver and multiple failing addresses; assert cancellation and one overall deadline without relying on real network timing. Include successful resolution and connection controls.

## Scope / verification limits
No stalled external DNS or network testing was performed.

Existing upstream issue titles/bodies were checked for duplicates before filing.

title: Offline smart previews lose source metadata needed for edits
author: AlexChambers
body:
# Offline smart previews lose source metadata needed for edits

Found while adding lossless smart previews (see PR #1400). The defect is on main `b3d392b4` and the PR branch `lossless-smart-previews` at `cf1c803a`; the lossless fixture below isolates its effect from JPEG quantization.

## Problem

Smart preview loading returns pixels and the stored camera tone curve with `info` set to `None`. Catalog reconstruction does not restore camera colour metadata, DNG local tone maps, or semantic mattes. Edits can render differently offline even when the proxy stores the reduced source pixels exactly.

The metadata loss exists on main at `b3d392b4` and affects LCSP1 Compact too. The exact pixel counts below use LCSP2 Lossless from the PR branch at `cf1c803a`, so JPEG quantization does not affect the comparison. Code inspection establishes the Compact scope; these counts do not measure Compact.

## Reproduction and fixture generation

In a checkout of PR #1400's branch, `lossless-smart-previews` at `cf1c803a`, save the code below as `crates/engine/examples/repro_smart_metadata.rs`. Run `cargo run -p lightcraft-engine --example repro_smart_metadata`, then remove that example. The code and generated fixtures do not need to be committed. It uses only existing workspace dependencies and generates all five fixtures in a fresh temporary directory. No downloaded or unpublished image is needed.

The generator creates a 96 by 64 Bayer DNG, a linear DNG with the same camera colour metadata, a float merge DNG, a DNG with a two-point gain map, and an oriented linear DNG with a semantic sky matte. The TIFF/DNG fields, sample formulas, colour matrices and edit settings are all specified in the code. Each case builds Lossless, asserts identical decoded source samples, renames the original, and compares online and offline 8-bit output with identical edits. The online job receives the saved original pixels and metadata; the offline job uses the normal filesystem loader and proxy fallback.

title: Help ▸ Check for Updates… (notify only, no auto-install)
author: Gremiger
body:
## Problem

LightCraft has no way to tell you that a newer version exists. Releases are coming out quickly: 0.4.0, 0.5.0, 0.6.0 and 0.7.1 all shipped within a week. Someone who installed 0.2.1 kept running it, and kept hitting bugs that were already fixed (dark/green NEFs, #212), because nothing in the app said a newer version was out. The parity tracker lists this as `MENU-APP-UPDATES | Check for updates | P2 | ⬜`.

## Proposal

Add **Help ▸ Check for Updates…**, a manual check that only tells you what's available:

- It runs only when the user picks it. There is no check at startup and nothing is sent in the background.
- It asks GitHub for the latest published release (`GET https://api.github.com/repos/storytold/lightcraft/releases/latest`) on a background thread, using the existing pure-Rust HTTPS client in `lightcraft-fetch`. The UI never waits for the network. The request carries no photo or library data.
- It compares the release tag with the running version (`CARGO_PKG_VERSION`) and shows one of:
  - "LightCraft X.Y.Z is available (you have A.B.C)", with a **Download** button that opens the release page in the browser, and **Later**.
  - "LightCraft A.B.C is the latest version."
  - A readable error when it can't reach GitHub ("Check the connection and try again").
- It never downloads or installs anything. Auto-install is out of scope for now.
- Agents: an `app.checkForUpdates` command that starts the check, and `app.updateStatus` that reports `{current, checking, latest, newer, url, error}`.
- Native builds only. The web build is always the deployed version, so it doesn't need this.

## Possible follow-ups (not in this issue)

- An opt-in "Check for updates at startup" setting.
- Auto-install per platform (Sparkle-style on macOS, the Windows installer, AppImage update info).

title: File › Save All: save every open document in one go
author: hubbo-se
body:
**What I'd like**
A File › Save All command (and ideally a shortcut, like ⌥⌘S) that saves every open document back to its own file in one go.

**What happens today**
With LightCraft 0.7.1 I can now send up to 50 photos to PhotoCraft at once with Edit In (thanks for #998!). Each one opens as a 16-bit TIFF edit copy. But to get them back I have to activate each tab and save it one by one. Close All doesn't save, and File › Save on a TIFF asks for Save As, so a batch of 30–50 photos takes a long time.

**Suggested behaviour**
Save All writes each open document to the file it was opened from, in its own format (a layered TIFF stays a layered TIFF), without asking per document. Documents that have no file yet (new, untitled) could be skipped or prompted for at the end. Optionally, a "Save All and Close" variant.

**Setup**
PhotoCraft 0.7.0 on macOS (MacBook Pro, Apple Silicon), used as the external editor for LightCraft.



**How I work around it today**
I wrote a small helper ("Hubbo Bildbrygga") that does the round trip over the control channels:

1. PhotoCraft is started with `--control 7878 --control-token-file … --automation-read-root / --automation-write-root /`.
2. To fetch the batch back it calls `session.inspect` to list the open documents, and for each one that belongs to the batch:
   `document.activate {document: i}` → `app.save {path: <the document's own -Edit.tif path>}` → `file.close {document: i}` (highest index first).
   The layered 16-bit TIFF is kept, including adjustment layers.
3. In LightCraft it then runs `photo.reload {ids}` on the edit copies (or `photo.relink` first, if I chose to move them to another folder).

This works well, so a built-in Save All would essentially be steps 1–2 as a menu command. One thing I noticed: after `app.save` to a TIFF the document still reports `dirty: true`, so PhotoCraft asks to save again on quit unless the document is closed.

title: Metadata: an empty GPS block (refs NUL, rationals 0/0) is read as 0° N 0° E, and exports write that location
author: KNUFFIXX
body:
**Version:** LightCraft 0.7.1, windows-x64 portable (`lightcraft-cli`), Windows 11 25H2. The code paths named below are unchanged on `main` (b3d392b).

Android phones write a GPS IFD even when the camera has no position fix: `GPSLatitudeRef` / `GPSLongitudeRef` are NUL and every rational is 0/0. Among 777 real-world phone photos with a `GPSLatitude` tag, 92 carried this placeholder (Google Pixel 10 Pro XL, Nothing Phone (3a) Pro, Samsung Galaxy A14 5G, Xiaomi 2201116SG, Motorola moto e13).

### Steps

```sh
lightcraft-cli run --import lc_gps_placeholder.jpg photo.inspect photo.allMetadata app.export path=out.jpg
```

Fixture: [`lc_gps_placeholder.jpg`](https://github.com/KNUFFIXX/artcraft-fixtures/blob/main/lightcraft/lc_gps_placeholder.jpg) (480×320, EXIF written byte by byte by [`make_lc_fixtures.py`](https://github.com/KNUFFIXX/artcraft-fixtures/blob/main/lightcraft/make_lc_fixtures.py); its GPS IFD has the same tags as the Pixel's, 0–7 and 29).

### Actual

- `photo.inspect` → `"gps": [0.0, 0.0]`, while `photo.allMetadata` lists the same tags as `—, —, —`.
- `out.jpg` (default metadata policy) gets a GPS IFD with `N 0° 0′ 0″` / `E 0° 0′ 0″`, and its XMP gets `exif:GPSLatitude 0,0.000000N` / `exif:GPSLongitude 0,0.000000E`. The exported photo now claims a location (in the Gulf of Guinea) that the original never had, and anything that reads GPS shows it there. `removeLocation: true` and `metadata: none` strip it, as they should.

### Expected

body:

### Steps

```sh
lightcraft-cli run --import lc_make_model.jpg photo.inspect app.export path=out.jpg app.export path=out.tif
```

Fixture: [`lc_make_model.jpg`](https://github.com/KNUFFIXX/artcraft-fixtures/blob/main/lightcraft/lc_make_model.jpg) — EXIF `Make` = `Canon`, `Model` = `Canon IXUS 185` (Canon repeats the maker in the model, as Nikon and others do).

### Actual

- `out.jpg` (default `metadata: all`): IFD0 has no `Make` (0x010F), and `Model` (0x0110) = `Canon Canon IXUS 185`. The XMP likewise has `tiff:Model` = `Canon Canon IXUS 185` and no `tiff:Make`. This happens for every camera: a Samsung photo exports with no Make and Model `samsung SM-A528B`. Tools that read the two fields separately (maker/camera filters in photo managers and on photo sites, exiftool-based renaming, a re-import into LightCraft itself) see no maker and a model name that does not exist.
- `out.tif` has neither tag (its metadata is XMP only, with the same `tiff:Model`).
- In the library the camera label repeats the maker whenever the model already names it: `Canon Canon IXUS 185`, `Nothing Nothing Phone (3a) Pro` (`camera` in `photo.inspect` / `catalog.query`, the Info panel, the `{camera}` rename token).

### Expected

Make and Model exported as they were read (`Canon` / `Canon IXUS 185`), as Lightroom does with All Metadata; and as the label, the model alone when it already starts with the maker (`Canon IXUS 185`).

### Likely cause

The catalog keeps one string: `meta_of` in `crates/engine/src/files.rs` builds `camera` as `[make, model].join(" ")`, and `export_metadata` in `crates/engine/src/export.rs` writes it back as `out.model = text(&m.camera)` with no `make`. Keeping make and model as separate catalog fields (and deriving the label from them) would fix the export and the label together.

title: Metadata: shutter speeds above 1/4 s are rounded to whole steps (0.4 s → 1/2, 0.8 s → 1/1, 1.3 s → 1), and exports write the rounded time
author: KNUFFIXX
body:
**Version:** LightCraft 0.7.1, windows-x64 portable (`lightcraft-cli`), Windows 11 25H2. The code paths named below are unchanged on `main` (b3d392b).

### Steps

For each fixture `lc_exposure_<t>s.jpg` (EXIF `ExposureTime` = t as a rational, e.g. 4/10; written by [`make_lc_fixtures.py`](https://github.com/KNUFFIXX/artcraft-fixtures/blob/main/lightcraft/make_lc_fixtures.py)):

```sh
lightcraft-cli run --import lc_exposure_0.4s.jpg photo.inspect app.export path=out.jpg
```

### Actual

| `ExposureTime` in the file | `meta.shutter` (`photo.inspect`) | `ExposureTime` in `out.jpg` (EXIF / XMP) |
|---|---|---|
| 0.3 s (3/10) | `1/3` | 0.333 s / `1/3` |
| 0.4 s | `1/2` | 0.5 s / `1/2` |
| 0.6 s | `1/2` | 0.5 s / `1/2` |
| 0.8 s | `1/1` | 1.0 s / `1/1` |
| 1.3 s | `1` | 1.0 s / `1/1` |
| 1.6 s | `2` | 2.0 s / `2/1` |
| 2.5 s | `2` | 2.0 s / `2/1` |
| 3.2 s | `3` | 3.0 s / `3/1` |

These are the standard third-stop speeds between 1/4 s and 4 s (tripod, night and long-exposure work). The library shows the wrong value, and the export rewrites the photo's EXIF with an exposure time that is off by up to a third (0.4 → 0.5, 0.8 → 1.0, 1.3 → 1.0). Times of 1/4 s and shorter are unaffected.

### Expected

The value from the file, written the way cameras show it (`0.4`, `0.8`, `1.3″`, `2.5″` …), and the original exposure time in the exported EXIF and XMP.

### Likely cause

`meta_of` in `crates/engine/src/files.rs` formats the time as `{t:.0}` (t ≥ 1) or `1/{1/t:.0}` (so 1/0.4 = 2.5 → `1/2`, 1/0.8 = 1.25 → `1/1`); the catalog keeps only that string, and `export_metadata` parses it back with `parse_shutter_seconds`. `lightcraft_meta::Metadata::exposure_display()` (`crates/meta/src/lib.rs`) already formats these times correctly (`0.4`, `1.3″`). Using it in `meta_of` (then `parse_shutter_seconds` also has to accept the `″`), or keeping the exposure time as a number in the catalog, would fix display and export. #1377 changes how the stored string is shown, not the string itself.

title: Export size: "Width × Height" fits either orientation (Lightroom's "Dimensions"); Lightroom's orientation-bound "Width & Height" has no counterpart
author: KNUFFIXX
body:
**Version:** LightCraft 0.7.1, windows-x64 portable (`lightcraft-cli`), Windows 11 25H2. `main` (b3d392b) behaves the same.

Lightroom Classic's Export → Image Sizing → Resize to Fit has two box modes (Adobe help, [Export files to disk or CD](https://helpx.adobe.com/lightroom-classic/desktop/export-photos/export-files-disk-or-cd.html)):

- **Width & Height**: "Specifying 400 x 600, for example, produces a 400 x 600 portrait photo or a 400 x 267 landscape photo."
- **Dimensions**: "Applies the higher value to the longer edge of the photo and the lower value to the shorter edge … produces a 400 x 600 portrait photo or a 600 x 400 landscape photo."

LightCraft has only the second, labelled "Width × Height" in the Export dialog (`ResizeMode::Dimensions`; `app.export width=… height=…`). Parity row LR-EXP-DIM is ✅ with the note "W × H fits either orientation".

### Steps

Any landscape photo, e.g. the 480×320 [`lc_make_model.jpg`](https://github.com/KNUFFIXX/artcraft-fixtures/blob/main/lightcraft/lc_make_model.jpg):

```sh
lightcraft-cli run --import lc_make_model.jpg app.export path=a.jpg width=270 height=337 app.export path=b.jpg width=240 height=300
```

### Actual

`a.jpg` is 337×225 and `b.jpg` 300×200: the landscape photo comes out wider than the box.

### Expected (Lightroom's Width & Height)

270×180 and 240×160: W limits the width and H the height.

### Why it matters

A box is usually typed for a target that has an orientation: a 1080 × 1350 portrait slot of a social feed, a fixed-width web column, a print template. With either-orientation fitting, every landscape photo of such a batch comes out wider than the target (1350 × 900 instead of 1080 × 720 for a 3:2 photo in 1080 × 1350).

Suggestion: add an orientation-bound **Width & Height** mode (the existing `ResizeMode::Width` and `Height` limits applied together) and call the current one **Dimensions**, as Lightroom does; until then LR-EXP-DIM is closer to 🟡 than ✅.

title: Make thumbnail rendering fully asynchronous and debounced
author: cajax
body:
There are two tickets made by me https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/issues/330 and https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/issues/343
and more importantly a [PR](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/pull/1412) that explains the origins of problems I described.
Also this change should close all other tickets where peoplyspeak about filmstrip and catalog slowness.


Per what I understand from the mentioned PR the problem is that thumbnails are rendered synchronously and in main thread (more or less, i don't have an access to code rn).
I suggest few changes to thumbnail rendering.

1. Move the entire thumbnail rendering to a separate thread, asynchronous to main
2. Add debouncing for each thumbnail to not render new version until 200ms of inactivity on photo. (and maybe even interrupt the current rendering process if we launching a new, since the previous one would be discarded anyway) 
3. Optional bonus with asynchronous code from point 1 -parallel rendering. The number of parallel rendering processes may vary. For example based on number of free CPU cores or GPU budget.

While separate thread is self-explanatory,  I want to explain my idea on debouncing.
As you see in PR, @dev-null-undefined reduced the number of render by a lot. But this can be reduced even more if we postpone thumbnail rendering until 200ms of inactivity. If user frantically click slider, or apply some macro with multiple edits, nobody would really care that thumbnail in filmstrip didn't show all intermediate steps. We'd care only the eventual result.

And as I said, this change should also resolve other issues, for example importing photos to catalog seems to be also slowed by the same thumbnail rendering

title: Flatpak on GNOME Wayland: cursor disappears after Crop & Rotate (sandbox has no cursor theme)
author: Lv2hack
body:
## Summary

In the Flatpak build on GNOME Wayland, opening Crop & Rotate makes the mouse cursor disappear over the rest of the window (panels, buttons, sliders) until LightCraft is restarted. The crop tool's own rotate glyph still draws over the photo, but the normal arrow never comes back.

The root cause is packaging, not the crop tool: inside the Flatpak sandbox LightCraft can't find any cursor theme, so on Wayland it can hide the cursor but can never set one. As a side effect, none of the named cursors (resize arrows on crop handles, grab hand, text beam, etc.) ever show on Wayland — users just see GNOME's default arrow until something hides it.

## Environment

- LightCraft 0.7.1, Flatpak bundle from the GitHub release (`ai.storyteller.lightcraft`, runtime `org.freedesktop.Platform//25.08`)
- Ubuntu 24.04, GNOME Shell 46.0 / mutter 46.2, Wayland session
- Works correctly when forced onto X11: `flatpak run --nosocket=wayland ai.storyteller.lightcraft`

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run the Flatpak build in a GNOME Wayland session.
2. Open a photo and click Crop & Rotate.
3. Move the pointer over the photo outside the crop box (the rotate glyph appears), then over any panel.

**Expected:** the normal arrow returns over the panels.
**Actual:** no cursor anywhere in the LightCraft window until restart. Outside the window the cursor is fine.

## Cause

`WAYLAND_DEBUG=1` shows LightCraft only ever sends `wl_pointer.set_cursor(serial, nil, 0, 0)` (hide). It never sends a `set_cursor` with a cursor surface — not at startup, and not when egui asks for `CursorIcon::Default` again after the crop tool's `CursorIcon::None` (`crates/ui-egui/src/panels/detail.rs`, rotate glyph).

mutter 46 doesn't advertise `wp_cursor_shape_manager_v1`, so winit/sctk falls back to loading the cursor from an Xcursor theme (`ThemedPointer::set_cursor_legacy`). In the sandbox that lookup fails, so no request is sent:

- `XCURSOR_PATH` is unset, and the Freedesktop runtime's `/usr/share/icons` contai…

title: all_masks_overlay_shows_every_visible_mask_at_once` fails: AllMasks overlay shows only the last mask
author: DWHowes
body:
On a fresh clone of `main` (b3d392b4), this test in `lightcraft-pipeline` fails:

```
---- visualize::tests::all_masks_overlay_shows_every_visible_mask_at_once stdout ----
panicked at crates\pipeline\src\visualize.rs:432:9:
assertion `left == right` failed: left mask region painted
  left: [0, 0, 0, 255]
 right: [255, 255, 255, 255]
```

Reproduce with `cargo test -p lightcraft-pipeline --lib -- visualize::tests` (Windows 10, Rust 1.99.0, MSVC toolchain).

**Cause.** In `visualize::apply`, `Overlay::AllMasks` calls `mask_view` once per mask plane. Every `MaskView` rewrites every pixel of the image (for example, `WhiteOnBlack` writes `255 * a` everywhere, including 0 outside the mask), so each mask erases the ones drawn before it and only the last visible mask appears. With two masks, the left one is painted black by the right mask's pass. The bug arrived with 8e61ad6b ("Add Ctrl+O / Cmd+O to show every mask overlay at once").

**Second problem, in the test itself.** After hiding the right mask, the test expects that region to equal the plain render (`plain.data[in_r]`). In the `WhiteOnBlack` view an unmasked pixel is black, not the plain image, so this assertion would fail even once the overlay is fixed.

**Suggested fix.** Combine the visible masks' alphas into one plane (per-pixel maximum) and call `mask_view` once. In the test, expect `[0, 0, 0, 255]` for the hidden mask's region, and drop the now-unused `plain` render. With this change all 174 `lightcraft-pipeline` unit tests pass and `cargo fmt --check` is clean.

+++ b/crates/pipeline/src/visualize.rs

             }

-            if let Some(planes) = masks {

title: Export: 8-bit PNG, TIFF and WebP always carry a fully opaque alpha channel (16-bit exports don't)
author: KNUFFIXX
body:
**Version:** LightCraft 0.7.1, windows-x64 portable (`lightcraft-cli`), Windows 11 25H2. The code path named below is unchanged on `main` (b3d392b).

### Steps

Any opaque photo, e.g. the 480×320 JPEG [`lc_make_model.jpg`](https://github.com/KNUFFIXX/artcraft-fixtures/blob/main/lightcraft/lc_make_model.jpg):

```sh
lightcraft-cli run --import lc_make_model.jpg \
  app.export path=t8.tif bitDepth=8 tiffCompression=none app.export path=t16.tif bitDepth=16 tiffCompression=none \
  app.export path=p8.png app.export path=p16.png bitDepth=16 app.export path=w.webp
```

### Actual

| Output | Channels | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `t8.tif` (8-bit; also with LZW or ZIP) | RGBA: `SamplesPerPixel` 4, `ExtraSamples` 2 (unassociated alpha) | alpha 255 everywhere; uncompressed 616,765 bytes, the same pixels as RGB 461,536 (+34 %) |
| `t16.tif` (16-bit) | RGB | |
| `p8.png` (8-bit) | RGBA | alpha 255 everywhere |
| `p16.png` (16-bit) | RGB | |
| `w.webp` | RGBA | alpha 255 everywhere |

The fourth channel carries nothing: since #1222 transparency is flattened onto white where the working image is built, so every 8-bit export is opaque. It still makes each 8-bit TIFF declare an alpha channel to other programs, makes uncompressed TIFFs a third larger, and gives the 8-bit and 16-bit exports of the same photo different channel layouts.

### Expected

RGB (or grey) output, as the 16-bit exports already are and as Lightroom writes its TIFF and PNG exports.

### Likely cause

`encode_with_metadata` in `crates/engine/src/export.rs` always hands the encoders `EncodeImage::rgba8(&img)` (4 channels), so PNG, TIFF (`ExtraSamples` 2) and WebP keep the alpha; `encode_deep` builds the 16/32-bit image with 3 channels. Encoding 3 channels when the image is opaque, which after the flattening is always, would fix it.

---
Tested and written by Claude (Anthropic) on behalf of Udo Funk, who reviews every report before it is posted.

| [DMC-G80 `P1000403.RW2`](https://raw.pixls.us/data/Panasonic/DMC-G80/P1000403.RW2) | `60mm F2.8 DN` (Sigma) | `""` |

### Actual

The lens is empty for every RW2 we tried: the Info panel shows no lens, `lens:` search and lens rules in smart albums find nothing, the `{lens}` rename token is empty, and exports carry no `LensModel`. Shutter, aperture, ISO and focal length are read, so the EXIF itself is found.

### Expected

The lens name, as Lightroom shows it for these files (e.g. `LUMIX S 85/F1.8`).

### Where it is

The RW2 IFD0 and its EXIF IFD (0x8769) have no `LensModel` (0xA434) and no maker note. The full EXIF, with Panasonic's maker note, is the APP1 of the JpgFromRaw (RW2 IFD0 tag 0x002E); maker-note tag **0x0051** (LensType, ASCII, 34–60 bytes) holds the lens name. `lightcraft_meta::extract` reads `lens_model` from EXIF `LensModel` only (`crates/meta/src/exif.rs`). Filling `lens_model` from 0x0051 when `LensModel` is absent, as #1590 does for Nikon's maker-note lens, would cover Panasonic (and Leica RWL, same container).

---
Tested and written by Claude (Anthropic) on behalf of Udo Funk, who reviews every report before it is posted.

title: LRC-LIB-PUBLISH: Export and Share to Google Photos (OAuth 2.0, Albums, RAW upload)
author: Maijin
body:
## Summary

Add support for sharing and exporting photos directly to **Google Photos** (`File > Share > Share to Google Photos…`), supporting both developed exports (JPEG/AVIF) and direct uploads of original RAW files (up to 200 MB).

This directly extends the Publish/Share architecture established by the Flickr integration (PR #1120, `LRC-LIB-PUBLISH`) and Apple Photos export (PR #643, `LR-EXP-PHOTOS`).

## Motivation

Google Photos is a widely used platform for delivering photos to clients and family, as well as a cloud backup target that natively supports RAW files (CR2/CR3, NEF, ARW, RAF, DNG, etc., up to 200 MB per file).

Currently, users must export files to a local folder and upload them manually via a browser. Adding native Google Photos export allows users to publish finished edits or backup their camera RAW files straight to Google Photos albums from within LightCraft.

## Proposed Architecture

1. **New Crate (L1):** `crates/lightcraft-google-photos`
   - Uses `lightcraft-fetch` with `rustls` (strictly pure-Rust, no libcurl/OpenSSL).
   - Implements Google OAuth 2.0 with PKCE (local loopback server on `127.0.0.1:<port>`).
   - Uses the `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/photoslibrary.appendonly` scope.
2. **Credential Management:**
   - Saved locally in the user's OS configuration directory (`~/.config/lightcraft/google_photos.json` with `0600` permissions on Unix).
   - Never written into catalog files and excluded in `--memory` mode.
   - Users can optionally provide their own Google Cloud Client ID/Secret in settings.
3. **Engine Commands (L4):**
   - `google_photos.signIn`, `google_photos.signOut`
   - `google_photos.listAlbums`, `google_photos.createAlbum`
   - `google_photos.upload`
4. **UI Integration (L5):**
   - **Settings → Accounts → Google Photos:** Account sign-in, token status, and client configuration.
   - **File → Share → Share to Google Photos…:**
     - **Mode:** Rendered export (JPEG/AVIF with size/quality controls) OR Original RAW file…
