title: LR-IMP-GPHOTOS: Import photos and RAWs via Google Photos Picker API
author: Maijin
body:
## Summary

Add the ability to import photos and camera RAW files from **Google Photos** into a local LightCraft catalog (`File > Import > From Google Photos…`), utilizing the modern **Google Photos Picker API**.

This complements the Google Photos publish/export feature and follows the pattern established by the Immich import integration (PR #587, `LR-IMP-IMMICH`).

## Motivation & Technical Context

Many photographers keep raw camera shots or mobile captures in Google Photos. While importing from cloud storage into a local LightCraft catalog is desirable, Google deprecated broad background library scanning (`photoslibrary.readonly`).

To import existing library content securely and sustainably, third-party applications must use the **Google Photos Picker API**:
- Rather than scanning an entire cloud library blindly, the user explicitly picks the photos, RAW files, or albums they want to import inside a secure picker interface.
- LightCraft receives temporary download session URIs to fetch the original, uncompressed media items into the local library folder.

## Proposed Architecture

1. **Authentication & Scope:**
   - Reuses or shares the Google account connection from `crates/lightcraft-google-photos`.
   - Uses the `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/photospicker.mediaitems.readonly` scope.
2. **Import Flow (`File > Import > From Google Photos…`):**
   - Initiates a picker session and opens the Google Photos Picker dialog.
   - User selects the photos/RAWs they want to bring into LightCraft.
   - LightCraft queries the session for selected media items and their download URLs.
3. **Ingest & Catalog Integration:**
   - Downloads original files (JPEG, PNG, or camera RAWs like CR3, ARW, NEF, DNG) into the user's chosen local folder (e.g. `~/Pictures/LightCraft/Imports/GooglePhotos/YYYY-MM-DD/`).
   - Runs files through the standard LightCraft ingest pipeline: reads metadata/EXIF, generates thumbnails/previews, and appends them to the catalog operations journal.

title: MCP client accepts mismatched reply IDs and incomplete response frames
author: euisuh
body:
The remote MCP backend can report an unrelated control response as the result of the current command. This remains present on main `a4b53b28cc52b68d9f5bdca09fa5666cdad5ad5f`, after the lost-reply/no-replay fix in #1574. It is separate from closed #1526.

### Reproduction

A disposable loopback control peer reads request `id: 1`, then sends:

```json
{"id":999,"ok":true,"result":"unrelated"}
```

The exact production backend returns `Ok("unrelated")` instead of rejecting the response ID. A separate case sends a valid JSON response and closes without the line terminator; this is also accepted as success.

These cases were run against the real backend source in a small Rust harness. The peer is synthetic; this does not claim that a healthy LightCraft server emits mismatched IDs. No live application, real library, or provider account was used.

### Source

[`backend.rs:136–140`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/a4b53b28cc52b68d9f5bdca09fa5666cdad5ad5f/crates/mcp/src/backend.rs#L136-L140) checks `ok` but does not correlate the ID before using `result`. The framing read also permits EOF without a newline.

### Expected behavior and impact

Only a complete, bounded, correctly correlated response should finish a command. Otherwise close the connection and report that its outcome is unknown; do not automatically replay a mutation. A faulty or wrong control peer must not cause an agent to proceed on a false success.

### Suggested regression

Assert that ID999 for request1 and a JSON object followed by EOF without newline both fail without a second mutation send. Preserve valid replies, normal server errors, and legitimate idless pre-dispatch refusals if supported by the protocol. The analogous GridCraft validation is covered by #1045 / PR#1262 in that separate repository.

All-state issue/PR searches found no exact response-correlation report here; #1526 addresses replay, not this validation gap. Full application/platform gates were not run for this report.

title: init_marker_is_written_during_creation_and_removed_after` fails when the gpu tests run in parallel on a machine with a GPU
author: DWHowes
body:
On Windows 10 with an NVIDIA GTX 1660 Ti (Rust 1.99.0, MSVC), `cargo test -p lightcraft-gpu --lib` fails every time:

```
---- backend::tests::init_marker_is_written_during_creation_and_removed_after stdout ----
panicked at crates\gpu\src\backend.rs:432:9:
and is removed afterwards
```

The same test passes when run alone (`... -- backend::tests::init_marker`, 3 of 3) and when the whole gpu suite runs with `--test-threads=1` (24 passed). It fails in the default parallel run (2 of 2).

**Likely cause.** The marker path (`MARKER`) and the scope counter (`ACTIVE`) are process-wide. The test sets `MARKER` to its own temporary path, then runs `with_init_marker`. Other tests in the same binary create a real GPU device through `with_init_marker` (from `lib.rs` and `nn.rs`). If one of them enters its scope while the test's marker is set, `ACTIVE` goes above 1. The test's own scope then ends without removing the file, because another scope is still active, and the `!m.exists()` assertion fails. The `GLOBAL` lock only serialises the tests in `backend.rs` that set the marker; it doesn't cover the device-creating tests in other modules. On machines without a usable GPU, those tests presumably finish or skip quickly, which would explain why this doesn't show up in CI.

**Possible fixes:**

- Make the test lock crate-wide (for example `pub(crate) static GPU_TEST_LOCK`) and take it in every test that creates a device, or
- Test the arm/disarm logic directly with a local `Mutex<u32>` (both functions already take `active` as a parameter), and keep a separate test for `with_init_marker` that tolerates other active scopes.

title: Feature Request: Support Exporting Edited Photos as HEIC
author: taylor-p-mason
body: ## Feature Request: Support Exporting Edited Photos as HEIC First of all, thank you for developing LightCraft! I really appreciate the work that goes into creating an image editor with non-destructive editing capabilities. I'd like to request support for **exporting edited photos to HEIC format, with all adjustments rendered into the final image**. ### Current behavior When I open a HEIC photo, make adjustments, and export it using **Original (+ XMP)**, the exported HEIC remains unchanged, while the editing adjustments are stored in a separate XMP sidecar file. I realize that HEIC encoding may require additional dependencies or platform-specific considerations, but I think this would be a valuable addition for photographers who use HEIC as their primary image format. Thank you for considering this feature request, and thanks again for your work on LightCraft!

title: Security Proposal: Enforce 2FA and Commit Signature Verification
author: Maijin
body:
Given the growing popularity and visibility of the Lightcraft project, I would suggest strengthening the repository's security posture to protect against potential supply chain attacks. 

I recommend implementing the following best practices:
1. Enforce Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) for all contributors.
2. Require verified commits to ensure the authenticity and integrity of all code changes (even if it's done with AI).

There are obviously more measures that would be good to take but these would be good start - For more information on setting up these protections, please refer to GitHub's documentation: https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/managing-commit-signature-verification - Implementing these measures would help maintain trust and security as the project scales.

title: render --settings accepts a .lcpreset file but applies nothing

body:
## What happens

`lightcraft-cli render --settings FILE` accepts a `.lcpreset` file written by `preset.export`, exits 0 and writes the output, but applies none of the preset's settings. The output is identical to a render without `--settings`. Only a bare settings object works.

LightCraft 0.7.1, CLI, macOS universal, macOS 26.1 (25B78)

body:
Environment

LightCraft 0.7.1, Linux AppImage

Source camera: Nikon Z9

Source format: Nikon NEF

Independent RAW converter: darktable
Steps to reproduce

Import a Nikon Z9 NEF into LightCraft.

Apply development adjustments.

Export the photo as DNG.

Try to open the exported DNG in darktable.

Actual result

Darktable reports that the Nikon Z9 color matrix cannot be found and fails to open the DNG correctly.

The original NEF opens successfully in darktable.

ExifTool inspection of the exported DNG produces:

Make              : NIKON CORPORATION
Model             : NIKON Z 9
UniqueCameraModel : NIKON CORPORATION NIKON Z 9
AsShotNeutral     : 0.489484 1 0.745269

The tags ColorMatrix1, ColorMatrix2, ForwardMatrix1, and ForwardMatrix2 are absent.

Possible root cause

In crates/raw/src/vendor/nef.rs, the NEF decoder initializes raw.color with ColorData::default(). The DNG writer (crates/raw/src/dngwrite.rs) only serializes color matrices when they are present in raw.color.

Consequently, the exported DNG may lack essential color calibration information, even though LightCraft can render the original NEF using its own camera color processing.

Expected result

DNG exports from supported Nikon NEFs should contain valid camera color calibration data and open correctly in independent DNG-compatible applications, including darktable.

Suggested regression test

Export a real Nikon Z9 NEF as DNG, verify the required color calibration tags and confirm that the file can be opened by an independent RAW converter.

The same issue should also be checked in Convert to DNG and Copy as DNG, as both use the same DNG writer.

title: GPU: concurrent large renders exhaust device memory, then a validation error retires the GPU for the session
author: aterveus
body:
# GPU: concurrent large renders run out of device memory, then a validation error retires the GPU for the session

**Environment:** LightCraft 0.5.0 (also present in 0.8.0 by code inspection: `crates/gpu/src/lib.rs` has no concurrency limit), Linux, NVIDIA RTX A1000 Laptop GPU, 4 GB VRAM, Vulkan (`buffers ≤ 2047 MiB`). Library of Sony ILCE-7RM4 raws (60 MP).

## What happens

Importing ~100 raws starts preview builds. The preview builder thread and up to six job-pool threads each render a 60 MP frame on the GPU at the same time. On a 4 GB card that overflows:

```
WARN [lc-build-previews] lightcraft_gpu: gpu: rendering on the CPU instead: GPU render: out of device memory: Out of Memory
WARN [lc-job-4] lightcraft_gpu: gpu: rendering on the CPU instead: GPU render: out of device memory: Out of Memory
WARN [lc-job-1] lightcraft_gpu: gpu: rendering on the CPU instead: GPU render: device error: Validation Error
Caused by: In Device::create_bind_group  Buffer with '' label is invalid
; the GPU is not used again
WARN [lc-job-2] ... out of device memory ...
```

Each OOM falls back to the CPU as designed, but one of the concurrent renders then hits a validation error on a buffer the OOM invalidated, and `FailKind::Fatal` disables the GPU for the rest of the process. Everything after that renders on the CPU.

## Cause

`lightcraft_gpu::render` has no notion of how much device memory the renders in flight hold. Six 60 MP renders × (source + working copies + output as float RGB) is ~17 GB of requests against 4 GB.

## Fix (tested on the A1000; branch linked below)

1. A shared **device-memory budget** in `crates/gpu/src/ctx.rs`: each render estimates its footprint (`width × height × 12 bytes × 4`), waits on a condvar until it fits within `max(1.5 × max_buffer, 3 GiB)` alongside the renders in flight, and releases on drop. A lone render always gets in, however large. wgpu exposes no VRAM size, so the largest-buffer limit stands in.

title: Panorama: real pairs rejected by match verification in scenes with moving water; dropped frames not reported
author: aterveus
body:
# Panorama: real pairs rejected by the match verification in scenes with moving water; dropped frames not reported

**Environment:** LightCraft 0.5.0 (same code in 0.8.0: `crates/merge/src/pano/camera.rs::match_pairs`), Sony ILCE-7RM4, 35 mm, 11-frame dusk pan of a waterfall, portrait frames.

## What happens

Selecting 9 overlapping frames, the Panorama Merge Preview says "9 photos" in the side panel and "4 photos · perspective" under the preview. Nothing says which frames were left out or why. The stitched result covers less than half the scene.

## Cause

`match_pairs` accepts a pair only when RANSAC inliers exceed Brown & Lowe's `8 + 0.3 × matches`. With per-pair debug logging added (on the branch), the table for this set shows real links failing that test:

```
0-2: 104 matches, 31 inliers, rejected (needs > 39)
0-3: 136 matches, 36 inliers, rejected (needs > 49)
1-2:  71 matches, 20 inliers, rejected (needs > 29)
1-3:  87 matches, 25 inliers, rejected (needs > 34)
2-3: 592 matches, 576 inliers, accepted
```

31–36 geometrically consistent matches at 3 px on a 1000 px working image is strong evidence of a true overlap. The 0.3 slope assumes putative matches are mostly right; moving water and foliage produce many wrong ratio-test matches per frame, which inflates `matches` and raises the bar for pairs that are fine. `largest_component` then keeps the bigger island.

## Fix (tested; branch linked below)

- Lower the verification slope to 0.15 (`VERIFY_SLOPE` constant with the reasoning in a comment). RANSAC's 12 inliers at 3 px still guard against false links. All five frames of the affected series now link; the synthetic panorama tests in `crates/merge/tests/pano.rs` still pass (rotation error < 0.1°).
- Keep the per-pair `log::debug!` lines: they made this diagnosable in one run.

Commits on the branch: `merge: log every panorama pair's matches and verification at debug level`, `merge: accept panorama pairs with a lower verification slope`.

title: Proposal: ColorChecker chart calibration and per-picture-style looks for cameras without colour matrices (Sony ARW)
author: aterveus
body:
# Proposal: ColorChecker chart calibration and per-picture-style looks for cameras without colour matrices (Sony ARW)

**Context:** Sony ARW files carry no colour matrices, so LightCraft fits each raw's colour to its embedded camera JPEG and, with `lightcraft-cli calibrate`, pools a per-model profile from many JPEGs. That inherits the camera's rendering and can't be more accurate than the JPEG. Users with a ColorChecker expect a measured profile, as DNG camera profiles give.

I have this working on a branch (based on 0.5.0, 10 commits for this feature, tests included) and would like to port it onto 0.8.0 and submit it in pieces. Posting the design first for feedback.

## What it adds

1. **Creative Style metadata.** `Metadata.creative_style` read from Sony MakerNote tag 0xb020 (`Standard`, `Landscape`, `Neutral`, `B&W`, `Vivid`, …). Verified on 139 ILCE-7RM4 files.
2. **Camera profile format 2** (`crates/engine/src/camera_profiles.rs`), backward compatible: version 1 files still load.
   - `chart`: a 3×3 matrix (white-balanced camera RGB → linear Rec.2020) measured from a ColorChecker Passport Photo 2 shot, with illuminant xy, per-patch error stats, lens and source file. Replaces the pooled matrix when present.
   - `looks`: one entry per picture style pooled from that style's camera JPEGs: tone curve knots, hue/saturation table, or for B&W a grey channel mix. Monochrome JPEGs skip the colour gate and never feed the colour matrix.
3. **`lightcraft-cli calibrate --chart RAW --corners x0,y0,… [--locate [PX]]`**: samples the 24 patches (central 50 % of each cell), rejects clipped patches and non-monotonic greys, white-balances on neutral 5, fits by weighted least squares with neutral rows, reports OkLab error per patch, refuses above mean 4 / worst 8. `--locate` searches shift, scale and quarter turn around a rough corner guess, so one guess serves a hand-held series. title: Lightroom import: radial masks are applied outside the circle (crs:Flipped read as invert)
author: bitshiftza
body:
## Summary

Radial masks imported from Lightroom Classic (catalog import and XMP sidecars) are applied on the wrong side of the circle in LightCraft. An adjustment that Lightroom applies **inside** the circle is applied **outside** it after import.

## Cause

`crates/engine/src/crs_masks.rs` maps `crs:Flipped` on a `Mask/CircularGradient` to LightCraft's `invert`:

```rust
"invert": flag(m, "crs:Flipped").unwrap_or(false),
```

Lightroom Classic writes `crs:Flipped="true"` on an ordinary radial mask, whose effect is inside the circle. Under this mapping every such mask becomes inverted in LightCraft. Lightroom's inversion of a mask is a separate field on the mask (`crs:MaskInverted`), not `Flipped`.

## How it was found

The DNGs used were synthetic, with known content and radial masks embedded as `crs:MaskGroupBasedCorrections`. After a round trip through Lightroom Classic 15.6 (import and export), every radial mask came back with `crs:Flipped="true"`, and Lightroom's renders apply the effect inside the circle. LightCraft rendering the same settings applies it outside the circle in all 12 radial cases. Linear gradients agree. No Adobe files or code were used; only XMP written by Lightroom for test files we generated.

## Expected

The inside/outside of a radial mask matches Lightroom after catalog import and XMP import. `crs:MaskInverted` is honoured as the inversion flag. The existing test in `crs_masks.rs` that asserts `Flipped="true"` → `invert = true` changes accordingly.

title: Before/After: Before snaps while After animates during click zoom
author: AlexChambers
body:
## What happens

In LightCraft v0.8.0 on macOS, clicking to zoom in the Side by Side Before/After view makes the left Before pane snap to the final zoom. The right After pane animates smoothly. The panes temporarily show different scales and positions while comparing the same photo.

## Steps

1. Open a photo in Detail at Fit.
2. Press Y to show Before and After side by side.
3. Click a point in the right After pane to zoom in.
4. Watch the left Before pane and right After pane during the transition.

Using the right pane for these steps avoids the separate Before click-position bug covered by #1742 and PR #1747.

## Expected behavior

Both panes should animate together, with the same scale and position relative to their panes. This matches the existing Detail click-zoom animation.

## Code cause

Inspected main commit: `3b4279fc2485bb51847c0071a1b3c514aa0f98f4`. The relevant rendering files are unchanged from the v0.8.0 tag.

In `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/detail.rs`:

- Line 427 computes the final `target_rect` from zoom and pan. Line 428 computes the animated `img_rect` over 0.22 seconds.
- Lines 615 and 616 recompute Before's rectangle directly from the final zoom and pan and draw its whole-frame texture there. Line 617 draws After using `img_rect`.
- Lines 554 through 558 also give Before's sharp region tiles the final rectangle for both drawing and requests. After's region view keeps animated drawing geometry separate from its final request geometry at line 555.
- Lines 355 through 357 place region textures using their drawing rectangle, so fixing only the whole-frame image would leave sharp Before tiles snapping.

The Before pane bypasses the animated transform. This does not depend on waiting for a sharp render.

Source: [whole-frame drawing](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/3b4279fc2485bb51847c0071a1b3c514aa0f98f4/crates/ui-egui/src/panels/detail.rs#L612), [region view geometry](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/3b4279fc2485bb51847c007…

title: Lightroom preset import: local grain dropped silently, Adobe base looks ignored (B&W presets import in colour), luminance ranges cut off at scene white
author: egegl
body:
**Version:** LightCraft 0.8.0 (build `16dbb90`), macOS 27.0.1, Apple M3 Pro. Imported with Presets ▸ ⋯ ▸ Import Presets… (`preset.import`).

Importing Lightroom Classic XMP presets loses three things. I hit all three with a commercial film-emulation pack of 23 presets. Every preset lost nearly all its grain, its B&W presets came in as colour, and its highlights masks stopped short of the brightest parts of the frame.

### 1. Local grain is dropped silently
`LocalGrain` isn't in `crs_masks::LOCAL`, and masks have no grain slider, so the value disappears. Nothing is added to `unmapped` either, so the import toast doesn't mention it. Film-emulation presets often put their grain in shadow, midtone and highlight luminance-range masks and leave the global `GrainAmount` at about 1, so they import with almost no grain. (The doc comment on `LocalAdjustments` says local grain isn't in Lightroom, but current Lightroom Classic writes `crs:LocalGrain`.)

### 2. Adobe's base looks are ignored
`crs:Look` is never read. A preset whose look is `Adobe Monochrome` and that has no `ConvertToGrayscale` field (true of the presets I have) imports as a colour preset, and its B&W mix does nothing. `Adobe Neutral`, `Adobe Vivid`, `Adobe Landscape` and `Adobe Portrait` have direct counterparts (`lc.neutral`, …) but are dropped as well. And because these presets never set the profile, applying one after another keeps the previous preset's profile.

### 3. Luminance ranges that run to white are cut off at scene white
`LumRange="a b 1 1"` means full strength all the way up to white, which is what a typical highlights mask uses. It maps through `lightness_to_range(1.0)` to `hi` = 0.667 (0 EV) with `hi_feather` 0. LightCraft's range scale goes on to +4 EV, so anything brighter than scene white falls out of the mask along a hard edge: the sun, specular highlights, or the whole sky after a positive exposure. In Lightroom that end of the range includes everything up to the brightest pixel.

title: Delete from Disk on Windows: move to the Recycle Bin through the shell, then enable it
author: bitshiftza
body:
Follow-up to #1706 (Delete from Disk). The Linux and BSD code is in; Windows is turned off until the work below is done.

## Where things stand

- `crates/engine/src/trash.rs`, `trash::available()` returns an error on Windows, so the command, the menu entry and the dialog button are all disabled there. The Windows code path (`recycle()`) is written but has never run on Windows.
- `recycle()` moves the file into the drive's Recycle Bin by hand:
  1. it finds the user's SID by running `whoami /user`;
  2. it writes a `$I` record (the original path and deletion time, in the layout the Recycle Bin uses) into `<drive>:\$Recycle.Bin\<SID>\`;
  3. it renames the file to the matching `$R` name.
- The record layout isn't a documented Windows API. Nothing has been checked against a real Recycle Bin.
- Network shares are refused.
- If the user's folder doesn't exist in that drive's Recycle Bin yet, the operation fails with a message asking the user to delete a file with Explorer first.

## What needs doing

1. **Pick the mechanism.** Two options:
   - **Windows shell API:** `IFileOperation` with the recycle flag, or `SHFileOperation`. This is the supported route, and Explorer's own Put Back will work. It needs FFI, so it has to live in its own helper crate with `// SAFETY:` on every `unsafe` block, a safe API, and a line in CLAUDE.md naming it. Only `crates/sysmem` may contain `unsafe` today.
   - **The `trash` crate** (MIT, `ArturKovacs/trash`, one maintainer, about 29 `unsafe` blocks, Windows support via the `windows` crate). Same isolation requirement, and a maintainer-risk decision.
   - Recommendation: the shell API, in an isolated crate. Remove the hand-written `$I` path unless it can be shown to match what Explorer produces.
2. **Use the shell's own answers instead of `whoami`.** Ask Windows for the Recycle Bin of each volume instead of building the path.
3. **Test on real Windows,** on:
   - a file on `C:`;
   - a file on a second internal or USB drive;
   - a file who…

title: Crop: save, name, reorder and delete your own aspect ratios, and hide built-in ones
author: switch87
body:
## The wish

Photographers who crop to the same handful of print, social or client formats want to keep those ratios in the crop tool instead of typing them again. In Lightroom this has been an open request since 2011: [Ability to name custom crops and have more than 5](https://community.adobe.com/feature-requests-676/p-ability-to-name-custom-crops-and-have-more-than-5-666398/index8.html) (80 replies; Lightroom only remembers the last five custom ratios, unnamed). The same frustration comes back on Reddit: https://redd.it/1ncoacn.

## Where LightCraft stands

The Aspect Ratio menu (`crates/ui-egui/src/panels/right.rs`) has the built-in presets and a one-off **Custom W × H** row. A custom ratio applies once and is gone: it is not kept in the menu, cannot be named, and the built-in list cannot be trimmed.

## Proposed behaviour

- The Custom row gets a name field and a **Save** button: the ratio is added to the menu under that name (no limit on how many).
- Saved ratios are listed in the menu below the built-ins; picking one locks the crop to it, and the Aspect button shows its name.
- An **Edit List** mode in the menu: move saved ratios up / down, delete them, and hide or show each built-in ratio (Original and Free always stay).
- Everything is kept in the UI settings (`ui.json`, like the remembered default aspect), so it survives restarts.
- Every change is a command (`crop.customAspect.save`, `.delete`, `.move`, `crop.builtinAspect.hide`), so the control channel and MCP can do the same.

Out of scope: per-ratio keyboard shortcuts (the shortcut table binds fixed command ids).

I'm working on this.

title: Feature Request: RAW+JPEG Pairing with JPEG-First Culling Workflow
author: minhdang03
body:
## Feature Request: RAW+JPEG Pairing with JPEG-First Culling Workflow

### Problem

Many photographers shoot RAW+JPEG simultaneously, especially for weddings, events, and high-volume photography.

The camera-generated JPEG already includes the manufacturer's color processing, film simulations, and picture profiles. It is often faster and more convenient to review these JPEGs before editing the corresponding RAW files.

Currently, LightCraft supports importing RAW and JPEG files and displaying embedded JPEG previews from RAW files. However, there does not appear to be a dedicated workflow for treating matching standalone RAW+JPEG files as one logical photograph.

### Proposed Solution

Introduce an optional **RAW+JPEG Pairing** feature.

When two files share the same base filename and are located in the same directory, LightCraft could recognize them as a pair.

For example:

```text
DSCF0001.RAF + DSCF0001.JPG → 1 photo
DSCF0002.RAF + DSCF0002.JPG → 1 photo
DSCF0003.RAF + DSCF0003.JPG → 1 photo
```

The suggested workflow:

1. **Group RAW+JPEG:** Display matching files as one photograph in the Library grid, while preserving both originals.
2. **JPEG-first culling:** Use the standalone camera JPEG for browsing and reviewing, preserving its original camera colors and processing.
3. **Synchronized selections:** Ratings, Pick/Reject flags, and color labels apply consistently to the paired photograph.
4. **RAW-first editing:** When opening the photo for development, automatically use the corresponding RAW file.
5. **Keep selected RAWs:** Allow photographers to copy or export the RAW files corresponding to their selected photographs.
6. **Optional behavior:** Allow users to disable pairing and continue treating RAW and JPEG files separately.

### Expected Behavior

A photographer imports 2,000 RAW+JPEG pairs from a wedding shoot.

Instead of displaying 4,000 separate photos, LightCraft displays 2,000 grouped photographs.

The photographer quickly reviews the camera-genera…

title: AI Denoise refuses 100 MP+ Bayer raws ("the picture has no size, or is too large"), including GFX100S II
author: poosh0803
body:
## Summary

AI Denoise fails on every full-resolution raw from the Fujifilm GFX100S II (11648 x 8736 = 101,744,128 px, a standard Bayer sensor). The photo state is `failed` with "the picture has no size, or is too large". Cropping the photo does not help, because the limit is checked against the full sensor image.

## Environment

- LightCraft version: 0.8.0
- OS: Windows 11 Pro (x86_64)
- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080 (DX12)
- Model: RawNIND UtNet2 (Bayer), `model_bayer.onnx` from darktable-ai release 5.6.0, installed from file with a hand-written `denoise-model.json`. Self-test passes (noise 0.0289 -> 0.0041, tile 10 ms on GPU).
- Camera: FUJIFILM GFX100S II, RAF, 11648 x 8736

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install the RawNIND Bayer model (Settings > AI Denoise > Install from file...).
2. Import a full-resolution RAF from a GFX100S II.
3. Check the photo with `denoise.status {id}` or try to queue it with `denoise.queue {id}`.

## Actual result

```
photo: { state: "failed", unsupported: false,
         why: "the picture has no size, or is too large" }
denoise.queue -> added: 0
```

Cropping to about 98.7 MP (1.5% off each side) gives the same result.

## Expected result

A valid Bayer raw from a supported camera is denoised. At the least, the message should say what the limit is and what the picture's size was, for example "11648x8736 (101.7 MP) exceeds the 100 MP limit".

## Cause

`crates/denoise-core/src/run.rs` declares:

```rust
pub const MAX_PIXELS: usize = 100_000_000;
```

and `denoise_bayer` rejects any mosaic with `width * height > MAX_PIXELS` with `Error::Input("the picture has no size, or is too large")`. The stored product is at sensor resolution, before crop, so the check cannot be passed by cropping. `product.rs` uses the same `MAX_PIXELS` for the cached product header.

## Suggestions

1. Raise `MAX_PIXELS` so common 102 MP medium-format sensors fit (GFX100, GFX100S, GFX100S II, GFX100RF, Hasselblad X2D/907X at 100 MP, Phase One IQ4 at 150 MP).

author: poosh0803
body: ## Summary An unedited import and immediate export of a Fujifilm GFX100S II RAF (DSCF0260.RAF) in LightCraft looks clearly different from both the camera's own JPG of the same frame and from the same RAF opened in Windows Photos. The LightCraft output has magenta-shifted, over-saturated pinks, crushed dark greens, a dark halo around petal edges and posterized or "painted" gradation in out-of-focus areas. This happens with no edits applied, using the default profile. ## Screenshots (all three: same frame, DSCF0260, viewed at the same crop) **1. title: keyword.export overwrites any file, including a library original (bypasses the original-file guard)
author: padilhaDEVELO
body:
**Version:** LightCraft 0.8.0 (`16dbb90`), macOS universal; `lightcraft-cli` 0.8.0 (macOS universal zip), macOS 26.7.1 on Apple M4. Still present on `main` (`0da998f`).

## Summary
`keyword.export {path}` (File ▸ Export Keywords…) writes the keyword list to whatever path it is given. If that path is a photo in the library, the photo is replaced by the keyword list. The original-file guard that the rest of the app uses is never consulted, so `export.checkTarget` refuses the same path:

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `export.checkTarget path=<original>` | `ok:false`: "… is the original of IMG_0001.jpg in the library: LightCraft never writes over an original …" |
| `keyword.export path=<original>` | `ok:true` |
| `IMG_0001.jpg` afterwards | 6 bytes, `beach\n` (was a 118 KB JPEG) |

In the desktop app the save panel's `.txt` filter makes this hard to hit by accident. Over the control channel, MCP (`run_command`) and the CLI, any path is accepted, and those are the paths agents drive.

On `main`, the two sibling exports, `preset.export` (`cmd/preset_files.rs`) and `curve.exportPresets` (`cmd/curves.rs`), already call `check_write_target` and write through `write_file_durable`. In 0.8.0 they overwrote originals the same way. `keyword.export` is the one left.

## Reproduce
```sh
mkdir -p /tmp/kw && cp any.jpg /tmp/kw/IMG_0001.jpg
lightcraft-cli run --library /tmp/kw/lib --keep-going \
  library.import 'paths=["/tmp/kw/IMG_0001.jpg"]' mode=add \
  photo.setMeta 'ids=[1]' 'addKeywords=["beach"]' \
  export.checkTarget path=/tmp/kw/IMG_0001.jpg \
  keyword.export path=/tmp/kw/IMG_0001.jpg
ls -l /tmp/kw/IMG_0001.jpg   # 6 bytes
```

## Expected
Refuse a path that is a library original (or its XMP sidecar), as `export.checkTarget`, `app.export`, `export.contactSheet`, `ui.render` and, on `main`, `preset.export` / `curve.exportPresets` do. Write atomically so a failed write can't truncate an existing keyword file.

title: Unedited exports darken near-white neutrals (255→254): the display tone map's shoulder applies at neutral settings
author: padilhaDEVELO
body:
**Version:** LightCraft 0.8.0 (`16dbb90`) / `lightcraft-cli` 0.8.0, macOS 26.7.1 on Apple M4. `crates/pipeline/src/tone.rs` is unchanged on `main` (`0da998f`).

## Summary
An unedited, display-referred photo (JPEG/PNG) does not export to the same values. Neutral near-white tones lose one level:

| Input (neutral grey) | 255 | 254 | 253 | 252 | 250 | 240 | 200 | 128 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Output | **254** | **253** | **252** | 252 | 250 | 240 | 200 | 128 |

- **Where:** every output format (PNG, JPEG, TIFF), JPEG and PNG sources, GPU and CPU (`LIGHTCRAFT_GPU=0`). Saturated primaries such as (255,0,0) are unchanged.
- **Consequences:** a pure-white background never exports as 255 (some marketplaces require RGB 255,255,255), and the README's "pixel-exact pass-through for JPEGs you haven't touched" doesn't hold.

## Reproduce
```sh
python3 - <<'EOF'
import struct, zlib
vals = [255, 254, 253, 252]
raw = b"\x00" + bytes(v for v in vals for _ in range(3))
c = lambda t, d: struct.pack(">I", len(d)) + t + d + struct.pack(">I", zlib.crc32(t + d) & 0xFFFFFFFF)
open("white.png", "wb").write(b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n" + c(b"IHDR", struct.pack(">IIBBBBB", 4, 1, 8, 2, 0, 0, 0)) + c(b"IDAT", zlib.compress(raw)) + c(b"IEND", b""))
EOF
lightcraft-cli render white.png -o out.png    # out.png row: 254, 253, 252, 252
```

## Cause
`ToneMap::display_hdr` (used through `ToneMap::display`) always applies the short shoulder for SDR. In the `else if o > 0.95` branch, `o = 0.95 + d - d*d/0.2` runs even when contrast, whites and blacks are all 0. With `d = 0.05`, 1.0 becomes 0.9875, and sRGB-encoded that is 253.6 → 254.

The module doc promises *"identity at neutral settings (an unedited JPEG renders exactly as the file)"*. The tests don't catch it:
- `display_identity_and_monotone` only checks `y` from 0.01 to 0.95, where the shoulder starts;
- `pipeline::tests::unedited_rendered_source_is_passthrough` accepts an 8-bit error of up to 3.

## Expected / suggested fix
- Make the neu…

title: Presets, develop.merge and render --settings accept invalid crop/curve/slider values → 1-px-wide or black exports
author: padilhaDEVELO
body:
**Version:** LightCraft 0.8.0 (`16dbb90`) / `lightcraft-cli` 0.8.0, macOS 26.7.1 on Apple M4. `DevelopSettings::merged()` is unchanged on `main` (`0da998f`).

## Summary
The direct setters clamp out-of-range input (`develop.set` exposure `1e308` becomes 5, and `crop.set` with an inverted rect falls back to the full frame), and crs XMP import is robust. Settings that arrive as JSON are not sanitized, though, and some values silently ruin the export:

- **`preset.apply` of an imported `.lcpreset`:** only the 122 slider controls go through the control specs (`presets::apply_partial`). Crop and curves are taken as they are:
  - an inverted crop rect `{"x0":0.9,"x1":0.1,"y0":0,"y1":1}` exports at **1×1000 px**;
  - `x0: 1e308, x1: -1e308` exports at 1×1000, all black;
  - a curve point `{"x":1,"y":1e308}` exports **100% black**.
- **`develop.merge` (Apply Settings JSON, the call agents use) and `lightcraft-cli render --settings`:** nothing is clamped.
  - `light.exposure: 1e308` is stored as `1e+308` and the export is black;
  - `vignette.amount: 1e308` exports 62% black;
  - `geometry.scale: 0` and `optics.distortion: 1e308` are stored as given.

Nothing reports an error. A malformed or hostile preset shared online is enough to ruin exports.

## Reproduce
```sh
cat > bad.lcpreset <<'EOF'
{"format":"lightcraft.preset","version":1,"presets":[

title: Photo Merge accepts duplicate ids and unbounded inputs (memory grows past 2 GB in under a second)
author: padilhaDEVELO
body:
**Version:** LightCraft 0.8.0 (`16dbb90`) / `lightcraft-cli` 0.8.0, macOS 26.7.1 on Apple M4 (16 GB). No de-duplication on `main` (`0da998f`).

## Summary
`merge.hdr`, `merge.panorama` and `merge.hdrPanorama` accept the same photo id several times: `ids:[25,25,25]` "merges" a photo with itself and returns `ok`. Duplicates aren't removed and the number of inputs isn't capped, so memory grows with the length of the id list. Measured with `merge.panorama` (a 1.5 MP source, `preview:true`); `merge.hdr` grows the same way from about 50 inputs (843 MB at 50):

| `ids` | Peak memory |
|---|---|
| `[25]×10` | 474 MB |
| `[25]×50` | 1.4 GB |
| `[25]×200` | > 2.1 GB within 0.6 s (stopped by my watchdog) |
| `[25]×2000` | > 4 GB (stopped by my watchdog) |

Through MCP or the control channel, a single call with a long list can push a 16 GB Mac into heavy swapping. The UI can't select a photo twice, but it also has no upper bound on how many selected photos go into a merge.

## Reproduce
```sh
lightcraft-cli run --demo --keep-going library.import 'paths=["/abs/path/in.jpg"]' mode=add \
  merge.hdr 'ids=[25,25,25]' preview=true previewPath=/tmp/hdr_prev.png        # ok: a "merge" of one photo
python3 -c "import json; print(json.dumps({'command':'merge.panorama','params':{'ids':[25]*200,'preview':True,'previewPath':'/tmp/p.png'}}))" > big.jsonl
lightcraft-cli run --demo --keep-going --import /abs/path/in.jpg --script big.jsonl    # watch RSS
```

## Expected
- De-duplicate `ids`, and refuse with an error when fewer than 2 distinct photos remain.
- Cap the number of inputs, or the total input megapixels, and say so in the error.
- In preview mode, downscale each input before it is kept in memory.

## Code
`crates/engine/src/cmd/merge.rs`: the ids are taken as given. `crates/merge` keeps every decoded input.

author: padilhaDEVELO
body:
**Version:** LightCraft 0.8.0 (`16dbb90`) / `lightcraft-cli` 0.8.0, macOS 26.7.1 on Apple M4 (Metal, 16 GB). Same classification on `main` (`0da998f`).

## Summary
Exporting a single very large image (20000×20000, 400 MP) on the GPU takes longer than the 60 s readback timeout. The timeout is classified as `FailKind::Fatal`, so the export is redone on the CPU and the GPU is switched off for the rest of the process. Any later slider drag then renders on the CPU. The device was not lost; the job was just slow.

```
gpuFallback: "GPU render: readback failed: The requested Wait timed out before the submission was completed.; the GPU is not used again"

| Path | Time | Peak RSS |
|---|---|---|
| GPU (then CPU fallback) | 86.7 s | 6.1 GB |
| CPU (`LIGHTCRAFT_GPU=0`) | — | > 7.4 GB within ~1 s (stopped by my watchdog) |

Related to #1764, where an out-of-memory error followed by a validation error also retires the GPU for the session. This is a different trigger: one healthy, slow render on Apple silicon, with no other renders in flight. A 96 MP JPEG exported fine on the GPU, though more slowly than on the CPU (7.7 s vs 6.5 s, with a few edits).

## Reproduce
```sh
python3 - <<'EOF'

title: U+25B8 "▸" has no glyph in Inter and renders as a box in UI strings
author: padilhaDEVELO
body:
**Version:** LightCraft 0.8.0 (`16dbb90`), about 24 UI strings; 11 remain on `main` (`0da998f`). Seen in headless snapshots on macOS 26.7.1 (Apple M4), in English and in pt-BR.

## Summary
The UI font, Inter (Regular/Medium/SemiBold, as bundled in `assets/fonts/`), has no glyph for **U+25B8 "▸"**, so every UI string that uses it as a menu-path separator shows a missing-glyph box (☐) instead. Examples:

| Where | String |
|---|---|
| Settings ▸ General, External Editing help | "Photo ▸ Edit In ▸ Edit in PhotoCraft (⇧⌘E…)" |
| Import review | "… right-click ▸ Restore, or Delete Permanently to import afresh" |
| Grid, Find Similar | "{n} similar photos · View ▸ Clear Filters to see all" |
| Reference view, empty state | "Right-click a photo ▸ Set as Reference Photo, then View → Reference View (Shift+R)" |
| Profile import toast | "Imported … profiles (Profile browser ▸ their groups)" |
| Faces errors | "choose a recognition model first (Settings ▸ Faces ▸ Use)" |

`→` (U+2192) and `⌘ ⇧ ⌥` render fine. In the same string, "View → Reference View" draws correctly while "▸" doesn't.

`crates/ui-egui/src/i18n.rs` already asserts that translations don't contain `▸`/`▾` ("uses an unpaintable menu triangle"), but the check doesn't cover the English source strings in `crates/ui-egui/src` and `crates/engine/src`. Languages fall back to English for untranslated strings, so the boxes show up there too.

## Expected
Use "›" or "→" (both in Inter) in user-visible strings, and extend the i18n test to the English sources (or add U+25B8 to the font fallback chain).

title: macOS Info.plist declares .pcraft (PhotoCraft's format), .psb and .qoi types that LightCraft can't open
author: padilhaDEVELO
body:
**Version:** LightCraft 0.8.0 (`16dbb90`), macOS universal DMG, installed in `/Applications`, macOS 26.7.1. `packaging/macos/Info.plist.in` is unchanged on `main` (`0da998f`).

## Summary
The macOS `Info.plist` looks copied from PhotoCraft's template:

- **`UTExportedTypeDeclarations`:** "LightCraft Document", `ai.storyteller.lightcraft.document`, with extension **`.pcraft`** and MIME `application/x-lightcraft`. LightCraft never reads or writes `.pcraft` (the only reference in the tree is a test temp-dir name). It is PhotoCraft's document format.
- **`UTImportedTypeDeclarations`:** `.psb` (Photoshop Large Document) and `.qoi`. LightCraft opens neither; there is no QOI code in the tree, and folder import skips `.qoi` files.

Because LightCraft claims `.pcraft`, Launch Services now types PhotoCraft documents as LightCraft documents:
```sh
touch test.pcraft && mdls -name kMDItemContentType test.pcraft
# kMDItemContentType = "ai.storyteller.lightcraft.document"
```
`lsregister -dump` on the same Mac shows three bundles claiming `.pcraft`, each with its own MIME type:

| MIME | App |
|---|---|
| `application/x-lightcraft` | LightCraft |
| `application/x-photocraft` | PhotoCraft |
| `application/x-designcraft` | DesignCraft |

Users who install several Crafting Apps get a UTI conflict, and which app "owns" `.pcraft` depends on registration order.

On the other side, there are no `CFBundleDocumentTypes`, so Finder's "Open With" doesn't list LightCraft for JPEG, TIFF or RAW files.

## Expected
- Remove the exported `.pcraft` type and the PSB/QOI imported types, or add them only once LightCraft actually reads those formats.
- Consider declaring `CFBundleDocumentTypes` (viewer role) for the image and raw formats LightCraft imports.

---
_Found while testing LightCraft 0.8.0 on macOS (bundle `Info.plist`, `mdls`, `lsregister -dump`). Tested and written with Claude Code._

title: Small findings from a 0.8.0 test pass: zero-area crop, PNG alpha, silent bitDepth fallback, LUT temp files, idle control connections, +Inf float TIFF
author: padilhaDEVELO
body:
**Version:** LightCraft 0.8.0 (`16dbb90`) / `lightcraft-cli` 0.8.0, macOS 26.7.1 on Apple M4. These are small, independent findings from the same test pass; I can split any of them into its own issue.

## 1. Zero-area crop is accepted and exports a 1×1 image
`crop.set rect=[0.5,0.5,0.5,0.5]` returns `ok` and is stored, and the next `app.export` writes a **1×1 px** file. An inverted rect, by contrast, is reset to the full frame.
```sh
lightcraft-cli run --demo --keep-going library.import 'paths=["/abs/in.jpg"]' mode=add library.select 'ids=[25]' \
  crop.set 'rect=[0.5,0.5,0.5,0.5]' app.export 'ids=[25]' path=/tmp/zero.png format=png
```
Expected: refuse it, or enforce a minimum crop size as the crop tool does.

## 2. PNG export always writes an alpha channel
Opaque sources (JPEG) and flattened transparent sources both export as RGBA PNGs with alpha = 255 everywhere: an alpha channel that carries nothing, because transparency is composited onto white anyway. Writing RGB when every alpha value is 255 would make the files smaller.

## 3. Unsupported `bitDepth` silently becomes 8-bit
`app.export format=jpeg bitDepth=16` and `format=png bitDepth=10` write 8-bit files and return `ok`, although the `app.export` doc says "a value of the wrong kind is an error, not a default".

## 4. `profile.import` of a folder recurses without a bound, and leaks temp files without a library
- `profile.import 'paths=["/"]'` walks the whole disk. Here it found the creative LUTs of an installed Adobe app.
- In a session with no library on disk (`--demo` / `--memory`), each imported LUT is copied to `temp_dir()/lightcraft-<id>.cube` and never removed: 124 files (29 MB) were left in `$TMPDIR` after one run.

Code: `crates/engine/src/cmd/lut_profiles.rs:126-130`.

## 5. Control channel: idle connections never time out
The server is careful in many ways: loopback only, bounded lines and 16 connections at most. But a connection that sends nothing holds its slot forever, so 16 idle connections lock…

title: macOS: app aborts when NSOpenPanel returns nil (file dialog refused) — objc2 panic can't unwind, no error shown
author: mattsivak
body:
## What happened

On macOS the desktop app aborted (exit code 134, SIGABRT) a few seconds after launch, when a native file dialog was requested (an Import / Browse Folder… style picker; the exact click isn't in the log):

```
thread 'main' panicked at .../objc2-app-kit-0.3.2/src/generated/NSOpenPanel.rs:127:5:
unexpected NULL returned from +[NSOpenPanel openPanel]
note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace
fatal runtime error: failed to initiate panic, error 3, aborting
```

The panic is raised by the `objc2-app-kit` binding that `rfd` uses, inside an Objective-C callback. It cannot unwind, so the runtime aborts the process: the panic hook and the `catch_unwind` guard around command dispatch never run, and the user gets no dialog and no chance to keep working. The library was fine afterwards (0 log records to replay), but any edits that hadn't been written yet would have been lost.

## When it happens

`+[NSOpenPanel openPanel]` returns `nil` when macOS won't give the process an Open panel. Here the app had been started by a background agent process in a restricted sandbox (`cargo run --release -p lightcraft -- --control 18431`), not from Finder or a normal terminal. Other cases that are known to make it return `nil` include a sandboxed build without the user-selected-files entitlement and a process with no window-server session. Started normally, the same build opens the panel without problems.

Environment: macOS 26.6.2, Apple M4 Max, LightCraft 0.8.0 (built from `main` @ 0da998f2 plus an unrelated UI branch), `rfd` 0.17.2, `objc2-app-kit` 0.3.2.

## Expected

Per the never-crash standard, a file dialog the OS refuses should be an error the user can act on ("Couldn't open the file chooser: …"), never an abort.

## Where

Every native dialog goes through `rfd` in `apps/lightcraft/src/main.rs`: `services()` → `picker` (`pick_files` / `pick_folder` / `save_file`, on its own thread since #191), `pick_folder` (Open Library), `pick_fil…

title: Allow opening source photo and rejecting false detections from Unnamed Faces
author: lostwald
body:
### Problem

The **Unnamed Faces** view currently displays detected faces but does not provide a way to open the corresponding source photo or reject an incorrectly detected face.

This is particularly problematic when face detection produces false positives (e.g., objects or patterns incorrectly identified as faces).

Users cannot easily review these detections in the context of the original photo or remove them from the Unnamed Faces list.

### Proposed Solution

1. ~~**Open source photo:** Allow users to open the original photo directly from a face thumbnail in the Unnamed Faces view (e.g., via double-click or context menu).~~ -> https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/issues/1664
2. **Reject false detections:** Add an option to mark a detected face as a false positive and remove it from the Unnamed Faces list.
3. ~~**Persist rejections:** Ensure rejected detections do not reappear after running face detection again.~~ -> https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/issues/1873
4. **Bulk rejection:** Allow selecting multiple face thumbnails and rejecting them together.

### Expected Benefit

This would make reviewing and cleaning up face detection results significantly easier, especially for large photo libraries with many false positives.

Currently, users have no practical way to identify and remove these false detections directly from the Unnamed Faces workflow.

title: [Bug Report] [LightCraft] Windows: UI brightness flickers on mouse movement with G-SYNC/VRR (OLED/VA monitors)
author: ticket-craft
body:
### Description

On Windows, moving the mouse over the app (launcher, LightCraft, and other apps in the suite) causes a visible brightness/exposure dip in the UI and preview. When the mouse stops, the screen returns to its normal, brighter state. It looks like constant micro-flickering while navigating.

- When focused and idle, the app renders at a low rate (~49 fps reported).
- On mouse movement, it jumps to the monitor's full refresh rate.
- The large refresh-rate swings trigger VRR brightness/gamma shifts, which are especially visible on OLED and VA panels.
- Each fps spike corresponds to a flicker. Brightness while the mouse is still matches the brighter "idle" state.

Turning off G-SYNC/VRR stops the flicker, which confirms it is VRR-related.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Windows 11, NVIDIA GPU, G-SYNC enabled (OLED or LG monitor).
2. Open the launcher or any app from the suite.
3. Move the mouse over the window and observe the UI brightness dip.
4. Stop moving the mouse and observe brightness return to normal.

## Expected behavior

No brightness flicker with VRR enabled.

## Workarounds tried

- **NVIDIA Control Panel → Set up G-Sync → Enable for full screen mode only:** VRR is still triggered.
- **Per-app profile with Monitor Technology = Fixed Refresh:** fixes the flicker for some users, but on others it causes the monitor to black out for ~2 s while G-SYNC switches off. This repeats on alt-tab between the app and other windows.
- **Disabling G-SYNC/VRR on the monitor or globally:** works, but is a poor tradeoff for games and other apps.

title: Timelapse module (v1): deflicker, keyframes, apply and image-sequence export
author: bitshiftza
body:
A Timelapse view for sequences of photos (intervalometer shoots, sunrises, sunsets), inside LightCraft.

## Scope for v1

1. **Deflicker:** measure each frame's brightness (median of log luminance on the proxy) and remove the frame-to-frame flicker, keeping the scene's real trend (running median, then smoothing). The correction is an exposure offset, clamped to a user limit.
2. **Keyframes:** set exposure, white balance (Temp, Tint), contrast, highlights, shadows, whites and blacks at chosen frames. Frames in between are interpolated monotonically, so exposure never overshoots.
3. **Apply:** write the per-frame develop settings to the photos as one undo step. Cancellable, with progress in the activity stack.
4. **Export:** the developed frames as an image sequence, through the existing export path.

Everything runs inside LightCraft: the view is a client of `timelapse.*` engine commands, so the CLI and MCP can run a whole sequence headless.

## Decisions

- Keyframes are stored as a JSON file in the library folder (no catalog change).
- Local masks and crop per frame are out of v1.
- Video output is out of v1 (it waits on the codec decision shared with the slideshow module).
- Multipass deflicker is the first item after v1.

## Testing

Synthetic sequences with known injected flicker (from `lightcraft-scenes`), so the measurement and deflicker can be checked against known answers. No photographs of anyone's shoots are used or published.

title: CR3: highlights between Canon's stated white level and sensor saturation are clipped, leaving a hard pale ring (EOS RP, R100)
author: jensgoemaere
body:
## Problem

For Canon CR3 files, the decoder takes the white level from `ColorData` (the word after the normal white level).
That value is lower than the point where the sensor actually saturates:

| Camera | Stated white | Where samples actually saturate | Range lost |
|---|---|---|---|
| EOS RP (every ISO) | 14558 | pile-up at 16383 | ~0.2 EV |
| EOS R100, ISO 640 (a −⅓-stop ISO) | 10439 | pile-up spread over 13300–13700 | ~0.4 EV |

The samples in that range are real light. On an EOS RP night shot of the moon (ISO 3200), the G/R and G/B ratios
of the same surfaces stay within 1% from G = 8000 all the way up to 16300. Highlight reconstruction treats
everything above the stated level as clipped and rebuilds it. So where a bright area crosses that level (a backlit
sky, sunlit clouds), the render shows a **hard-edged pale band**, which becomes a ring around a backlit portrait.
The Highlights slider can't bring it back.

**To reproduce:** open an EOS RP CR3 with a bright sky that is close to clipping but not blown out, and compare it
with the camera JPEG. The sky shows a washed-out ring at the 14558 boundary.

## Proposed fix

A fix is ready on branch `claude/cr3-highlights-camera-profiles` (commits `b1211424` and `5d6daf5c`). I can't push
to this repo, so I can open a PR from a fork or send a patch, whichever you prefer.

- New function `RawImage::extend_white_to_saturation` (`crates/raw/src/saturation.rs`), called from
  `vendor/cr3.rs` on full decodes. It runs only when at least 1 in 100,000 samples (and at least 64) are above the
  stated white level.
- For each colour, it finds the lower edge of the pile-up at the top of the data. The search uses coarse bins of
  1/128 of the range, so a spread plateau like the R100's still counts. The new white level is the lowest of the
  three colours. If the data runs past the stated level without piling up anywhere, the new level is the top of the
  bit depth.
- The difference goes into the **baseline exposure**, so everythi…

title: Older Fujifilm RAFs (no raw IFD, SuperCCD) fail: "RAF without a raw IFD (older FinePix layout)"
author: kkilchrist
body:
Older Fujifilm RAFs fail to decode with `RawError::Unsupported("RAF without a raw IFD (older FinePix layout)")`, raised from `raw_ifd` in `crates/raw/src/vendor/raf.rs` (seen at `a4b53b2`). Newer bodies (F550EXR, F600EXR) decode fine.

## Affected samples (CC0, raw.pixls.us)

Values below were read directly from the sample files (RAF header pointers at byte 84, then the big-endian header-record directory). No raw-decoder source was consulted.

| Camera | Header version (bytes 60–63) | Record `0x130` bytes | Record `0x100` (two `u16`) | Raw block |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [FinePix E550](https://raw.pixls.us/data/Fujifilm/FinePix%20E550/) | `0100` | `80 81 82 83` | 3080, 2048 | 12,615,680 bytes = 3080 × 2048 × 2; does not start with a TIFF header |
| [FinePix E900](https://raw.pixls.us/data/Fujifilm/FinePix%20E900/) | `0100` | `83 82 …` | 3688, 2512 | does not start with a TIFF header |
| [DBP for GX680](https://raw.pixls.us/data/Fujifilm/DBP%20for%20GX680/) | `0161` | `00 01 …` | 3856, 5504 | does not start with a TIFF header |
| FinePix F550EXR / F600EXR (decode today) | `0101` / `0100` | `0a 0b …` | 2464, 3328 | little-endian TIFF with the `0xf000` raw IFD |

For the E550 the raw block length is exactly two bytes per sample of the `0x100` size, which suggests uncompressed 16-bit samples. Byte order and CFA phase are untested.

## What's needed

1. **Legacy container (GX680 and similar):** when the raw block has no raw IFD, take the geometry from the header records (ExifTool lists `0x100` RawImageFullSize, `0x110` RawImageCropTopLeft, `0x111` RawImageCroppedSize and others) and unpack the samples directly.
2. **SuperCCD (E550, E900 and other SuperCCD bodies):** these sensors use octagonal photosites on a grid rotated 45° relative to the image ([Super CCD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_CCD)). Rendering them needs a mapping from the stored sample grid to image coordinates and a rotation back to an upright rectangular image, which is a geometry stage the pipeline…

title: Web build: automatic language ignores the browser's language
author: mccoy88f
body:
In the browser build (v0.8.0), the interface language set to *Auto* always shows English, even when the browser is set to a language the app has a catalog for. The desktop build follows the system language correctly.

**Steps:** open the web build in a browser set to Italian (`navigator.languages` = `["it-IT"]`) with no saved preferences → the interface is in English.

**Cause:** The browser build doesn't read the browser's languages, so *Auto* resolves to English.

**Suggested fix:** on wasm, use `navigator.languages` (falling back to `navigator.language`) as the system language tags. GridCraft (`crates/ui-egui/src/i18n.rs`, `navigator().language()`), FilmCraft (`apps/filmcraft-web/src/lib.rs`, `navigator().languages()`), VectorCraft, WordCraft and CadCraft already do this in their browser builds.

title: Fractional command indices can delete or restore the wrong object
author: AlexChambers
body:
## What happens

Fractional command indices are truncated instead of rejected. On `main` at `f34c7a8a`, a public `Session::execute` regression creates version A and then executes:

```json
{"command":"version.delete","params":{"index":0.9}}
```

The command returns `Ok(Null)` and deletes version 0. The regression confirms that the catalog changes.

## Expected

An index must be a representable, non-negative whole number. A fractional index should return `BadParams` before changing settings, versions, history, the history cursor, or undo state. Existing integral JSON floats such as `2.0` should remain valid.

## Where

`crates/engine/src/cmd/mod.rs::index_req` validates that a value is finite and non-negative, then casts it to `usize`. This still accepts `0.9` as 0. Version commands, point-color deletion, and red-eye commands use this helper. `history.restore` has a separate cast with the same fractional-input gap.

The conversion also needs checked integer bounds without routing integer JSON values through a lossy `f64` conversion.

## Reproduction evidence

Synthetic public-engine-command test, no external files or photos:

1. Create a demo session and select a demo photo.
2. Execute `version.create` with `{"name":"A"}`.
3. Execute `version.delete` with `{"index":0.9}`.
4. Observe success and the deletion of version 0.

The failing regression reports: `index 0.9 must be refused; got Ok(Null); catalog unchanged: false`.

This is a remaining case related to #1740 finding 4 and merged #1793. The earlier negative-index fix is present on main. I am preparing a fix with regression coverage.

title: Malformed mask and spot targets silently change the active object
author: AlexChambers
body:
## What happens

Several mask and spot commands treat malformed explicit targets as if the target was omitted. They then operate on the active mask or selected spot.

On `main` at `f34c7a8a`, synthetic regressions through public `Session::execute` reproduce:

- `mask.delete {"id":-1}` succeeds and deletes the active mask.
- `mask.update {"component":-1,"shape":{"kind":"brush","strokes":[]}}` succeeds and replaces component 0.
- `spot.delete {"index":-1}` succeeds and deletes the selected spot.
- `mask.select {"id":-1}` and `spot.select {"index":-1}` succeed and clear selection.

The deletion and update tests confirm that session state changes. Undo is available, but these malformed requests should never change another object.

## Expected

Reject a malformed supplied target before changing settings, selection, saved effects, or undo/history state. Use checked integer conversions so a large ID cannot wrap to a different mask.

Preserve existing valid defaults: omitted or null optional mutation targets use the active mask/spot; omitted or null selection targets clear selection. Preserve each command's component default.

## Where

`crates/engine/src/cmd/masks.rs` has shared and duplicated target parsers that combine `get`, `as_u64`, fallback selection, and unchecked casts. The affected paths include mask IDs, component indices and spot indices. `cmd/mask_effects.rs` also falls back to the active mask for malformed explicit targets and filters malformed entries out of effect target lists.

## Reproduction evidence

Create a procedural demo session with an active photo, create masks or spots using the public commands, then submit the malformed calls above. No external files or photographs are required.

Five public command regressions fail on unchanged main. For example, `spot.delete {"index":-1}` returns `Ok(Null)` while the state comparison reports `unchanged: false`.

I am preparing a bounded fix for these mask/spot target parsers and saved mask-effect targets, with …

title: LR-EXP-PRESETS: Named export presets (Instagram, Web, Full-Res)
author: Maijin
body:
## Summary

Add support for saved and built-in **Named Export Presets** in the Export dialog (`cmd:app.export`), addressing the gap noted in row `LR-EXP-PREVIOUS` (*"no named export presets yet"*).

## Motivation

While LightCraft supports aspect cropping (1:1, 4:5) and export sizing/sRGB conversion, users currently have to reconfigure dimensions, file formats, and color profiles manually every time they switch between exporting for print, web, and social media.

Having named presets - both built-in common targets and user-saved presets—would streamline common delivery pipelines.

## Proposed Presets

1. **Built-in Social & Web Presets:**
   - **Instagram Feed:** JPEG, sRGB, resize long edge to 1080 px, 85% quality, standard screen sharpening.
   - **Instagram Story / Reel:** JPEG, sRGB, resize long edge to 1920 px (9:16).
   - **Web / Portfolio:** JPEG/WebP, sRGB, 2048 px long edge, metadata stripped except copyright.
   - **Full Resolution Master:** Original size, JPEG 95% or 16-bit TIFF/AVIF, Display P3 / Rec. 2020.
2. **User-defined Presets:**
   - Ability to save the current Export dialog options under a custom name (`cmd:export.savePreset`).
   - Stored in user config (`~/.config/lightcraft/export_presets.json`).

## Parity Reference
- Tracks the gap in `docs/parity-checklist.md` under **`LR-EXP-PREVIOUS`**.

I understand from `docs/raw-parity.md` that for raws without a measured colour matrix LightCraft fits the starting look to the camera's embedded JPEG. That is what I see, and #577 asks for a way to opt out. This report adds a Panasonic-specific angle: the RAW carries colour metadata that a raw developer can read directly, and LightCraft currently ignores it.

`exiftool P1455577.RW2` (Panasonic DC-S5M2):

title: Edit In / Open Original In: the `app` parameter launches any executable (control channel, MCP --connect)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** Medium (code execution as the user for any client that can issue commands). **Confidence:** Confirmed by code trace.

## Source evidence
- [`crates/ui-egui/src/menus.rs:2303`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/f34c7a8a89e0d1bade0a6889185f40acecc84a9f/crates/ui-egui/src/menus.rs#L2303) (`photo.editInExternal`): `let editor = p.get("app").and_then(Value::as_str).map_or(configured, str::to_string);`
- [`crates/ui-egui/src/menus.rs:2397`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/f34c7a8a89e0d1bade0a6889185f40acecc84a9f/crates/ui-egui/src/menus.rs#L2397) (`photo.openOriginalInExternal`): same, falling back to `settings.external_editor`.
- [`apps/lightcraft/src/editors.rs:84-88`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/f34c7a8a89e0d1bade0a6889185f40acecc84a9f/apps/lightcraft/src/editors.rs#L84-L88): `Launcher::Program(p) => { let mut c = Command::new(p); c.args(paths); … }` (also `open_with`, [`apps/lightcraft/src/editors.rs:50-54`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/f34c7a8a89e0d1bade0a6889185f40acecc84a9f/apps/lightcraft/src/editors.rs#L50-L54)).
- `editors::check` only verifies that the launcher resolves; it does not restrict *which* program it is.
- `ui.set` can also deep-merge `settings.external_editor` from the control channel (`crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs:342-350`).

## Conditions and impact
Any client that can run commands picks the executable; the photo paths become its arguments (no shell, so no shell injection, but the program itself is attacker-chosen, and an imported file can be crafted to be both a valid image and a valid script for some interpreters).

Reach:
- the `--control` port via `engine.execute` → `LightcraftApp::run` → `menus::run_ui_command`; until #1970 lands that port has no authentication, so on shared / RDS machines another local user can trigger it;
- `lightcraft-cli mcp --connect` → `command_run` — an agent steered by prompt-injected photo metadata (title, caption, XMP) can be talked…

title: A 35-byte GIF makes the import probe decode a 1-gigapixel image (header fallback + 1 Gpx default cap → OOM abort)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** Medium (process abort on import; allocation failure is not a panic, so `catch_unwind` does not help). **Confidence:** Confirmed, reproduced (16384² canvas: `read_header` → `Ok` after ~1 s with a 5.1 GB peak; 32768² is allowed).

## Source evidence

```

title: Tiled raw decode still has no aggregate memory budget: every tile's nominal buffer is held at once (residual of #1512)

title: Lossy JPEG tiles and embedded previews in raws allocate from the JPEG header up to 65536² (~12.9 GB)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** Medium (OOM abort on desktop; on wasm32 a panic inside zune-jpeg, i.e. abort). **Confidence:** Confirmed by trace into zune-jpeg 0.5.15 (`decoder.rs:215-218`: `decode_headers()?; let size = self.output_buffer_size().unwrap(); let mut out = vec![0; size];`).

## Source evidence
- [`crates/raw/src/tiffraw.rs:228-240`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/f34c7a8a89e0d1bade0a6889185f40acecc84a9f/crates/raw/src/tiffraw.rs#L228-L240): `DecoderOptions::default().set_max_width(1 << 16).set_max_height(1 << 16)…; d.decode()` — the dimension check happens after `decode()`.
- Callers: DNG lossy tiles (`tiffraw.rs:182`) and `crates/raw/src/wb_estimate.rs:69` (`from_preview`), which decodes the file's *embedded preview*; its `MAX_PREVIEW_PIXELS` check runs only after decoding.

## Conditions and impact
A JPEG SOF declaring 65535×65535 RGB makes zune allocate ~12.9 GB from a few hundred bytes. On wasm32 `65535*65535*3` overflows `usize`, `output_buffer_size()` is `None` and zune's own `unwrap` panics (abort under the web profile).

## Recommended remediation
```diff
- let px = d.decode()?;
+ d.decode_headers().map_err(…)?;
+ let info = d.info().ok_or(…)?;
+ if (info.width as u64) * (info.height as u64) > expected_max_px { return Err(RawError::Limit(…)) } // tile cw*ch, or MAX_PREVIEW_PIXELS
+ let px = d.decode()?;
```
and set `max_width` / `max_height` to the expected tile or preview size instead of `1 << 16`.

## Suggested regression test
`lossy_jpeg` on a minimal JPEG whose SOF says 65535×65535 returns an error without allocating (dhat peak < 1 MiB).

title: ERF/MEF: the raw IFD is accepted on its declared StripByteCounts, and the import probe allocates up to 2 GiB
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** Medium (multi-GiB allocation per file at import, in parallel across a folder; with the preview decode it can abort). **Confidence:** Confirmed by code trace.

## Source evidence
- [`crates/raw/src/vendor/erf.rs:50`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/f34c7a8a89e0d1bade0a6889185f40acecc84a9f/crates/raw/src/vendor/erf.rs#L50): `matches!(info.chunks(len as u64).as_slice(), [c] if Some(c.len) == (w * 8 / 5).checked_mul(h))` — `c.len` is the *tag value*; `chunk_bytes` later clips silently.
- [`crates/raw/src/vendor/erf.rs:96-103`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/f34c7a8a89e0d1bade0a6889185f40acecc84a9f/crates/raw/src/vendor/erf.rs#L96-L103): runs in `Mode::Header` too ("the white balance is measured from the samples, so the header probe reads them too"): `let mut d = vec![0u16; n]; unpack(src, &mut d); … wb_estimate::as_shot(bytes, …)`.
- `crates/raw/src/vendor/mef.rs:44` and `:92-99`: identical pattern.

## Conditions and impact
An Epson- (or Mamiya-) tagged TIFF with width 32760 × height 32768 and a StripByteCounts value matching the formula, but only a few KB of real data, allocates and writes 2 GiB during the header probe, then decodes the embedded preview (see the lossy-JPEG issue).

## Recommended remediation
```diff
- [c] if Some(c.len) == (w * 8 / 5).checked_mul(h)
+ [c] if Some(c.len) == (w * 8 / 5).checked_mul(h) && chunk_bytes(bytes, c).is_some_and(|s| s.len() as u64 == c.len)
```
(same in `mef.rs`).

## Suggested regression test
`probe_info` on a 4 KB ERF declaring 32760×32768 with a matching StripByteCounts returns an error (truncated) without allocating the sample buffer.

title: XMP: nested struct property keys grow quadratically (423 KB packet → 2.3 GB), reached automatically on import
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** Medium (OOM abort). **Confidence:** Confirmed, reproduced (423 KB packet → 2.32 GB of `properties` keys in 3.7 s, 5,492×).

## Source evidence
- [`crates/meta/src/xmp.rs:312`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/f34c7a8a89e0d1bade0a6889185f40acecc84a9f/crates/meta/src/xmp.rs#L312) `collect_property`: `let key = format!("{prefix}{}", p.name); … let struct_prefix = format!("{key}/");` — every leaf key copies the full ancestor path.
- [`crates/meta/src/xmp.rs:151`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/f34c7a8a89e0d1bade0a6889185f40acecc84a9f/crates/meta/src/xmp.rs#L151) / [`crates/meta/src/xmp.rs:226`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/f34c7a8a89e0d1bade0a6889185f40acecc84a9f/crates/meta/src/xmp.rs#L226): `MAX_DEPTH = 64` and `MAX_NODES` bound the shape, but nothing bounds element/attribute name length or total key bytes; attribute-form properties ([`crates/meta/src/xmp.rs:301`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/f34c7a8a89e0d1bade0a6889185f40acecc84a9f/crates/meta/src/xmp.rs#L301) `collect_description`) are not counted against `MAX_NODES`.

## Conditions and impact
Shape: 58 nested `<a:nnnn…(2000 chars) rdf:parseType="Resource">` elements, then 200 k distinct empty leaves (`<b:0/>…<b:199999/>`); ~2 MB is past 20 GB.

Reached from `.xmp` sidecars (`crates/engine/src/sidecar.rs:502` `read_packet`, an unbounded read), from embedded XMP in PNG iTXt / WebP `XMP ` / TIFF tag 700 via `probe_bytes` on every import, from preset import (zip entries up to 256 MiB; this pattern compresses extremely well) and from `merge_xmp`.

## Recommended remediation
- In `parse_tree`: refuse input > 16 MiB, element/attribute names > 1 KiB, and count attributes toward `MAX_NODES`.
- In `collect_*`: carry a total key-bytes budget (e.g. 64 MiB) and return `TooComplex` past it.

## Suggested regression test
The PoC shape (depth 58 × 2000-char names × 20 k leaves) returns `Err(TooComplex)` in under 100 ms.

title: prefs.json LUT profile paths are trusted: read unbounded on library open, and Delete Imported Profile can delete outside Profiles/ via `..`
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** Medium. **Confidence:** read path Confirmed; delete path Plausible (needs the library path).

## Source evidence
- [`crates/engine/src/cmd/lut_profiles.rs:29-35`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/f34c7a8a89e0d1bade0a6889185f40acecc84a9f/crates/engine/src/cmd/lut_profiles.rs#L29-L35) `register_all`: `std::fs::read_to_string(&p.file)` with no size cap and no containment check, called synchronously from `open_stores` (`crates/engine/src/library.rs:504`).
- [`crates/engine/src/cmd/lut_profiles.rs:160`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/f34c7a8a89e0d1bade0a6889185f40acecc84a9f/crates/engine/src/cmd/lut_profiles.rs#L160): `if profiles_dir(s).is_some_and(|d| Path::new(&gone.file).starts_with(d)) { let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&gone.file); }` — `Path::starts_with` is lexical and does not resolve `..`.

## Conditions and impact
A library whose `prefs.json` names
- `"/dev/zero"` → grows until the allocator aborts;
- a FIFO → the UI thread blocks forever on open;
- `\\host\share\x.cube` (Windows) → an SMB connection on open (NTLM hash exposure) plus a stall;
- `"<lib>/Profiles/../../home/u/doc"` → passes the delete check; "Delete Imported Profile" deletes that file.

Weaker relatives: `smart_previews_dir` (`library.rs:517`) redirects where previews are written; `export_presets[].subfolder` keeps `/` and `..` (`export.rs:1040`); watermark / identity-plate / printer-profile paths are read on use.

## Recommended remediation
```rust
fn inside_profiles(s: &Session, f: &Path) -> bool {
    let (Some(d), Ok(f)) = (profiles_dir(s).and_then(|d| d.canonicalize().ok()), f.canonicalize()) else { return false };
    f.parent() == Some(d.as_path()) && f.metadata().is_ok_and(|m| m.is_file() && m.len() <= 64 << 20)
}
```
Use it before reading (with a capped read) and before deleting; reject `..` in `subfolder` as `folder_template_error` already does for folder templates.

title: catalog.log: `resync` is quadratic in the line length, so a damaged log line hangs library open
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** Medium (UI hang when opening a hostile or badly damaged library). **Confidence:** Confirmed by code trace (not timed).

## Source evidence
- [`crates/catalog/src/journal.rs:270-276`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/f34c7a8a89e0d1bade0a6889185f40acecc84a9f/crates/catalog/src/journal.rs#L270-L276):
```rust
(1..line.len().saturating_sub(START.len() - 1)).filter(|&i| line[i..].starts_with(START)).find_map(|i| {
    let rec = std::str::from_utf8(&line[i..]).ok().map(|l| l.trim_end_matches('\r')).and_then(decode_record)?;
```
Each `{"seq":` occurrence in a line that fails to decode triggers an O(L) `from_utf8` plus decode.

## Conditions and impact
A 2 MB line of `{"seq":` repeated costs ~10¹¹ operations; at 16 MB opening effectively never finishes. It runs on library open.

## Recommended remediation
Only the record that retried the failed append can match, so try the last occurrence only:
```diff
- (1..len).filter(|&i| line[i..].starts_with(START)).find_map(|i| { … })
+ let i = line.windows(START.len()).rposition(|w| w == START).filter(|&i| i > 0)?;
+ let rec = std::str::from_utf8(&line[i..]).ok()…and_then(decode_record)?;
```

## Suggested regression test
`MemStore` with a valid snapshot and a log of `"{\"seq\":".repeat(300_000)`: `Journal::open` finishes in under 1 s.

title: TIFF and PNG decoder limits are pixel-derived byte budgets of 32 GiB / 8 GiB; multiband TIFF bypasses the pixel check
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** Medium (OOM abort from a few-KB file). **Confidence:** Confirmed (tiff 0.11.3 `read_image` → `to_result_buffer(&limits)` allocates the whole result up front).

## Source evidence
- [`crates/codecs/src/tiff_codec.rs:97`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/f34c7a8a89e0d1bade0a6889185f40acecc84a9f/crates/codecs/src/tiff_codec.rs#L97): `limits.decoding_buffer_size = opts.max_pixels.saturating_mul(4 * 8)` → 32 GiB at the default 2³⁰ px.
- [`crates/codecs/src/png_codec.rs:17`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/f34c7a8a89e0d1bade0a6889185f40acecc84a9f/crates/codecs/src/png_codec.rs#L17): `bytes: opts.max_pixels.saturating_mul(8)` → 8 GiB.
- `check_size` ignores SamplesPerPixel; `layout()` accepts `Multiband { num_samples }` up to 65535.

## Conditions and impact
A deflate-compressed 1024×1024 TIFF with SamplesPerPixel = 4000 at 8 bits passes `check_size` as 1 Mpx and allocates a 4 GB `DecodingResult` from a file of a few KB; at the 1 Gpx cap up to 32 GiB.

## Recommended remediation
Give both crates a real byte budget (2–4 GiB, or derived from physical RAM) rather than `max_pixels × bytes`, and refuse `n_samples > 8` (or count samples in `check_size`).

## Suggested regression test
A synthetic multiband TIFF with 4000 samples returns `TooLarge`/`Malformed` without allocating.

## Scope / related
Note PR #1989 (fix for #1983) proposes `intermediate_buffer_size` = 32 bytes per allowed pixel, i.e. also up to 32 GiB; a fixed byte cap that still admits #1983's 138 MB strip would cover both.

title: release.yml passes every code-signing secret to a reusable workflow tracked at `craft-common-actions@main`
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** Medium (supply chain). **Confidence:** Confirmed.

## Source evidence
- [`.github/workflows/release.yml:23-45`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/f34c7a8a89e0d1bade0a6889185f40acecc84a9f/.github/workflows/release.yml#L23-L45): `uses: storytold/craft-common-actions/.github/workflows/release.yml@main` with `APPLE_CERTIFICATE`, `APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD`, `APPLE_ID`, `APPLE_PASSWORD`, `WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE*`, `AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET`, `AZURE_SIGNING_*` passed as secrets, and `permissions: contents: write`.

Anyone who can push to (or compromises) `craft-common-actions` main receives the Developer ID certificate, notarisation credentials and Azure Trusted Signing credentials on the next push to `release`, and can ship signed binaries. `freebsd.yml` / `windows-arm64.yml` use the same `@main` pattern but without secrets (lower risk).

## Recommended remediation
- Pin the *release* reusable workflow to a commit SHA (`…/release.yml@<40-hex> # vX.Y`) and let Renovate/Dependabot bump it; keep `@main` for secret-free CI if desired.
- Protect `craft-common-actions` main (required review, no force-push).
- Move signing secrets into a GitHub Environment with required reviewers.

## Scope / related
Related in spirit: #1727 (2FA / signed commits).

| rustls-webpki 0.102.8 | 2026-0049, 0098, 0099, 0104 | `rustls-rustcrypto 0.0.2-alpha` | path validation uses webpki 0.103.15 (patched); 0.102 appears to be used for algorithm ids only — needs verification |
| rsa 0.9.10 | 2023-0071 (Marvin) | `rustls-rustcrypto` | verification only, no private-key ops — low |
| quick-xml 0.38.4 | 2026-0194, 0195 | meta, lensdb | not reached (`Reader` with `with_checks(false)`, no `NsReader`); PR #1464 bumps it |
| zip 7.2.0 | 2026-0367/0368/0369 | candle-core (SAM) | not reached (no `extract()` call) |
| paste, ttf-parser | unmaintained | faer-core, ab_glyph | informational |

## Conditions and impact
`rustls-rustcrypto` is an alpha, unaudited provider used for every model download. Downloads are SHA-256-pinned (limits integrity impact), but not the SAM tokenizer files. The repo has no `deny.toml` (so `cargo deny check licenses` rejects everything) and no workflow runs `cargo audit` / `cargo deny`.

## Recommended remediation
- `cargo update -p rustls` (and merge #1464).
- Track `rustls-rustcrypto` releases (the pure-Rust rule excludes ring / aws-lc-rs, so this is an accepted risk to watch).
- Add a `deny.toml` (licence allow-list, `[sources] allow-git = ["https://github.com/storytold/craft-libs"]`), run `cargo deny check` in `cargo xtask ci`, and a weekly scheduled `cargo audit`.
