title: TIFF/raw: O(n²) chunk-length inference and range building let a few-MB file hang the import probe
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** Medium (CPU denial of service at import). **Confidence:** Confirmed by code trace (not timed).

## Source evidence
- [`crates/tiff/src/image.rs:145`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/f34c7a8a89e0d1bade0a6889185f40acecc84a9f/crates/tiff/src/image.rs#L145): `let next = self.offsets.iter().copied().filter(|&o| o > offset).min().unwrap_or(data_len);` runs once per chunk when byte counts are missing → O(n²).
- [`crates/raw/src/sparse.rs:51-75`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/f34c7a8a89e0d1bade0a6889185f40acecc84a9f/crates/raw/src/sparse.rs#L51-L75): `Ranges::insert` rebuilds the whole vector on every insert; called per chunk at [`crates/raw/src/sparse.rs:250-253`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/f34c7a8a89e0d1bade0a6889185f40acecc84a9f/crates/raw/src/sparse.rs#L250-L253) → O(n²).

## Conditions and impact
The offset count is bounded only by the value budget (8 × file length): a few-MB DNG with ~10⁶ TileOffsets and no TileByteCounts costs ~5·10¹¹ comparisons *per call*, and the header probe calls `chunks` several times (check_image, preview candidates, header plan).

## Recommended remediation
Sort + dedup offsets once and use `partition_point` for the next larger offset; build ranges by collecting, sorting and merging in one pass; cap the chunk count (e.g. 2²⁰ → `Limit`, or fall back to `HeaderPlan::Whole`).

## Suggested regression test
A synthetic TIFF with 10⁶ tile offsets and no byte counts: `probe_info` returns within 1 s.

title: Face index: a torn or failed append shifts every later record (silent corruption of suggestions and scanned set)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** Low (derived data, silently wrong). **Confidence:** Confirmed by code trace.

## Source evidence
- [`crates/engine/src/faces_index.rs:158-169`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/f34c7a8a89e0d1bade0a6889185f40acecc84a9f/crates/engine/src/faces_index.rs#L158-L169) and `:327-329`: a partial trailing record is ignored but `file_matches = true` is set.
- [`crates/engine/src/faces_index.rs:203-208`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/f34c7a8a89e0d1bade0a6889185f40acecc84a9f/crates/engine/src/faces_index.rs#L203-L208) and `:343-347`: `save()` then appends after the fragment; a failed `write_all` (full disk) keeps `unsaved` and appends it again after the partial bytes.

## Conditions and impact
Every later record is misaligned: wrong photo ids, garbage embeddings that still pass `is_finite`, wrong "already scanned" ids → wrong face suggestions and photos that are never scanned.

## Recommended remediation
On load, if `rest.len() % RECORD != 0`, set `rewrite = true` (or `set_len` back to the last whole record); on an append error, `set_len(old_len)` before returning `Err`, as `Journal::append` does.

## Suggested regression test
Write a valid index, append 5 junk bytes, load, add an entry, save, reload: every key is intact.

title: Journal: a snapshot with `seq` near u64::MAX wraps in release, and every later edit is silently dropped on reopen
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** Low (needs a hostile or corrupted snapshot). **Confidence:** Confirmed by code trace.

## Source evidence
- [`crates/catalog/src/journal.rs:479`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/f34c7a8a89e0d1bade0a6889185f40acecc84a9f/crates/catalog/src/journal.rs#L479): `append` computes the next seq with unchecked `+ 1` (release has no overflow checks).
- [`crates/catalog/src/journal.rs:274`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/f34c7a8a89e0d1bade0a6889185f40acecc84a9f/crates/catalog/src/journal.rs#L274) and `:395`: `j.seq + 1` / `last + 1` — panics in debug builds.

## Conditions and impact
`"seq":18446744073709551615` in `catalog.snap` → the next record gets seq 0, every new record is ≤ the snapshot seq and is skipped as stale on the next open: all later edits are lost without an error.

## Recommended remediation
Treat `seq > u64::MAX / 2` as `Corrupt` when reading a snapshot; use `checked_add` in `append` and `resync`.

## Suggested regression test
Open a `MemStore` whose snapshot has `seq = u64::MAX`: `Journal::open` returns `Corrupt` (no panic in debug, no silent wrap in release).

title: XMP writer emits characters XML 1.0 forbids (U+0000–U+001F, U+FFFE), so other tools reject the whole sidecar
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** Low–Medium (interop corruption of sidecars). **Confidence:** Confirmed, reproduced: `caption = "a\u{1}b\u{0}c\u{FFFE}"` is written raw into `<rdf:li xml:lang="x-default">…</rdf:li>`.

## Source evidence
- `crates/meta/src/xmp.rs` writers escape only `<>&"'` (the `rdf:li` writers and `partial_escape` for `lc:*`).
- [`crates/meta/src/xmp.rs:175`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/f34c7a8a89e0d1bade0a6889185f40acecc84a9f/crates/meta/src/xmp.rs#L175) `entity()` accepts numeric references such as `�` / `` on read, so such characters round-trip.

## Conditions and impact
Sources: EXIF ASCII values (cut at NUL, other controls survive), IPTC Latin-1 decoding, XMP numeric references, MCP / user strings. LightCraft re-reads them (quick-xml doesn't check characters, so `merge_xmp`'s read-back check passes), but compliant parsers (Adobe XMP Toolkit, Exiv2/expat, libxml2) refuse the whole file — Lightroom ignores it or rewrites it and drops `lc:settings`.

## Recommended remediation
Filter to the XML 1.0 `Char` production before escaping:
```rust
fn xml_safe(s: &str) -> String {
    s.chars().filter(|&c| matches!(c, '\t' | '\n' | '\r') || (c >= '\u{20}' && c != '\u{FFFE}' && c != '\u{FFFF}')).collect()
}
```
and make `entity()` reject invalid code points.

## Suggested regression test
After `write_xmp` with a caption containing `\u{1}`, no character below U+0020 other than `\t \n \r` appears in the output.

title: Export: a panic inside the batch `thread::scope` leaves lanes waiting forever, so export hangs instead of reporting an error
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** Low (hang instead of an error dialog). **Confidence:** Plausible (control flow traced; no panic source demonstrated).

## Source evidence
- [`crates/engine/src/export.rs:2012-2034`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/f34c7a8a89e0d1bade0a6889185f40acecc84a9f/crates/engine/src/export.rs#L2012-L2034): if `placer.place` or the caller's `progress` closure panics inside `std::thread::scope`, `queue.stop()` is never called; the lane threads stay in `cv.wait`, the scope's implicit join never returns, and the command's last-resort `catch_unwind` never gets control.

## Conditions and impact
Any future panic in placement or progress reporting turns into a permanently busy export task (and a stuck UI if it is awaited).

## Recommended remediation
A drop guard created before the work starts:
```rust
struct StopOnDrop<'a>(&'a Queue);
impl Drop for StopOnDrop<'_> { fn drop(&mut self) { self.0.stop() } }
```

## Suggested regression test
Inject a `progress` closure that panics on the second call: the export returns an error within a second instead of hanging.

title: denoise-serve: unauthenticated clients can hold connection slots (120 s per read) and guess tokens without back-off
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** Low (opt-in service; loopback by default). **Confidence:** Confirmed.

## Source evidence
- [`crates/denoise/src/remote.rs:192`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/f34c7a8a89e0d1bade0a6889185f40acecc84a9f/crates/denoise/src/remote.rs#L192): `set_read_timeout(opts.timeout)` applies 120 s *per read call*, also before authentication.
- [`crates/denoise/src/remote.rs:56-58`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/f34c7a8a89e0d1bade0a6889185f40acecc84a9f/crates/denoise/src/remote.rs#L56-L58): the header line is read up to 4097 bytes.
- A failed token check only closes the connection; there is no back-off.

## Conditions and impact
A peer that sends one byte every ~100 s keeps a slot for days; `max_connections` (8) such peers deny service. When bound to a LAN address, tokens can be guessed at line rate (only a 16-character minimum).

## Recommended remediation
Give the auth line its own short deadline (e.g. 10 s total, recomputed on each read), switch to `opts.timeout` only after a good token, and add a per-IP back-off after a bad token.

## Scope / related
What's already right: the token is checked before any payload is read, the compare is constant-time, payload and inflation are capped, and a non-loopback bind prints a warning.

title: SAM 3 worker: no token, serves one client at a time, and a transient accept error ends the server
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** Low. **Confidence:** Confirmed.

## Source evidence
- [`crates/segment/src/remote.rs:188-206`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/f34c7a8a89e0d1bade0a6889185f40acecc84a9f/crates/segment/src/remote.rs#L188-L206): `for stream in listener.incoming() { serve_client(…) }` with a 10 min read timeout and no authentication.
- [`crates/segment/src/remote.rs:198`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/f34c7a8a89e0d1bade0a6889185f40acecc84a9f/crates/segment/src/remote.rs#L198): `let mut stream = stream.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;` returns from the accept loop on `EMFILE` / `ECONNABORTED`.
- `Client::connect` (`:82-91`) trusts any loopback peer.

## Conditions and impact
Any local process can occupy the worker for 10 minutes or use the GPU; a process that binds the port first receives the user's image pixels and can return arbitrary masks; one transient accept error kills the worker.

## Recommended remediation
`let Ok(mut stream) = stream else { continue };`, plus a random token (env var or a 0600 file) sent in the first frame, and a short handshake timeout.

## Scope / related
Frames are already size-limited and panics are caught; browser HTTP requests are rejected by the length prefix.

title: TIFF reader: up to 1024 IFDs × 8192 entries from overlapping tables (~400 MB of entries from ~100 KB)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** Low–Medium (memory amplification per parse; `Tiff::parse` runs several times per file and across parallel imports; can reach the wasm memory ceiling). **Confidence:** Plausible (computed from the code, not measured).

## Source evidence
- [`crates/tiff/src/reader.rs:25`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/f34c7a8a89e0d1bade0a6889185f40acecc84a9f/crates/tiff/src/reader.rs#L25): `ParseOptions` defaults `max_ifds: 1024`, `max_entries: 8192`.
- [`crates/tiff/src/reader.rs:194-199`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/f34c7a8a89e0d1bade0a6889185f40acecc84a9f/crates/tiff/src/reader.rs#L194-L199): `Vec::with_capacity(dir.read)` and one `Entry` per table entry; count-0 entries cost nothing from the value budget, and IFD tables at different offsets may overlap.

## Conditions and impact
A ~8 K-entry table with SubIFD pointers each shifted by one entry reuses the same bytes for up to 1024 IFDs → ~8 M `Entry` values × ~48 B ≈ 400 MB from a ~100 KB file.

## Recommended remediation
Charge every entry at least its 12-byte table size against the budget, or add a total-entries cap across the parse (e.g. 64 K) to `ParseOptions`.

title: `engine` and `meta` crate roots lack the `deny(clippy::unwrap_used, …)` attribute; `assert!` in production GPU code
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** Low (hardening; the never-crash rule isn't enforced in the largest crate). **Confidence:** Confirmed.

## Source evidence
- [`crates/engine/src/lib.rs:11`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/f34c7a8a89e0d1bade0a6889185f40acecc84a9f/crates/engine/src/lib.rs#L11) and [`crates/meta/src/lib.rs:12`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/f34c7a8a89e0d1bade0a6889185f40acecc84a9f/crates/meta/src/lib.rs#L12) carry `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` but not `#![deny(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic, clippy::unimplemented, clippy::todo, clippy::unreachable)]`, which CLAUDE.md says every production crate root has. A scan finds no production `unwrap` in engine today, but regressions in its ~86 k lines would pass `cargo xtask ci`. (`crates/meta/src/xmp.rs:256, 291-294` has guarded `expect`s that would need the documented `#[allow(clippy::expect_used)]` form.)
- `clippy::panic` does not cover `assert!`: `crates/gpu/src/ctx.rs:514, 538` and `crates/gpu/src/params.rs:151` assert in production (mitigated by `catch_unwind`; an `assert` on `len <= src.len` also guards a possible empty `slice(..0)` in wgpu).

## Conditions and impact
Without the attribute, the policy in CLAUDE.md is not machine-checked for these crates.

## Recommended remediation
- Add the attribute to both roots (and annotate the provably infallible `expect`s).
- Have an xtask check verify that every production root carries both `forbid(unsafe_code)` and the deny list.
- Replace the GPU `assert!`s with `fail(FailKind::Fatal, …)` + return, and return early when `len == 0`.
- Optional ratchet: `clippy::indexing_slicing` / `arithmetic_side_effects` in parser crates (`tiff`, `raw`, `codecs`, `meta`, `catalog`) with a count baseline that may only go down.

## Scope / related
The "tests don't run on three platforms in CI" part is #1050 / PR #1148 and is not repeated here.

title: wasm32: unchecked `usize` products in raw/codecs wrap and defeat size validation (abort in the web build)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Assessment
**Severity:** Info–Low (web build only; on 64-bit `u32 × u32` fits). **Confidence:** Plausible.

## Source evidence
- [`crates/raw/src/vendor/arw.rs:624`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/f34c7a8a89e0d1bade0a6889185f40acecc84a9f/crates/raw/src/vendor/arw.rs#L624): `if w * h > crate::MAX_SAMPLES` — 65536 × 65536 wraps to 0 on 32-bit; later `vec![0u16; w*h]` at `:645, 662`.
- [`crates/raw/src/lib.rs:767`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/f34c7a8a89e0d1bade0a6889185f40acecc84a9f/crates/raw/src/lib.rs#L767): `self.data.len() != self.width * self.height * self.cpp`.
- `crates/raw/src/vendor/cr2.rs:164` (`fw * fh * nc`), `crates/raw/src/tiffraw.rs:200`, `crates/codecs/src/convert.rs:94` (`n * ch` for 2³⁰ px × 4).

## Conditions and impact
A wrapped validation lets later stages index with the true dimensions → panic, which aborts under `profile.web` (`panic = "abort"`).

## Recommended remediation
Use `checked_mul` (as most decoders already do), e.g. `w.checked_mul(h).filter(|n| *n <= MAX_SAMPLES)`; consider a lower default pixel cap on wasm32 and a `clippy --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -W clippy::arithmetic_side_effects` pass for raw and codecs.

title: MCP: file-writing tools (export, render_photo, screenshot) are annotated `destructiveHint: false` although they overwrite any path

title: Nikon D750: colours less saturated than Lightroom + ColorChecker DCP (mean ΔE2000 5.6 flash / 3.3 indoor)
author: dieli
body:
LightCraft 0.8.0 renders Nikon D750 NEFs noticeably less saturated than Lightroom Classic 15.6 with a ColorChecker DCP, and shifts the brightness of reds/yellows and blues in opposite directions. The grey patches match closely, so this is colour rendering, not white balance or tone.

## Measurement

title: History steps store a full copy of every segmentation mask (98 % of catalog.snap)
author: Eliksir67
body:
Hello,

*Investigated and written with Claude Code.*

On LightCraft 0.8.0 (Linux), a library of 528 photos has a `catalog.snap` of 187.8 MB. Measured with `jq` on the file:

| Part of the photo records | Size |
|---|---|
| All photo records | 187.8 MB |
| History steps | 184.9 MB |
| Masks in history steps | 183.6 MB |
| Segmentation grids (`side` / `data`) in history steps | 181.8 MB |
| Versions | 0.8 MB |

Only 20 photos have a history (475 steps, 90 at most on one photo), so about 390 KB per step. Those photos had model segmentation masks, added through `mask.add` with a segmentation (the stored form SAM 3 masks use too), and the masks were deleted later; the photos' current settings take about 2 MB.

Each history step keeps its own copy of every segmentation grid of the photo, so an unchanged mask is stored again with each slider change. The history holds 830 grids (all 1024 × 1024, about 220 KB each), but only 126 distinct ones, 25.9 MB in all. To check it on one photo: ten masks added one after another (people and body parts), then a preset, gave 11 new history steps holding 65 copies of the 10 grids, and `catalog.snap` went from 187.8 MB to 209.2 MB; each further slider change on that photo adds another copy of all ten, about 2.7 MB. Deleting a mask keeps the copies in the older steps, as expected for undo, until the 200-step limit drops them. The whole file is rewritten at each compaction and read at each open.

Would it make sense for history steps (and versions) to share a segmentation grid that hasn't changed, for example by keeping each distinct grid once in the catalog and referring to it? Here that would take the grids from 181.8 MB to 25.9 MB. As far as I can see, #800's compact records would keep masks as they are, since a mask is never a default value.

Thanks for the work on the catalog.

title: Lens corrections for Canon EOS 5D RAW files
author: p0ancf-36
body:
## Description

Lens corrections fail for RAW files (`.CR2`) from the original Canon EOS 5D when the `LensModel` EXIF field is missing, even though ExifTool can identify the lens from other metadata.

LightCraft displays the following error when I try to enable lens corrections:

```
No lens data embedded in this file (DNG lens opcodes only).
```

Adding an EXIF `LensModel` tag using the lens name reported by ExifTool's `LensID` resolves the problem.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open a `.CR2` file taken with the original Canon EOS 5D.
2. Try to enable lens corrections.
3. Observe the error shown above.
4. Check the file's lens metadata:

```bash
exiftool -G1 -a -s -LensType -LensID -LensModel <path/to/image.CR2>
```

Output:

```
[Canon]     LensType  : Canon EF 50mm f/1.4 USM or Other Lens
[Canon]     LensType  : Canon EF 50mm f/1.4 USM or Other Lens
[Composite] LensID    : Yongnuo YN 35mm f/2
[Canon]     LensModel :
```

The `LensModel` field is empty, but ExifTool can identify the lens as `Yongnuo YN 35mm f/2`.

## Comparison with a newer Canon camera

For comparison, a Canon EOS 600D RAW file works with lens corrections without any metadata modifications.

Its metadata:

```
[Canon]     LensType  : Canon EF-S 18-135mm f/3.5-5.6 IS
[Canon]     LensType  : Canon EF-S 18-135mm f/3.5-5.6 IS
[Composite] LensID    : Canon EF-S 18-135mm f/3.5-5.6 IS
[Canon]     LensModel : EF-S18-135mm f/3.5-5.6 IS
[ExifIFD]   LensModel : EF-S18-135mm f/3.5-5.6 IS
```

Unlike the original EOS 5D file, this file contains populated `LensModel` metadata.

## Workaround

Running the following command on the original EOS 5D RAW file:

```bash
exiftool '-EXIF:LensModel<LensID' <path/to/image.CR2>
```

produces the following metadata:

```
[Canon]     LensType  : Canon EF 50mm f/1.4 USM or Other Lens
```

title: `catalog.query` / `library.filter`: an unknown filter key is ignored and every photo is returned
author: mischiatti75-spec
body:
**Summary.** `catalog.query` and `library.filter` accept a filter key that does not exist (a typo or a guessed name such as `cameraModel` instead of `camera`) and silently drop it, so the result is the whole library instead of an error. An agent or script then works on all photos while believing it has a filtered subset. `app.export` already rejects unknown parameters ("an unknown parameter … is an error, not a default"), so the filter is the odd one out.

**Environment.** lightcraft-cli 0.9.1, macOS 26, Apple M4 Max, headless.

**Steps to reproduce.**
```sh
python3 -c "from PIL import Image; [Image.new('RGB',(64,48),c).save(f'p{i}.jpg') for i,c in enumerate([(200,0,0),(0,200,0),(0,0,200)])]"
exiftool -overwrite_original -Make=TestMake -Model=TestCam p0.jpg
lightcraft-cli run --keep-going --import p0.jpg --import p1.jpg --import p2.jpg \
  catalog.query 'filter={"camera":"Nonexistent"}' \
  catalog.query 'filter={"cameraModel":"Nonexistent"}' \
  catalog.query 'filter={"foo":1}' \
  library.filter cameraModel=Nonexistent
```

**Actual.** `camera: "Nonexistent"` → `total: 0` (correct). `cameraModel: "Nonexistent"` → `ok: true, total: 3`; `foo: 1` → `ok: true, total: 3`; `library.filter cameraModel=…` → `ok: true, count: 3`. No warning in any reply.

**Expected.** An unknown filter key is an error (`ok: false`, naming the key and listing the valid ones), as `app.export` does for its parameters. A warning in the reply would also do, as long as it is not silent.

**Why / use case.** Driving the library from MCP/CLI scripts: a filter that quietly matches everything is worse than a failed command, because the next step (export, keyword, delete) then runs on the whole catalog.

title: Fill Location from GPS: small towns get the nearest city of 15,000+ people, several km away, with no notice
author: mischiatti75-spec
body:
**Summary.** `metadata.reverseGeocode` uses GeoNames `cities15000`, so a photo taken in a town under 15,000 inhabitants gets the name of the nearest larger town, which can be several kilometres away and a different municipality. The reply does include `distance`, but the City field is filled anyway and nothing in the UI or docs mentions the limit (`docs/parity-checklist.md` only says "offline from GeoNames").

**Environment.** lightcraft-cli 0.9.1, macOS 26, Apple M4 Max, headless. Dataset: `cities15000.txt`, `admin1CodesASCII.txt`, `countryInfo.txt` from download.geonames.org, passed with `dataset=`.

**Steps to reproduce.**
```sh
python3 -c "from PIL import Image; Image.new('RGB',(64,48)).save('a.jpg'); Image.new('RGB',(64,48),(9,9,9)).save('b.jpg')"
exiftool -overwrite_original -GPSLatitude=45.4342 -GPSLatitudeRef=N -GPSLongitude=12.3388 -GPSLongitudeRef=E a.jpg   # Piazza San Marco, Venice
exiftool -overwrite_original -GPSLatitude=44.3036 -GPSLatitudeRef=N -GPSLongitude=9.2097 -GPSLongitudeRef=E b.jpg    # Portofino (~400 inhabitants)
# GeoNames files in ./geonames (or run metadata.downloadPlaceNames first)
lightcraft-cli run --import a.jpg --import b.jpg metadata.reverseGeocode dataset=geonames dryRun=true
```

**Actual.** `a.jpg` → `Venice, Veneto, Italy`, distance 580 m (fine). `b.jpg` → `Rapallo, Liguria, Italy`, distance 5317 m: a different town.

**Expected.** One or more of:
- document the 15,000-inhabitant limit in the command help and the Fill Location dialog;
- an option to use a denser GeoNames list (`cities5000`, `cities1000` or `cities500`) for rural areas;
- a `maxDistance` parameter (or a default cut-off) above which City is left empty or flagged, rather than filled with a neighbouring town.

**Why / use case.** Site photos in small municipalities (surveying, inspections): the town name ends up in captions and reports, and a neighbouring municipality is a wrong record rather than a missing one.

title: Nikon Z 400mm f/4.5 + Z TC-1.4x: Lensfun correction profile unavailable
author: JuergenTenckhoff
body:
# Lensfun profile matching fails for Nikon Z 400mm f/4.5 with Z TC-1.4x teleconverter

### Environment
- LightCraft v0.9.1, Linux x86_64 AppImage
- Nikon Z9
- NIKKOR Z 400mm f/4.5 VR S
- Nikon Z TC-1.4x teleconverter
- Latest Lensfun database from the official GitHub repository
- `LIGHTCRAFT_LENSFUN_DIR` correctly configured and verified in the running process

### Observed behavior

**Without teleconverter:**
- EXIF lens model: `NIKKOR Z 400mm f/4.5 VR S`
- Focal length: 400 mm
- LightCraft successfully recognizes and applies the Lensfun profile.

**With Z TC-1.4x:**
- EXIF lens model: `NIKKOR Z 400mm f/4.5 VR S Z TC-1.4x`
- Focal length: 560 mm
- LightCraft does not recognize a matching lens correction profile.

Both configurations use the same Nikon Z9 camera body.

### Possible cause

Looking at `crates/lensdb/src/lib.rs`, the current lens name matching algorithm appears to require agreement between numerical tokens in the EXIF lens model and the database profile name.

The additional `1.4` in the teleconverter designation may prevent a match.

However, the existing Lensfun calibration for the 400mm lens should not automatically be applied to the 560mm combination, since the teleconverter changes the optical characteristics.

### Suggested enhancement

Would it be possible to:

1. Recognize Nikon lens and teleconverter combinations separately from the base lens?
2. Identify the base lens even when a teleconverter is attached?
3. Apply corrections only when a suitable calibration for the complete optical combination exists, or when reliable embedded Nikon correction data is available?
4. Optionally display the recognized lens and teleconverter separately, even when no correction profile is available?

### Additional information

The original Nikon Z9 NEF files can be provided for independent testing.

I have also successfully verified the recent DNG color matrix fix from PR #1750 using real Nikon Z9 NEFs under Linux with darktable.

title: Contributors: the About window's list is stale since 2026-10-10 and nothing refreshes it
author: valenfys
body:
## Summary

The About window's contributor list is a week out of date. `contributors/contributors.json` is a snapshot at `c545cc5e` (2026-10-10) and has not been regenerated since, so nobody whose first commit landed after that date is credited. Four releases have shipped with the stale list: v0.6.0 (10-10), v0.7.1 (10-12), v0.8.0 (10-14) and v0.9.1 (10-17).

## Why it goes stale

- `crates/ui-egui/build.rs` bakes `contributors.json` + `people.toml` into the binary, so the About window shows whatever snapshot is committed.
- The snapshot is only regenerated by hand (`AGENTS.md`, `docs/contributors.md` → "Refreshing (maintainers)": `python3 ../../craftrules/scripts/contributors.py .`). Nothing in `.github/workflows/` or `xtask` runs it, and it isn't part of the release steps: the last refreshes were `1cc0dde7` (the 0.5.0 bump) and `54369512`.
- Outside contributors can't refresh it themselves: `storytold/craftrules`, which holds the script, returns 404 for non-members (see #1183).

## Options (maintainer decision)

1. **Scheduled workflow**: a weekly (or on-push-to-`main`) GitHub Action that checks out craftrules, runs `contributors.py .`, and opens a PR when `contributors.json` changes.
2. **Release checklist step**: run `contributors.py .` in the release-prep commit, so every tagged build credits everyone up to that point.
3. **Staleness check**: a `cargo xtask` check (in `ci`, or release-only) that fails when the snapshot's `head` is more than N commits or days behind `main`.

These can be combined (e.g. 2 + 3 so a release can't ship stale). Any of them needs the script to be fetchable from CI.

In the meantime, a one-off refresh would credit everyone who has contributed since 2026-10-10.

## Evidence

- `main` at `31a677fe`; `contributors/contributors.json` → `"head": "c545cc5e…"`, `"head_date": "2026-10-10T05:40:18Z"`.
- `git log -- contributors/contributors.json`: last changed `54369512` (2026-10-10).
- Related: #252 (credits compiled in), #1183 (craftrules unr…

title: A preset that can't be saved is reported nowhere, and the web backup leaves it out
author: francoisgn
body:
A preset that can't be saved is reported nowhere, and the web backup leaves it out


Preset commands (`preset.create/delete/rename/move/favorite`) change `s.presets` directly, outside `pending_log`. When writing `presets.json` fails, `Session::persist()` (`crates/engine/src/library.rs`, around l.644-657) only logs the error: nothing goes to `unsaved()` or `last_error`, and the write is retried only at the next command.

Effects:
- Web: after a storage failure (quota exceeded, storage evicted), creating a preset and then File ▸ Back Up Library reports success, but the zip holds the previous `presets.json`. The unsaved-changes guard (#1987) doesn't see it, and a reload loses the preset.
- Desktop: with a full disk, a new preset is lost with no warning.

Proposed fix (small): surface the failed presets write as unsaved (a visible error, counted by `unsaved()`), retry it from `persist_if_dirty`, and have the backup refuse while it's pending. I'd like to take this one, on top of #1987.

Related: #103 (settings files, closed) covered unreadable and non-atomic writes, not a failed write going unreported. Noted as out of scope by @AlexChambers in the review of #1987.

title: Web build: a host bridge for embedding pages (?host=parent), like PdfCraft's
author: philkunz
body:
We run the LightCraft web build as a window in a web desktop that frames the web build, the same way as PdfCraft, GridCraft and CADCraft. Their `?host=parent` bridge lets the embedding page open files and receive saves. Without one, LightCraft can't tell the page about unsaved changes, so the page can't ask before a window with edits closes, and saves become browser downloads.

Proposal, the same family protocol as storytold/deckcraft#983 and storytold/wordcraft#2919, posted to the parent only with `?host=parent`:
- `lightcrafteady` / `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-philkunz-foss-global/410470bf-81b1-4e09-9a60-86819268a2c6/scratchpad/issues/lightcraftiled`: start-up handshake
- `lightcraft:open {name, bytes}`: the parent hands over a file to open
- `lightcraftve, Save As and exports go to the parent instead of a download
- `lightcraft:dirty {dirty}`: on every change of the unsaved state

title: Assisted Culling: adjustable burst gap and similarity
author: helgehelge123
body:
## Problem

Assisted Culling (`photo.analyze`, `crates/engine/src/cmd/cull.rs`) groups look-alike shots taken close together and marks the sharpest one. Both thresholds are constants:

- `BURST_GAP = 10` seconds between consecutive shots
- `SAME = 0.93` signature similarity

Sports and wildlife sequences break these: a panning burst changes the background from frame to frame, so the 8 × 8 signature drops below 0.93 and one 15-frame sequence splits into several groups (or none). A slow sequence (one frame every few seconds over a minute) runs past 10 s. The opposite case, a studio shoot where every frame looks alike, groups unrelated shots.

`stack.auto` already takes its gap as a parameter, and the Auto-Stack dialog has a slider for it.

## Proposal

- `photo.analyze` takes `burstGap` (seconds, default 10) and `similarity` (0..1, default 0.93). Bad values (negative, NaN, out of range) are refused before anything changes.
- The Assisted Culling dialog gets the two settings ("Shots in a burst are at most … apart", "How alike: Loose … Strict"), remembered for the next run.
- Defaults stay as today, so results don't change unless the user moves a control.

No new dependency, no model.

Related: #1251 / #1418 (background worker for the same command; whichever lands second rebases).

title: Assisted Culling: measure focus on the subject (face regions, camera focus point)
author: helgehelge123
body:
## Problem

Assisted Culling measures focus as the 90th percentile of block detail energy over the whole frame (`crates/pipeline/src/cull.rs`, `sharpness`). In sports, events and wildlife the sharp detail is often not the subject: a crowd, advertising boards, a net or grass in the focal plane. The frame with the sharpest background then wins its burst, and "Reject below focus" keeps frames whose subject is soft.

LightCraft already knows where the subject is for many photos, without a new model:

- **face regions** (`Photo::regions`, kind Face / Pet): from XMP, or from Detect Faces with the YuNet detector (`crates/engine/src/cmd/face_detect.rs`);
- **the camera's focus point** (`Photo::focus`, LR-VIEW-FOCUSPOINT, #1480), including what the camera tracked ("Face tracking", "Animal Eye Tracking").

Lightroom's Assisted Culling also rates the subject's focus rather than the frame's.

## Proposal

- `photo.analyze` measures focus inside the subject when the photo has one: the face regions (and pet regions), else the focus point's box, padded a little; else the whole frame as today.
- Small subjects get enough pixels: the subject is measured on a larger source than the 512 px thumbnail when its box would be too small to score (scores within a burst stay comparable, since they use the same measure).
- The stored analysis says which was measured (`subject: face | focusPoint | frame`) and keeps the frame score, so smart albums and filters keep working (`sharpness` = the subject score when there is one). Older catalogs read unchanged.
- The burst's best is chosen by the subject score; the dialog's text says "focus on faces / the focus point where known".
- Never runs a detector itself: photos without regions or focus point behave as today (the dialog can say "Detect Faces first for subject focus").

Out of scope here: eyes-open / expression scoring, which needs a landmark or eye-state model (maintainer's decision, like other model choices).

Related: #1418 (same command, bac…

title: Assisted Culling: stack each burst with its best photo on top
author: helgehelge123
body:
## Problem

After Assisted Culling, a 15-frame burst still takes 15 cells in the grid. The groups it found are only visible as the "Best of Similar Shots" rule / filter. Auto-Stack (`stack.auto`) stacks by capture time only, so it puts unrelated shots taken in quick succession into one stack and doesn't know which frame is best.

Requests nearby: #2232 (rate a whole collapsed stack), #2233 (expand/collapse by double click), #154 (bracket-aware auto-stacking).

## Proposal

- `photo.analyze` takes `stackGroups: bool` (default false). When set, each burst group of two or more photos becomes a collapsed stack with the group's best photo on top, in the same undo step as the analysis.
- Photos already in a stack are left alone (no re-stacking, no stack split), as `stack.auto` does.
- The Assisted Culling dialog gets a checkbox "Stack each burst, best photo on top".
- The result reports `stacks` (how many were made).

With this, culling a burst is: expand one stack, check its top frame in Loupe or Survey, done.

Related: #1418 (same command, background worker).

title: HDR display: render the HDR rendition on the GPU (so drags show HDR)
author: JordyUSA
body:
## Problem

On an HDR display, an HDR edit's loupe needs two renditions: the 8-bit SDR one (overlays, previews, histogram) and the float HDR one (display-linear, 1.0 = SDR white) that the scRGB window shows. The GPU kernel only writes 8-bit output (`lightcraft_gpu::handles`, `crates/gpu/src/lib.rs`), so the HDR rendition is a second render on the CPU (`crates/engine/src/media.rs`, `RenderJob` with `hdr_display`).

That second render is slow: it made a drag's drafts 3–5× slower than the GPU's SDR draft (measured 30 → 104 ms at 667×1000, 40 → 164 ms at 1067×1600, 49 → 264 ms at 1600×2400). So #1221 skips it for drafts: while a slider or brush drags, the photo shows its SDR rendition, and HDR comes back with the full render on release. Full renders still pay for the CPU HDR pass.

## Proposal

Render the HDR rendition on the GPU:

- a float output target (e.g. `Rgba16Float`) next to the 8-bit one, for `OutputDepth::F32Hdr` requests in sRGB primaries, without the SDR highlight compression;
- ideally keep it on the device and hand the texture to the HDR presenter (`lightcraft-hdr-display`) instead of reading it back and re-uploading;
- then let drafts carry HDR again (drop the `Quality::Draft` exclusion in `media.rs`) and update `docs/hdr-display.md` ("Not yet: … a GPU HDR render").

The same float path could also move Visualize HDR (`Overlay::HdrRange`) and 16-bit exports off the CPU.

## Acceptance

- GPU and CPU HDR renditions match within a tolerance (test like the existing GPU/CPU parity tests, skipping without a GPU).
- A drag on an HDR edit on an HDR display shows HDR, and the draft stays within the slider budget (≤ 16 ms draft on ~2.5 MP).
- CPU fallback still works when there is no GPU.

Follow-up to #1221.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Sidebar: deep folder trees push names out of a narrow panel — let the indent step follow the panel width

title: Capture One–style sessions, DAM-safe XMP sidecars, and Fujifilm film simulation / DR awareness
author: Lorenzoeffe
body:
## Context

I'm a long-time Capture One user (mostly Sessions) looking at LightCraft as a replacement. My setup, as a concrete test case:

- **Camera:** Fujifilm X-H1 (X-Trans CMOS III), always shooting RAW+JPEG.
- **Archive:** about 300,000 files since 2009, in `Year/Year-Month/Event` folders on local disks. Part of it will move to a disk that is stored offline.
- **Other programs:** I also use a DAM (digiKam). LightCraft shouldn't depend on it or on any other program, but the XMP it writes should be readable by them.
- **Legacy sidecars already in the archive:** ACDSee (2009, `acdsee:`), Adobe Camera Raw 7.2 (2013, `crs:` process version 2012, with masks and crops), darktable (2019–2021, `darktable:`, XMP versions 2 and 4).

**Updated 2026-10-22:** sections 1 and 2 are rewritten to describe the whole model more precisely; the section numbers are unchanged. I read the source at `c66014e` (2026-10-22). Corrections are welcome wherever I've misread it. The sections are independent and numbered, so they can be picked up one at a time, as was done for #2396.

### Already there

- **Local** browsing (`library.browse`): working in a folder without adding it to the library.
- Any folder can be a library (`lightcraft --library <dir>`, File ▸ Open Library…), with its own journal (`catalog.snap`, `catalog.log`), guarded by `catalog.lock`.
- XMP sidecars that are **merged, never replaced**: other programs' namespaces kept byte for byte, `.bak` copies of unreadable sidecars, stem/full naming, and the shared-stem rule for RAW+JPEG ([xmp-interop.md][xmp]).
- **Smart previews** with their own location, which render and edit with the original offline (LR-CLOUD-SMARTPREVIEW).
- **Find Missing Photos**, which matches by name, size and content hash (LRC-LIB-MISSING).
- **Fujifilm embedded lens corrections** (distortion and vignetting), with the X-H1 among the validated bodies ([fuji-lens-corrections.md][fuji-lens]).
- RAF decoding (uncompressed, lossless and lossy; Bayer and X-Trans)…

title: Feature request: Relink missing files when opening a project on a different OS
author: Hoferlukaslh
body: ## Description When a project is created on one OS (e.g. Windows) and then opened on another (e.g. Linux), the imported media files can't be found because the stored paths are not valid on the new OS (e.g. Windows paths with `\` separators or drive letters). Currently this results in an OS error and the user can't continue working. ## Steps to reproduce 1. On Windows, create a project in Lightcraft and import files. 2. Work on the project and save it. 3. Open the same project on a Linux machine. 4. Lightcraft fails with an OS error (the path contains `\`). ## Current behavior An OS error is raised because the stored path is invalid or not found on the current OS. The user has no way to fix it from within the app. ## Expected behavior If a file path is invalid for the current OS or the file can't be found, Lightcraft should: 1. Detect the missing/invalid file instead of raising a raw OS error. 2. Show a dialog asking the user where the file is located (file picker). 3. Update the project with the new path. ## Suggested improvements - Normalize path separators (`\` ↔ `/`) when loading a project, so paths saved on Windows can be resolved on Linux/macOS and vice versa. - Once the user locates one missing file, try to automatically resolve the other missing files by applying the same folder mapping (e.g. `C:\Users\me\Photos` → `/home/me/Photos`). - Offer a "Relink all missing files" option, with a list of the files that couldn't be found. - Optionally, store paths relative to the project file when possible, to improve portability.

title: [Feature] People masks: pick a person, then select parts (skin, hair, lips, eyes…), as in Lightroom
author: helgehelge123
body:
## What

Lightroom's Masking panel has a **People** entry. It lists the people it finds in the photo. You pick one and tick parts: Entire person, Face skin, Body skin, Eyebrows, Eye sclera, Iris and pupil, Lips, Teeth, Hair, Clothes. Each ticked part becomes its own mask component or one combined mask. For portraits this is the most used AI mask after Subject.

## What LightCraft already has

- **The data model.** `MaskShape::People { person, parts }` exists in `crates/develop/src/settings.rs`. `crates/pipeline/src/masks.rs` evaluates it from embedded DNG semantic mattes (iPhone ProRAW: skin, hair, teeth, glasses). Without a matching matte it falls back to the Subject heuristic. The Masking panel can show such a mask but cannot add one.
- **Faces.** `crates/faces` finds faces (YuNet with five landmarks) and aligns them. The face regions (MWG, optionally named) live in `meta.regions`.
- **SAM 3.** `crates/segment` gives per-instance masks and boxes for a text prompt (`Sam3::detect`). It also segments objects from clicks (`segment_clicks`), and Object / Describe store the result as a `seg`.

No issue or PR covers this yet. Related: #377 (Subject / Sky / Background via AI), #1219 (Sky via SAM 3), #1227 (Subject draft), #1322 (whole-photo heuristics), and row 5 B in `docs/gaps.md`.

## Proposal in two steps

### Step 1: people and coarse parts with SAM 3 (no new model) — draft PR

I have this working in draft PR #2358, so the questions below are about whether and how you want it:

- Masking ▸ **People** (and + / − ▸ People…) opens a chooser that lists the photo's faces, by name where it has one, else "Person 1, 2…". If the photo has no faces, it offers Detect Faces.
- **Entire Person:** SAM 3 `person` instances; the instance whose mask covers the face centre wins, with the instance box holding the face as the fallback. This separates people standing next to or behind each other.
- **Face Skin, Body Skin, Hair, Clothes:** SAM 3's own `skin`, `face`, `hair` and `clothes` …

title: Remove tool: brushed spots draw a stack of white rings, and content-aware Fill smears large holes
author: helgehelge123
body:
### What happens

On a real photo (indoor sports, a brushed stroke of ~10 dabs over a hand/ball edge) the Remove tool is hard to use:

1. **The overlay buries the result.** A brushed spot is drawn as one white circle per stored point. Holding or slowly dragging the brush stores a point every frame, so a short stroke shows dozens of stacked white rings (and a solid white blob while painting). The selected spot draws the same stack again for its source. With the rings on top you can't judge whether the patch matches its surroundings.
2. **Content-aware Fill looks smeared.** Big holes come out as a soft average: no grain, structure fades towards the middle, edges of the removed object ghost through the feather.

### Why (from the code, main d999e382)

**Stroke capture and overlay** (`crates/ui-egui/src/panels/detail.rs`, `remove_overlay`)
- Painting pushes `map.norm(q)` on every `dragged()` frame with no spacing or stationary check (the mask brush has both, #518). `spot.add` stores the points as-is.
- Every point gets its own `circle_stroke`, and the selected spot gets a second set for the source. The paint preview stacks `circle_filled(alpha 60)` per point.
- Render cost grows the same way: `spots::apply` takes the minimum distance over *all* points for every pixel of the box.

**Fill** (`crates/pipeline/src/spots.rs` `fill_box`, `crates/inpaint/src/patchmatch.rs`)
- Source patches only come from the stroke's box plus `2r`, so a large hole has little to copy from.
- Fine levels of holes over 96 px are refine-only: 1 EM iteration, 1 PatchMatch pass, search radius 2. The detail is mostly an upsampled coarse level.
- Every level ends with a weighted-average vote. That averages away grain and texture, so the fill reads as a smooth smear.
- Patch distance is SSD on scene-linear RGB, so highlights dominate and shadows match badly.

### Proposal

Two PRs:
1. **Stroke and overlay.**
   - Capture the brush stroke at a spacing of about r/4, and skip stationary frames.
   - Draw…

title: Render fidelity data: per-slider ΔE00 against Lightroom Classic (162 renders, Sony ILCE-6400)
author: NgmThanh
body:
I measured how LightCraft's develop sliders respond compared with Lightroom Classic, one slider at a time, as data for the render-fidelity work (`docs/gaps.md` #3, roadmap item 3). No code, just numbers and one board; sharing in case it helps.

## Setup

- **Photos:** 3 Sony ILCE-6400 raws (E 17-70mm F2.8), different scenes and white balances.
- **Variants:** 54 single-setting variants per photo, written as `crs:` XMP sidecars (`crs:ProcessVersion="11.0"`, `WhiteBalance="As Shot"`), plus a reference with no settings. That makes 162 renders on each side. Colour grading uses `crs:SplitToning*` for shadows and highlights hue and saturation, plus `crs:ColorGradeBlending`.
- **Lightroom Classic:** imported the raws with their sidecars and exported sRGB JPEGs with the Adobe Standard profile, 2048 px long edge, default sharpening.
- **LightCraft:** `lightcraft-cli render` of the same raws and sidecars at `d999e382` (2026-10-19), sRGB, 2048 px long edge.
  - The `lc.neutral` profile is the closest to Adobe Standard: ΔE00 5.15 against Lightroom's reference, versus 5.53 for `lc.color`.
  - LightCraft reads every sidecar correctly: each sidecar render is byte-identical to the same values set with `--set` (checked on all variants, colour grading included).
- **Isolating each slider's response:**
  1. For each photo, fit a smooth colour mapping (17³ LUT over a degree-2 polynomial) from LC(reference) to LR(reference).
  2. Apply that mapping to LC(variant).
  3. Measure ΔE00 against LR(variant).

  This removes the baseline look difference, so only the slider's response remains. Verdicts use slightly smoothed images (σ = 2 px), because resampling and sharpening alone leave a 2.7 ΔE00 floor at full resolution. The floor after smoothing is 1.08.
- **Best LightCraft value:** for every variant above 2 ΔE00, a 1-D search (about 15 values within the slider's range) for the LightCraft value that best matches Lightroom.
- **Verdict:**
  - **OK:** ≤ 2 ΔE00.
  - **Scale:** > 2 at the same …

title: Presets: applied preset highlight is lost after switching photos and returning
author: leokunze
body:
## What happens

After applying a preset to a photo, its highlight in the Presets panel disappears when I switch to another photo and then return. The edit is still applied, but I have to open History to find out which preset I used.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open photo A and the Presets panel.
2. Click a preset to apply it to photo A.
3. Switch to photo B.
4. Return to photo A without changing its edits.
5. Look at the Presets panel.

## Actual behavior

The preset used on photo A is no longer marked, although the photo still has that preset's edits.

## Expected behavior

Remember the applied preset for each photo and restore its indication when returning to that photo. Photo B should show its own preset state, rather than inheriting photo A's highlight.

This is distinct from the earlier problem where the last preset stayed highlighted on a different photo that had never received it. Clearing the highlight on photo B makes sense; losing it when returning to photo A makes the panel less useful.

## Source context and related work

In [v0.9.1, panels/presets.rs](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/v0.9.1/crates/ui-egui/src/panels/presets.rs), the panel stores a temporary `AppliedPreset` and discards it when `is_current` fails after a selection change.

Related: #1187 protects Amount from undoing unrelated edits. Open PR #1641 proposes persistent photo-local preset provenance and may provide the underlying state needed here.

The navigation behavior above is a user observation; no automated UI reproduction was run for this report.

title: Crop: golden spiral overlay becomes incomplete at different aspect ratios
author: leokunze
body:
## What happens

The Spiral crop overlay does not remain a complete composition guide when the crop's aspect ratio changes. Depending on the ratio, it becomes a short fragment or appears to disappear.

In Lightroom, the golden-spiral-style guide I use stays complete while adapting to the crop rectangle. I would like the same usable behavior in LightCraft.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open a photo and the Crop & Rotate tool.
2. Select the Spiral overlay.
3. Set the crop to 1:1.
4. Compare the guide with other crop ratios, such as 3:2 and 16:9.

## Actual behavior

At 1:1, the construction reduces to a single quarter-circle rather than a complete spiral. Other ratios produce different numbers and sizes of arcs, so changing the crop shape changes or truncates the guide itself.

## Expected behavior

Keep a complete golden-spiral-style guide visible across supported crop aspect ratios, including square, landscape and portrait crops, with the existing orientation/flip options.

One possible approach is to construct a complete reference guide independently of the crop dimensions and map it into the crop rectangle. Unequal horizontal/vertical scaling would distort the mathematical curve, but would preserve its usefulness as a composition guide. This is a proposed implementation approach, not a claim about Adobe's internal algorithm.

## Source context

In [v0.9.1, panels/crop_overlay.rs](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/v0.9.1/crates/ui-egui/src/panels/crop_overlay.rs), `spiral(w, h)` repeatedly takes `s = cw.min(ch)` from the actual crop rectangle. For a square, the first subtraction leaves one dimension zero, so the next iteration stops. The existing tests check bounds and continuity but do not require a complete spiral across aspect ratios.

The reported problem is the aspect-dependent loss of the guide; the choice between Fibonacci quarter-circle approximations and a logarithmic golden spiral can be decided separately.

title: Web build: report the open document in the viewport title
author: robertcsakany
body:
The web build sends no `ViewportCommand::Title` naming the open document (eframe would log it as `Unhandled egui viewport command: Title(…)` on the web). WordCraft, GridCraft, PhotoCraft and VectorCraft do (`<document>[ •] — <App>`).

An embedding host (pi-agent-dashboard runs the web build in a sandboxed iframe and delivers the document as a synthetic drop) uses that title to confirm WHICH document the app opened and whether it has unsaved changes. Without it the host can only assume the drop worked after a delay; when a drop is refused, the app's default document is mistaken for the file (seen with CADCraft 0.8.0 and a `.dwg`: it showed `Drawing1`).

Ask: send `Title("<file name>[ •] — <App>")` on open, rename and dirty change, like WordCraft.

title: Add native support for Nikon Z5 II Lossless Compressed NEF
author: PR-Builders
body:
### Camera Model
Nikon Z5 II

### Description of the Issue
When attempting to import standard **Lossless Compressed** NEF files from the Nikon Z5 II, LightCraft incorrectly triggers a false-positive error message stating: 
*"Nikon High Efficiency NEF (HE / HE★) uses intoPIX TicoRAW compression. LightCraft does not currently have a license for this codec..."*

The files are **not** shot in High Efficiency (HE/HE★) mode; they are shot using standard Lossless Compression. It appears LightCraft does not yet recognize the "NIKON Z 5 II" metadata string identifier, causing it to fall back to the generic TicoRAW warning instead of parsing the file through the native Rust decoder.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Set a Nikon Z5 II to Photo Shooting Menu > RAW recording > Lossless compression.
2. Capture an image and attempt to import the `.NEF` file into LightCraft.
3. The TicoRAW license error message is displayed, and only the embedded JPEG preview is available.

### Sample Raw File
The sample Lossless Compressed NEF file exceeded GitHub's direct 25MB attachment limit, so I have hosted it via a cloud link for testing and color matrix calibration:
* **Download Link:** https://drive.google.com/file/d/1uQgWkM1WncaJnq85pBC19vxaBWen7d4a/view?usp=sharing
* **Filename:** DSC_0799.NEF

### Expected Behavior
LightCraft should recognize the Nikon Z5 II camera ID string and decode the standard Lossless Compressed raw sensor data normally, matching the behavior of existing EXPEED 7 cameras like the Z8 and Z9.

title: [Feature request][LightCraft] "Show in Folders" option in the photo context menu
author: laucouren
body:
## Summary

Add a **"Show in Folders"** option to the right-click context menu on a photo. It would sit next to the existing **"Show in Explorer"** option and work like the equivalent feature in Lightroom Classic.

## Current behavior

Right-clicking a photo offers **"Show in Explorer"**, which opens the photo's location in the operating system's file manager. Lightcraft has no built-in way to find the folder that holds the selected photo in its own **Folders** panel (left sidebar).

## Proposed behavior

When the user right-clicks a photo and selects **"Show in Folders"**, Lightcraft would:

1. **Highlight** the folder that contains the photo in the Folders panel on the left.
2. **Automatically expand** any collapsed parent folders as needed so the target folder is visible.
3. *(Optional)* **Scroll** the Folders panel so the highlighted folder is in view.

## Use case

This is especially useful when browsing photos from a collection, a search result, a filter or an "All Photos" view, where you can't immediately tell where a photo is stored. It lets users quickly:

- see where a photo is located in their folder hierarchy,
- move to neighboring photos in the same folder,
- reorganize or manage folders without leaving Lightcraft.

## Reference

Lightroom Classic offers this exact feature via right-click → **"Go to Folder in Library"**, and users who switch from Lightroom will expect it.

Thanks for considering this suggestion!

title: Feature Request: Enhance › Super Resolution — AI 2× / 4× upscaling on a local model (Real-ESRGAN x4plus and friends)
author: jegly
body:
## What

Lightroom's **Enhance › Super Resolution** doubles a photo's width and height with a neural upscaler and saves the result as a new DNG next to the original. LightCraft has nothing like it yet. `docs/parity-checklist.md` lists `LR-EDIT-DETAIL-SUPERRES`, `LR-ENH-DIALOG` and `LR-ENH-INPLACE` as not started, and gap 11 in `docs/gaps.md` names Super Resolution as missing. AI Denoise (RawNIND) is the only Enhance feature so far.

An ESRGAN-family upscaler would close most of this gap, and it would give LightCraft an AI sharpening option too.

## Proposed

- **Enhance › Super Resolution** in the Enhance dialog, with **2×** (Lightroom parity) and **4×** output. The result goes to a new file stacked with the original (Lightroom names it `-Enhanced-SR`), so the original and its edits are untouched.
- **Optional AI sharpening at the same size**: run the model, then downsample the result back to the original resolution. This sharpens fine detail without changing pixel dimensions. It's the same approach as PhotoCraft's Edit › Generative Sharpen in storytold/photocraft#8104.
- **Models are downloaded, never bundled.** Use the same opt-in catalog, terms dialog and sha256 pinning that AI Denoise already uses (`crates/denoise-core/src/known.rs`, `licence.rs`, `manifest.rs`). Candidates:
  - **Real-ESRGAN x4plus**: the classic general-photo 4× model (BSD-3-Clause)
  - **Real-ESRGAN General v3** (`realesr-general-x4v3`): tiny and fast, good for previews and low-end machines
  - RealPLKSR 2×/4×, 4x Nomos2 RealPLKSR, Swin2SR Real-World 4×: PhotoCraft#8104's catalog already has pinned ONNX URLs for these, though each licence needs checking before it goes in.
- **Tiled inference with overlap**, reusing `crates/denoise-core/src/tiles.rs`, so a 4× pass on a 40+ MP raw stays inside a few GB of memory. It shows progress and can be cancelled, as a background job like Denoise.
- **Headless**: `lightcraft-cli` and MCP get the same command.

title: Edit Capture Time writes garbage for a capture time it can't fully read, and skips photos without saying so
author: clydecbrown
body:
### Problem

`shift_iso` (`crates/catalog/src/dates.rs:46`) shifts whatever `iso_seconds` (`crates/catalog/src/stacks.rs:290`) can read, and copies the rest of the string into the result without checking it. So a capture time that is only partly readable comes out of Edit Capture Time looking valid, but it's wrong or doesn't read back. Such strings reach the catalog through Lightroom catalog imports, which copy `captureTime` as it is (`crates/engine/src/lightroom_catalog.rs:968`).

- **A time that is cut short loses its hour.** `2026-01-01T10:0` and `2026-01-01T10` are read as midnight (`stacks.rs:298` needs 16 bytes for a time). A one-hour shift writes `2026-01-01T01:00:00`.
- **Unreadable seconds become zero.** `2026-01-01T10:00:xx` reads as `10:00:00` (`num(17, 19).unwrap_or(0)`, `stacks.rs:298`). The shift writes a clean-looking `11:00:00`.
- **Anything after the time is kept as it is.** The tail is copied unchecked (`dates.rs:53`). `2026-01-01T10:00:00+` becomes `…T11:00:00+`, and `2026-01-01T10:00:00 and more` becomes `…T11:00:00 and more`, which isn't a time.
- **Photos it can't shift are skipped without a word.** `photo.setCaptureTime` drops a photo whose time doesn't read (`crates/engine/src/cmd/manage.rs:227-233`). Its result, `{changed, captured}` (`manage.rs:253`), doesn't say how many were skipped.
- **The preview shows the wrong message.** In the dialog's Shift and Time Zone modes, the preview for such a photo says "Enter a date as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS" (`crates/ui-egui/src/panels/dialogs.rs:529`), though the user typed no date.

Follows issue #2146, which fixed a time with minutes but no seconds.

### Proposed fix

- `shift_iso` returns `None` unless the input is one of:
  - a date alone;
  - a date and a time (`T` or a space between them) with hours and minutes, optional seconds with an optional fraction (`.5`), and an optional zone (`Z`, `+02:00`, `-0500`, `+02`), and nothing after. A fraction after the minutes (`10:00.5`, half a minute) is refused t…

title: Lens Correction has some flaws
author: caveflyer
body:
**Lightcraft 0.9.1 standalone on a Win11 i9 machine**

I spent about 2 hours last night trying to get Lens Correction (LC) to work. Here are some of the issues I came across:

- The log file apparently doesn't show anything if the LC finds and loads the XMLs. I would think some indication that it found the XMLs, where it found them, and that they are available would definitely have saved me 30 minutes. There should also be a message generated if the environment variable "LIGHTCRAFT_LENSFUN_DIR" has issues (not found, doesn't contain XML files, etc.)
- Coming from Lightroom, I expected to see a list of LC lenses and could pick one. But apparently your routine is to auto-match Lens Model and Lens Make. The warning message "No lens data embedded in this file" is so very unhelpful if trying to figure out what is wrong.
- The biggest issue, however, was that the Lens Model had to be LETTER-PERFECT or there would be no match. E.g., TAMROM and Tamron would not be a match. At the very least, it should be case insensitive. I can understand why the other elements of the Lens Model are important, but, "TAMRON 28-300mm F/3.5-6.3 Di VC PZD A010" should match with "Tamron 28-300mm f/3.5-6.3 Di VC PZD A010". It took me an hour to trace down why this match wasn't working.  I also seriously feel the Lens Maker should not be used for comparison... many cameras only create a Lens Model field... adding the Len Maker as a required field makes it less likely to be matched
- Finally, when there is a match, there should be a helpful message below the checkbox, perhaps the Lens Model string?

Tangentially related, the lens correction that was actually made was, uh, kind of lame. It shrunk the image a tiny bit and had ragged edges. I'm not sure what I expected -- other than I wanted it to be like LR -- but at least readjust the size of the image so that the ragged edges are gone.

title: Bug: PSD from "Edit in PhotoCraft" sorted by file creation date instead of its EXIF capture date
author: laucouren
body:
## Description

When using **"Edit in PhotoCraft"**, a PSD file is created in the same folder as the original photo, and Lightcraft groups the original and the new PSD in a **stack**.

When the grid view is set to **"Sort By Capture Date"**, this stack (the original photo and the PSD) is sorted as if its capture date were **today**, which is the PSD's file creation date.

The PSD **does contain the correct capture date** in its EXIF metadata, so Lightcraft doesn't seem to read `DateTimeOriginal` from PSD files. It appears to fall back to the file creation date.

## Metadata check

The original JPG and the generated PSD both hold the same `DateTimeOriginal` value:

```
$ exiftool -DateTimeOriginal 20230514.144039.0000.8C75B35AE65AB4390DBF92CF36E81406-000.jpg
Date/Time Original              : 2023:05:14 14:40:39

$ exiftool -DateTimeOriginal 20230514.144039.0000.8C75B35AE65AB4390DBF92CF36E81406-000-Edit.psd
Date/Time Original              : 2023:05:14 14:40:39
```

## Steps to reproduce

1. Select a photo taken on any past date.
2. Right-click → **"Edit in PhotoCraft"**.
3. Save the edit so the PSD is created next to the original.
4. Back in Lightcraft, set the grid view to **"Sort By Capture Date"**.

## Expected behavior

Lightcraft reads the capture date from the PSD's EXIF `DateTimeOriginal` (`2023:05:14 14:40:39` in the example above), so the stack stays in its correct chronological position in the grid.

Lightroom Classic behaves this way.

## Actual behavior

Lightcraft uses the **PSD's file creation date** (today) as its capture date. The whole stack moves away from the other photos from the same shoot.

## Environment

- Lightcraft version: `0.11.00`
- PhotoCraft version: `0.12.0`
- OS: `Windows 11`

title: FreeBSD CI: control_server idle-timeout test fails intermittently
author: helgehelge123
body:
`control_server::tests::persistent_requests_and_slow_replies_outlive_the_idle_read_timeout` fails in the FreeBSD 15 workflow on many PRs since 2026-10-22. It does not fail on every run:

```
thread 'control_server::tests::persistent_requests_and_slow_replies_outlive_the_idle_read_timeout' panicked at apps/lightcraft/src/control_server.rs:319:9:
assertion failed: eof.is_empty()
test result: FAILED. 69 passed; 1 failed
```

**Evidence**

- Each of the last 14 finished FreeBSD runs is on a branch that contains 67d6e187 (Merge PR #1991, idle read timeout plus single-stream `serve_lines`).
- 6 of those runs passed, for example `perf-parallel-walk`, `settings-window-size` and `ui-buttons`.
- 8 failed. 7 of them failed on this test alone: `settings-ask-first`, `settings-legible`, `thumb-overlay`, `drag-drop-contract` and three others. The eighth, `toast-timing`, failed on a different test.
- Earlier runs failed on this test the same way: `people-masks` (run 39724355328), `1278-bmd-dct`, `coolpix-two-field`, `fix/2462-planar-tiff`, `fix/smb-flush-fallback` and `fix/2248-before-flicker`.
- None of the failing PRs touch `apps/lightcraft`.
- So the test looks flaky on the FreeBSD runner, not broken by any one PR.

**Probable cause (not verified on FreeBSD)**

The test gives the connection a 100 ms idle read timeout. After the reply to request 2 arrives, the client has to call `shutdown(Write)` before the server's next read waits 100 ms. If the test thread is not scheduled in time on a loaded VM, the server times out first. It then writes `{"ok":false,"error":"control connection idle read timed out; closing the connection"}`, and that line is what `read_to_string` returns as `eof`.

**Possible fixes**

- Accept that one idle-timeout line in `eof`. Either way the connection was closed correctly.
- Or give the test more margin: for example a 500 ms idle timeout and a 1 s reply delay. The test then still checks that a slow reply outlives the timeout.

title: Control channel / MCP: the `app` parameter of Edit In / Open Original In launches any executable
author: PierrunoYT
body:
**Severity:** High · **Confidence:** Confirmed (code trace) · **Found at:** `31ee2643` · Audit ID LC-01

## Problem
`photo.openOriginalInExternal` and `photo.editInExternal` accept an `app` parameter that selects the program to launch. Any value other than PhotoCraft becomes a program path (or `open -a` on macOS) and is spawned as-is; `check_editor` only validates PhotoCraft, and the `open_path::openable` gate (#2135) checks the *file* handed over, not the *program*.

The control channel (`--control`) has no authentication, and `mcp --connect` exposes the same commands to an agent. Other commands on the same channel can place files with chosen content and make any file a photo's source, so a control-channel or MCP client can get code execution as the user. Details of a working chain are deliberately left out of this public issue.

## Where
- [`crates/ui-egui/src/menus.rs#L2522`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/31ee2643cf208a18cf780b8a63c677e87ab256f7/crates/ui-egui/src/menus.rs#L2522) (and `#L2419` for Edit In): `let editor = p.get("app")…map_or_else(|| app.ui.settings.external_editor.clone(), str::to_string);`

title: Library folder: `catalog.log` and `catalog.lock.owner` are still truncated / written through planted symlinks
author: PierrunoYT
body:
**Severity:** High · **Confidence:** Confirmed (reproduced) · **Found at:** `31ee2643` · Audit ID LC-02

## Problem
Three library-folder file operations follow symlinks:
- `FsStore::truncate` opens with `OpenOptions::write(true)` and calls `set_len` — [`crates/catalog/src/store.rs#L157-L169`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/31ee2643cf208a18cf780b8a63c677e87ab256f7/crates/catalog/src/store.rs#L157-L169). `Journal::open` truncates the log to 0 when its first line isn't a record ([`journal.rs#L440-L443`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/31ee2643cf208a18cf780b8a63c677e87ab256f7/crates/catalog/src/journal.rs#L440-L443)).
- `FsStore::append` — `OpenOptions::create(true).append(true)` ([`store.rs#L140`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/31ee2643cf208a18cf780b8a63c677e87ab256f7/crates/catalog/src/store.rs#L140)).
- The lock owner note — `std::fs::write(dir.join(OWNER), json)` ([`crates/catalog/src/lock.rs#L121`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/31ee2643cf208a18cf780b8a63c677e87ab256f7/crates/catalog/src/lock.rs#L121)), on every acquisition including the `check_library` preflight.

`FsStore::read` (`store.rs#L88`) is also an unbounded `fs::read`, so a link to a device makes open allocate until abort. `write_atomic` is already link-safe (#1502); these paths are not.

## Impact
Opening (or just checking) a library folder that arrived from a share, NAS or symlink-preserving archive can truncate an unrelated user file to 0 bytes or replace it with the lock JSON. Mainly macOS/Linux; reproduced on Windows with a symlink.

## Suggested fix
- `refuse_link(path)` (`symlink_metadata(..).file_type().is_symlink()` → Err) in `append`, `truncate` and `read`; on Unix also `O_NOFOLLOW`.
- Write the owner note through `safe_file::write_atomic_nosync`.
- Refuse to open a library whose `catalog.*` entries aren't regular files; cap `FsStore::read`.

## Regression test

title: Import probe: a tiny GIF or BMP declaring a 1-gigapixel canvas is fully decoded (4.3 GB allocation → abort)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
**Severity:** High · **Confidence:** Confirmed (code trace) · **Found at:** `31ee2643` · Audit ID LC-03

## Problem
`read_header_unguarded` has no header reader for GIF, BMP or JPEG XL, so it falls back to a full decode with `DecodeOptions::fit(64, 64)` — whose `max_pixels` is still the default `1 << 30` ([`crates/codecs/src/lib.rs#L206-L212`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/31ee2643cf208a18cf780b8a63c677e87ab256f7/crates/codecs/src/lib.rs#L206-L212)). The GIF/BMP decoders get no `set_limits` (unlike PNG and WebP), and `check_size` rejects only `> max_pixels` ([`crates/codecs/src/other.rs#L11-L23`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/31ee2643cf208a18cf780b8a63c677e87ab256f7/crates/codecs/src/other.rs#L11-L23)). `DynamicImage::from_decoder` then allocates `w·h·4` up front.

The header fields are unrelated to the file size, so a file of a few dozen bytes passes the import work gate (`engine/src/files.rs#L1096`, which counts file size only).

## Impact
Importing a folder that contains such a file requests ~4.3 GB; a failed allocation aborts the process (`catch_unwind` can't catch it) and unsaved work is lost. Always fatal on wasm32.

## Suggested fix
- Header-only readers for GIF/BMP (and JXL): `GifDecoder::new(..).dimensions()` doesn't decode.
- `d.set_limits(image::Limits { max_alloc: Some(..), .. })` on GIF/BMP.
- A small `max_pixels` on the probe path (the thumbnail path already uses 64 MP, `lib.rs#L260`).

## Regression test
A synthetic GIF header declaring 32768×32768 with no image data: `read_header` must return quickly with a heap peak under 1 MiB.

## Related
Previously reported in #2116 (closed without a fix). See also #2125.

title: Tiled raw decode: tiles may be far larger than the image and every decoded tile is held at once (no aggregate budget)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
**Severity:** High · **Confidence:** Confirmed (code trace) · **Found at:** `31ee2643` · Audit ID LC-04

## Problem
In [`crates/raw/src/tiffraw.rs#L99-L177`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/31ee2643cf208a18cf780b8a63c677e87ab256f7/crates/raw/src/tiffraw.rs#L99-L177), `check_image` checks the *image* size, while each tile is only checked against `MAX_SAMPLES` (2³⁰ samples). Tile dimensions are independent of the image, and the lossless-JPEG branch accepts a frame covering only the visible rows and then does `v.resize(n, 0)` (up to 2 GiB per tile). All tile results are collected into `decoded` before copying, with no total cap; tiles may alias the same bytes, so plausibility checks are cheap to satisfy. Same pattern in `vendor/arw.rs` `read_quad_tiles` (`#L352-L371`) and `read_ycbcr_tiles` (`#L439-L449`).

## Impact
A small DNG passes the header-only import, then the first thumbnail/develop/export requests N × 2 GiB and aborts. On wasm32 one tile is enough.

## Suggested fix
- Reject tiles whose area greatly exceeds the image area; cap the sum of tile areas at a small multiple of `w·h·cpp`.
- Pass `n` (not `max(2n, 65536)`) to `ljpeg::decode`.
- Copy each tile into the output as it's decoded instead of collecting `decoded`.

## Regression test
A synthetic 16×16 DNG with 16384² tiles returns `Err(Limit)` with a heap peak of a few MiB.

## Related
Previously reported in #2117 (closed without a fix). Residual of #1512.

title: Develop settings: sidecar `lc:settings` skips range clamping, so a crop rect/angle can make a full-size export request ~10¹³ pixels
author: PierrunoYT
body:
**Severity:** High · **Confidence:** Confirmed (code trace; size computation reproduced) · **Found at:** `31ee2643` · Audit ID LC-05

## Problem
- A sidecar's `lc:settings` becomes the photo's full settings through `DevelopSettings::from_json`, which is plain `serde_json::from_value` with no `keep_in_range` ([`crates/engine/src/sidecar.rs#L205`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/31ee2643cf208a18cf780b8a63c677e87ab256f7/crates/engine/src/sidecar.rs#L205), [`crates/develop/src/lib.rs#L37-L39`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/31ee2643cf208a18cf780b8a63c677e87ab256f7/crates/develop/src/lib.rs#L37-L39)). Snapshots, log ops and MCP full loads are the same.
- Even `merged()` only clips the crop when the angle is exactly zero ([`develop/src/lib.rs#L73-L76`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/31ee2643cf208a18cf780b8a63c677e87ab256f7/crates/develop/src/lib.rs#L73-L76)), so any non-zero angle keeps an arbitrary rect.
- `native_size` is the crop rect in source pixels, and the export memory check exempts every export not larger than native size ([`crates/engine/src/export.rs#L1778-L1782`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/31ee2643cf208a18cf780b8a63c677e87ab256f7/crates/engine/src/export.rs#L1778-L1782)).

The Camera Raw `crs:` crop mapping is fine (edges clamped to 0..1, angle to ±45).

## Impact
A crop rect far outside 0..1 on a 6000×4000 photo gives a native size of ~2.4·10¹³ px; a full-size export passes the memory check, the GPU falls back to the CPU, and the allocation aborts the app. Previews aren't affected.

## Suggested fix
```diff
  pub fn from_json(v: &Value) -> Result<DevelopSettings, serde_json::Error> {
-     serde_json::from_value(v.clone())
+     let mut s: DevelopSettings = serde_json::from_value(v.clone())?;
+     s.sanitize(); // keep_in_range + list caps + NaN → default for every untrusted load
+     Ok(s)
  }
```
- Clamp the angle to ±45 (non-finite → 0) and clip a turned crop to a bounded box (e.g. `-0.5..1.5`).
…

title: Develop settings: no caps on masks, strokes, brush size, spots, colour-range samples or red-eye entries (full-resolution plane per mask)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
**Severity:** High · **Confidence:** Confirmed (measured) · **Found at:** `31ee2643` · Audit ID LC-06

## Problem
- `masks`, `spots` and `red_eye` are plain `Vec`s with no cap on load ([`crates/develop/src/settings.rs#L135-L137`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/31ee2643cf208a18cf780b8a63c677e87ab256f7/crates/develop/src/settings.rs#L135-L137)); only `detail` is capped. `crs_masks` turns every `crs:` correction into a mask without a limit.
- `pipeline::masks::evaluate` keeps one full w×h plane per visible mask, all at once ([`crates/pipeline/src/masks.rs#L143-L149`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/31ee2643cf208a18cf780b8a63c677e87ab256f7/crates/pipeline/src/masks.rs#L143-L149)); `StageCache` doubles that. `render_weight` ignores masks.
- Brush size is uncapped (`masks.rs#L529`, `cmd/masks.rs#L319`); each dab scans (2r)² and strokes per mask are uncapped.
- Colour-range samples are unbounded on CPU (`masks.rs#L252-L258`) and GPU (`gpu/src/render.rs#L1008-L1012`); red-eye (`redeye.rs#L159-L186`) and spot paths (`spots.rs#L317-L325`) loop over every item per pixel.

Measured at 1 MP (release): 10 masks 42 MiB, 100 → 385 MiB, 300 → 1,148 MiB; one whole-frame brush with 200 points 6.7 s.

## Impact
A sidecar with thousands of small masks, or an agent calling `mask.add` in a loop, makes previews need tens of GB (abort) on every view; huge sample counts can exceed the GPU watchdog, lose the device and disable the GPU for the session. The CPU pipeline has no cancel flag.

## Suggested fix
- Capped deserializers (like `de_detail`) for `masks`, `Mask::components`, `Brush::strokes`, `BrushStroke::points`/`pressure`, `ColorRange::samples`, `red_eye`, `spots`, `Spot::points`, curve points; the same caps in `crs_masks`, `Preset::apply`, `mask.add`.
- Clamp brush size and budget total dab area; skip pixels outside each spot/eye bounding box; count masks in `render_weight`.
- Longer term: fold masks one at a time; a cancel flag for `pipeline::render`.
