title: Lightroom `.lrcat` reader: rows padded to the declared column count, shared cells and per-duplicate cloning amplify a small file to GiB–TiB
author: PierrunoYT
body:
**Severity:** High · **Confidence:** Confirmed (measured) · **Found at:** `31ee2643` · Audit ID LC-07

## Problem
- Every record is padded to the column count declared by the file's own schema (≤ `MAX_COLUMNS = 16_384`): `values.resize(ncols, Value::Null)` ([`crates/engine/src/lightroom_sqlite.rs#L558-L570`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/31ee2643cf208a18cf780b8a63c677e87ab256f7/crates/engine/src/lightroom_sqlite.rs#L558-L570)).
- Cell pointers are only range-checked (`#L302`), so many pointers can share one tiny cell.
- `lightroom_catalog.rs#L64-L76` expands each `Null` into a `BTreeMap` entry.
- `settings: develops.get(&id).cloned()` runs once per `Adobe_images` row (`lightroom_catalog.rs#L605`); duplicate ids are only rejected later by `validate` (`#L252`), which `library.inspectLightroom` doesn't call.
- `decode_xmp_bytes` allows 16 MiB per row (`#L326-L337`) and `xmp_table` keeps every decoded row (`#L99-L133`) with no total budget.

Measured: a 128 KiB file retained 976 MiB; the same constructions scale to tens of GiB per page and TiB overall.

## Impact
Inspecting or importing a received `.lrcat` aborts the app on out-of-memory.

## Suggested fix
- A decoded-value budget per database; sparse rows instead of padding; reject duplicate/overlapping cell offsets on a page.
- Reject duplicate image ids inside the loop (or `develops.remove(&id)`).
- A shared decoded-XMP budget, or decode lazily for photos actually imported.

## Regression test
A page with tens of thousands of pointers to one cell under a 16,384-column schema: `read_table` returns a budget error.

## Related
See #1247 (stream table rows instead of per-table caps).

title: Keywords: a hierarchical keyword thousands of levels deep overflows the stack in `keyword_tree` (crash on every launch)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
**Severity:** High · **Confidence:** Confirmed (reproduced) · **Found at:** `31ee2643` · Audit ID LC-08

## Problem
`keyword_tree`'s inner `build` recurses once per keyword level with no depth limit ([`crates/catalog/src/keywords.rs#L305-L317`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/31ee2643cf208a18cf780b8a63c677e87ab256f7/crates/catalog/src/keywords.rs#L305-L317)), and also clones the growing prefix per level (O(L²), `#L266-L286`). The import path `from_file` only calls `clean()` (`#L49-L55`); `MAX_LEVELS = 64` is enforced only for keyword-list files. Sources: XMP `lr:hierarchicalSubject` / `dc:subject`, IPTC keywords, sidecars and `SetMeta`. The tree is built on the UI thread (`ui-egui/src/lib.rs#L1778`, `panels/keyword_list.rs`); serializing and dropping it recurse too.

Reproduced: 3,000 levels (~6 KB of metadata) overflow a 1 MiB stack (the Windows main thread); 20,000 overflow 8 MiB.

## Impact
One imported photo crashes the app with a stack overflow (an abort, not catchable). The keyword is saved in the catalog, so the crash repeats on every launch.

## Suggested fix
```diff
  pub fn clean(k: &str) -> String {
-     k.split(SEP).map(str::trim).filter(|s| !s.is_empty()).collect::<Vec<_>>().join("|")
+     k.split(SEP).map(str::trim).filter(|s| !s.is_empty()).take(MAX_LEVELS).collect::<Vec<_>>().join("|")
  }
```
Apply the cap in `Op::SetMeta` and `Catalog::repair` (for catalogs that already contain one), and make `build` iterative.

## Regression test
A photo with one 100,000-level keyword: `keyword_tree()` on a thread with a 256 KiB stack returns one root.

title: XMP: nested struct property keys are copied per child, so a ~0.5 MB packet produces ~1.9 GB of keys
author: PierrunoYT
body:
**Severity:** High · **Confidence:** Confirmed (measured) · **Found at:** `31ee2643` · Audit ID LC-09

## Problem
`collect_property` builds `format!("{key}/")` at every struct level and stores a full-length key for every child and attribute ([`crates/meta/src/xmp.rs#L323-L359`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/31ee2643cf208a18cf780b8a63c677e87ab256f7/crates/meta/src/xmp.rs#L323-L359)). `MAX_DEPTH = 64` and `MAX_NODES = 200_000` (`#L151-L152`) count elements only; there is no cap on attributes, name length, total key bytes or input size. Sidecars are read whole without a cap (`engine/src/sidecar.rs#L432,L463,L529`), and `merge_xmp` re-parses the existing sidecar before every write.

Measured: 143 KB → 121 MB of keys; 495 KB → 1.93 GB (2.98 s).

## Impact
Import or the next automatic sidecar write aborts on out-of-memory, and keeps doing so while the sidecar sits next to the photo.

## Suggested fix
`MAX_XMP_BYTES` (e.g. 16 MiB), an attribute-count cap in `parse_tree`, and a key-byte budget threaded through `collect_*` returning `TooComplex` (or cap `struct_prefix` length). Cap sidecar reads in the engine.

## Regression test
Deeply nested `parseType="Resource"` properties with long names and tens of thousands of leaf attributes → `Err(XmpError::TooComplex)`.

## Related
Previously reported in #2120 (closed without a fix).

title: Raw: lossy-JPEG tiles and embedded previews let zune-jpeg allocate from the JPEG header up to 65536² before any size check
author: PierrunoYT
body:
**Severity:** Medium (High on web) · **Confidence:** Confirmed (code trace) · **Found at:** `31ee2643` · Audit ID LC-10

## Problem
`lossy_jpeg` allows up to 65536×65536 ([`crates/raw/src/tiffraw.rs#L232-L245`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/31ee2643cf208a18cf780b8a63c677e87ab256f7/crates/raw/src/tiffraw.rs#L232-L245)); it's used for lossy DNG tiles (`#L182`) and embedded previews in `wb_estimate.rs#L68`. zune-jpeg allocates `w·h·c` right after the headers (~12.9 GB at the limit); `wb_estimate` checks `MAX_PREVIEW_PIXELS` only after decoding. On wasm32, `w·h·3` overflows inside zune and hits its own `unwrap()`. ERF (and MEF without an RGB preview) estimate white balance in header mode, i.e. at import.

## Suggested fix
For tiles, set zune's max width/height to the tile size; for previews, read the JPEG header first and refuse dimensions over `MAX_PREVIEW_PIXELS` or implausible for the byte length.

## Regression test
An embedded preview JPEG whose SOF declares 65535×65535: white-balance estimation returns an error with a small heap peak.

## Related
Previously reported in #2118 (closed without a fix).

title: Raw vendor decoders (ERF, MEF, ORF, ARW) size the sensor buffer from declared strip byte counts, not the bytes present
author: PierrunoYT
body:
**Severity:** Medium · **Confidence:** Confirmed for ERF/MEF/ORF · **Found at:** `31ee2643` · Audit ID LC-11

## Problem
- ERF/MEF: `raw_ifd` compares the *declared* `StripByteCounts` with the expected packed size, then allocates `vec![0u16; n]` with n up to 2³⁰ — in header mode, i.e. at import ([`vendor/erf.rs#L42-L49`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/31ee2643cf208a18cf780b8a63c677e87ab256f7/crates/raw/src/vendor/erf.rs#L42-L49), `#L98-L101`; [`vendor/mef.rs#L40-L47`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/31ee2643cf208a18cf780b8a63c677e87ab256f7/crates/raw/src/vendor/mef.rs#L40-L47), `#L92`).
- ORF 12-bit single strip: same in header mode when the CFAPattern is missing (`vendor/orf.rs#L230-L241`).
- ARW one-byte and packed-12 paths: same on full decode (`vendor/arw.rs#L617-L660`).
- Needs verification: `vendor/srw.rs#L98-L110` and `vendor/mrw.rs#L71-L79`.

## Impact
Each tiny file costs ~2 GiB and seconds of CPU at import; parallel import multiplies it; fatal on wasm32.

## Suggested fix
Check the real slice length (`data.get(off..off + len)`) before allocating, as `raf.rs#L157` and `rw2.rs#L567` already do.

## Related
Previously reported (ERF/MEF) in #2119 (closed without a fix).

title: Codecs: default `max_pixels = 1 << 30` allows ~13 GB working buffers; PNG and JPEG XL budgets are larger still
author: PierrunoYT
body:
**Severity:** Medium · **Confidence:** Confirmed (code trace) · **Found at:** `31ee2643` · Audit ID LC-12

## Problem
- The default cap is 1 Gpx ([`crates/codecs/src/lib.rs#L70`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/31ee2643cf208a18cf780b8a63c677e87ab256f7/crates/codecs/src/lib.rs#L70)), ~40× a 24 MP photo; `Rgb32f` is `w·h·12` bytes (~12.9 GB at the cap). Callers keeping the default include `engine/src/export.rs#L507`, `engine/src/files.rs#L566,L751,L1061`, `mcp/src/tools.rs#L461`.
- PNG sizes its output from IHDR (`png_codec.rs#L118-L119`) with `png::Limits { bytes: max_pixels * 8 }` (~8.6 GB, `#L111`).
- JPEG XL: `Vec::with_capacity(fw * fh * keep)` of f32 (`jxl.rs#L111`), with an `AllocTracker` budget of `max_pixels * 128` (~137 GB, `jxl.rs#L21,L33`).

## Impact
Opening a forged PNG/JXL requests 4–16 GB and aborts on machines without that much free memory (always on wasm32).

## Suggested fix
Lower the default (e.g. 256 MP) and pass smaller caps from probe/thumbnail/preview call sites; size the JXL tracker to `max_pixels * 16`; refuse a PNG on `info.width/height` before `output_buffer_size()`.

## Related
Previously reported in #2125 and #2116 (closed without a fix). JPEG XL part is new.

title: CI: code-signing secrets passed to a reusable workflow at `craft-common-actions@main`; SonarCloud gets `secrets: inherit`
author: PierrunoYT
body:
**Severity:** Medium · **Confidence:** Confirmed (config) · **Found at:** `31ee2643` · Audit ID LC-13

## Problem
- [`.github/workflows/release.yml#L25`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/31ee2643cf208a18cf780b8a63c677e87ab256f7/.github/workflows/release.yml#L25) calls `storytold/craft-common-actions/.github/workflows/release.yml@main` and passes the Apple and Windows signing certificates and the Azure client secret (`#L32-L46`).
- [`.github/workflows/sonarcloud.yml#L19-L20`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/31ee2643cf208a18cf780b8a63c677e87ab256f7/.github/workflows/sonarcloud.yml#L19-L20) calls `…/sonarcloud.yml@main` with `secrets: inherit` on every push to `main`, though it only needs `SONAR_TOKEN`.

## Impact
A commit landing on `craft-common-actions@main` (compromised account or a bad merge there) receives LightCraft's signing keys on the next release, and every repository secret on the next push.

## Suggested fix
```diff
- uses: storytold/craft-common-actions/.github/workflows/release.yml@main
+ uses: storytold/craft-common-actions/.github/workflows/release.yml@<commit SHA>   # bumped by Dependabot
- secrets: inherit
+ secrets:
+   SONAR_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SONAR_TOKEN }}
```
Put the signing secrets in a protected `release` environment with required reviewers.

## Related
Previously reported (release part) in #2126 (closed without a fix; PR #2201 closed unmerged). The SonarCloud part is new.

title: `mask.exportEffects` writes anywhere, including over a catalogued original, without the original guard or an atomic write
author: PierrunoYT
body:
**Severity:** Medium · **Confidence:** Confirmed · **Found at:** `31ee2643` · Audit ID LC-14

## Problem
[`crates/engine/src/cmd/mask_effect_files.rs#L494-L497`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/31ee2643cf208a18cf780b8a63c677e87ab256f7/crates/engine/src/cmd/mask_effect_files.rs#L494-L497) does `create_dir_all(dir)` then `std::fs::write(&path, text)`. Every other exporter (preset, curve, slideshow, print, contact sheet, merge) calls `s.check_write_target(path)` and writes through `export::write_file*`. `keyword.export` has the same problem and is tracked in #1944 (fix PRs #2015 / #1954 open, not merged yet at `31ee2643`).

## Impact
A control/MCP client or a mistyped path overwrites a raw original or its sidecar; a full disk leaves a truncated file.

## Suggested fix
```diff
- std::fs::write(&path, text)?
+ s.check_write_target(&path).map_err(|e| bad("mask.exportEffects", e))?;
+ crate::export::write_file_durable(&path, text.as_bytes()).map_err(EngineError::Other)?;
```
`check_write_target` could also refuse the library's own `catalog.*` and `prefs.json`.

## Regression test
Catalogue `IMG_1.CR3`; `mask.exportEffects` with that path returns Err and the file is unchanged.

## Related
#1944 (same issue for `keyword.export`).

title: prefs.json LUT profile paths are trusted: read unbounded on every library open; Delete Imported Profile's path check is lexical
author: PierrunoYT
body:
**Severity:** Medium · **Confidence:** Confirmed (code trace) · **Found at:** `31ee2643` · Audit ID LC-15

## Problem
- On library open, `register_all` reads every LUT path from `prefs.json` with `std::fs::read_to_string` on the UI thread ([`crates/engine/src/library.rs#L509-L510`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/31ee2643cf208a18cf780b8a63c677e87ab256f7/crates/engine/src/library.rs#L509-L510), [`cmd/lut_profiles.rs#L31`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/31ee2643cf208a18cf780b8a63c677e87ab256f7/crates/engine/src/cmd/lut_profiles.rs#L31)). Any path is accepted.
- `profile.deleteImported` checks `Path::new(&gone.file).starts_with(profiles_dir)` (`#L157`), which doesn't resolve `..`.

## Impact
A shared library's `prefs.json` can point a LUT at a device (unbounded read → abort on every open), a FIFO (UI hangs), or a UNC path (an SMB connection on open, leaking credentials on Windows). A `..` path lets deleting that profile remove a file outside `Profiles/`.

## Suggested fix
Accept `file` only when it's a direct child of `<library>/Profiles` (component compare, no `..`, `symlink_metadata` says regular file); read through `File::take(MAX_CUBE + 1)`; skip with a warning otherwise.

## Regression test
prefs with `Profiles/../outside.cube` and with an oversized file: the library opens and neither LUT registers; delete leaves the outside file alone.

## Related
Previously reported in #2123 (closed without a fix; PR #2186 closed unmerged).

title: Quadratic work on file-derived input: IPTC keyword dedup, XMP unescaping and namespace lookup, catalog repair, keyword/people helpers
author: PierrunoYT
body:
**Severity:** Medium · **Confidence:** Confirmed (measured) · **Found at:** `31ee2643` · Audit ID LC-16

## Problem
| Site | Cost | Measured (release) |
|---|---|---|
| [`crates/meta/src/iptc.rs#L45-L50`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/31ee2643cf208a18cf780b8a63c677e87ab256f7/crates/meta/src/iptc.rs#L45-L50) `!m.keywords.contains(&k)` | O(n²); IPTC in TIFF/DNG IFD0 can be as large as the file, parsed twice by `extract()` | 1.9 MB → 45 s |
| `meta/src/xmp.rs#L205-L224` `unescape_attr` (`rest.find(';')` per `&`); same in `lensdb/src/xml.rs#L54-L72` | O(n²) | 200k `&` → 0.9 s |
| `meta/src/xmp.rs#L159-L173` `canonical` scans every in-scope `xmlns` per name | O(N²) | 1.1 MB → 0.7 s |
| `catalog/src/lib.rs#L1069-L1089` `repair` parent-chain walk per album | O(A²) | 20k folders → 5.2 s |
| `catalog/src/keywords.rs#L51` `from_file`; `model.rs#L486-L495` `Photo::people`; `stacks.rs#L52-L56` `group_ops` | O(n·m) | 8k×8k → 3.1 s |

## Impact
Import and reload workers stall for minutes to hours on crafted files; a crafted snapshot delays library open; every search over an affected photo is slow.

## Suggested fix
`HashSet` dedup (IPTC, `from_file`, `people`, `group_ops`) plus a keyword cap; look for `;` only within the next 12 bytes; a prefix→URI map in `canonical`; memoize `repair` (or cap depth at 64, matching `folders::MAX_DEPTH`); input-size caps on XMP/IPTC.

## Related
`journal::resync` is the same class and is tracked in #2124 (PR #2153).

title: Lightroom `.lrcat` reader: schema parsing is quadratic with token blow-up and no cancel; WAL frames are held twice
author: PierrunoYT
body:
**Severity:** Medium · **Confidence:** Confirmed (code trace) · **Found at:** `31ee2643` · Audit ID LC-17

## Problem
- Duplicate-column check is O(n²) ([`crates/engine/src/lightroom_sqlite.rs#L715`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/31ee2643cf208a18cf780b8a63c677e87ab256f7/crates/engine/src/lightroom_sqlite.rs#L715)) and `MAX_COLUMNS` is checked only afterwards (`#L459`). The tokenizer makes a ~32-byte token per 1-byte `(` or `,` (64 MiB of SQL → ~2 GiB of tokens).
- Root-page dedupe is O(n²) over up to 1M schema rows (`#L462`). None of it checks the cancel flag.
- Every committed WAL frame is copied with `.to_vec()` while the (up to 4 GiB) WAL buffer is still alive (`#L536`), peaking ~8 GiB.

## Suggested fix
Stop as soon as `MAX_COLUMNS` is passed; `HashSet`s; cap SQL length, tokens and schema rows; check cancel; map page id → offset into the WAL buffer instead of copying.

## Related
See #1247.

title: Dependencies: rustls-webpki 0.103.15 and webpki-roots 1.0.9 accept distrusted intermediates; rustls 0.23.45 advisories still open; no audit in CI
author: PierrunoYT
body:
**Severity:** Medium · **Confidence:** Confirmed (`cargo audit`) · **Found at:** `31ee2643` · Audit ID LC-18

## Problem
`cargo audit` at `31ee2643` reports 17 vulnerabilities. Reachability:

| Crate | Advisory | Reachable? |
|---|---|---|
| rustls-webpki 0.103.15 | RUSTSEC-2026-0382 (distrusted intermediates) | **Yes** — every https download (`crates/fetch`). Fixed in ≥ 0.103.16. |
| webpki-roots 1.0.9 | RUSTSEC-2026-0381 (distrusted emSign intermediates) | **Yes** — `fetch/src/http.rs#L225`. Fixed in ≥ 1.0.10. |
| rustls 0.23.45 | RUSTSEC-2026-0346/-0347/-0348/-0349 | Partly (no brotli/ECH with default-features off; -0349 needs verification). Fixed in ≥ 0.23.46. |
| rustls-webpki 0.102.8, rsa 0.9.10 | via `rustls-rustcrypto 0.0.2-alpha` | Likely not (signature glue only; client never RSA-decrypts). Move to a maintained provider. |
| zip 7.2.0 | RUSTSEC-2026-0367/-0368/-0369 | No — `ZipArchive::extract` is never called (via candle-core). |
| quick-xml 0.38.4 | RUSTSEC-2026-0194/-0195 | No — `attributes().with_checks(false)` everywhere, `NsReader` unused. Bump tracked in #1464. |

Model/face/lens downloads are SHA-256-pinned, which limits the TLS impact to unpinned files (GeoNames, SAM 3 tokenizer). There's no `deny.toml`, and neither `cargo audit` nor `cargo deny` runs in CI.

## Suggested fix
`cargo update -p rustls -p rustls-webpki -p webpki-roots`; add `cargo deny check advisories` to `cargo xtask ci` with a `deny.toml` that documents the unreachable advisories.

## Related
Previously reported (rustls part) in #2127 (closed without a fix; PR #2196 closed unmerged). The webpki 0.103.15 / webpki-roots advisories are new.

title: wasm32: CR3 preview box scan adds untrusted u32 lengths without overflow checks, then slices (abort in the web build)
author: PierrunoYT

title: Unbounded reads of command- and folder-supplied files; `metadata().len()` size checks are bypassed by devices and FIFOs
author: PierrunoYT
body:
**Severity:** Low–Medium · **Confidence:** Confirmed (code trace) · **Found at:** `31ee2643` · Audit ID LC-20

## Problem
**Read whole, no limit:** `cmd/curves.rs#L315` (`curve.importPresets`), `cmd/lut_profiles.rs#L49,L58,L81` (`profile.import`), `cmd/manage.rs#L75` (GPX), `export.rs#L506` (watermark/layout images from presets/prefs), `sidecar.rs#L529` and `import.rs#L1083-L1084` (sidecars; `sync.rs` caps at 16 MiB but these don't), `catalog/src/store.rs#L88`.

**`metadata().len()` then `fs::read`** (devices, `/proc` files and FIFOs report 0): `cmd/mask_effect_files.rs#L438-L443` (`read_capped`, also used by preset import), `camera_profiles.rs#L93`, `print_color.rs#L153`, `slide_template.rs#L392,L414`.

**Walk without entry cap:** `mask_effect_files.rs#L410-L423` follows directory symlinks to depth 8 (a few self-links → ~10⁸ entries).

All paths are under `crates/engine/src/` at [`31ee2643`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/tree/31ee2643cf208a18cf780b8a63c677e87ab256f7/crates/engine/src).

## Impact
A command parameter or a file on an imported share pointing at a device or FIFO aborts the app or hangs a worker (or the UI thread, where the read happens there).

## Suggested fix
One helper `read_bounded(path, max)`: require `symlink_metadata` to report a regular file, read through `File::take(max + 1)`, error past `max`. Use it at every site above; use `walk::files_in` in `mask_effect_files`.

## Related
#2176 (MCP file-access roots).

title: Export: the preset `subfolder` keeps `/` and `..`, so exports can land outside the chosen folder
author: PierrunoYT
body:
**Severity:** Low · **Confidence:** Confirmed (code trace) · **Found at:** `31ee2643` · Audit ID LC-21

## Problem
[`crates/engine/src/export.rs#L1105`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/31ee2643cf208a18cf780b8a63c677e87ab256f7/crates/engine/src/export.rs#L1105) sanitizes the subfolder with `replace(['\\', ':', '\0'], "_")`, keeping `/` and `..`, and `join_path(&base, &self.o.subfolder)` (`#L2273`) uses it. A shared export preset with a `..` subfolder writes outside the intended tree (content is images only; originals stay protected).

## Suggested fix
Reject `..` components and absolute subfolders; if nested subfolders are intended, split on `/` and sanitize each component with `rename::sanitize`.

title: Desktop: the panic log defaults to a fixed shared path (`/tmp/lightcraft-panics.log`) opened create+append
author: PierrunoYT
body:
**Severity:** Low · **Confidence:** Confirmed (code trace) · **Found at:** `31ee2643` · Audit ID LC-22

## Problem
Without `LIGHTCRAFT_CONFIG_DIR` (the default), `panic_log_path_with` uses `std::env::temp_dir().join("lightcraft-panics.log")` ([`apps/lightcraft/src/main.rs#L839-L846`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/31ee2643cf208a18cf780b8a63c677e87ab256f7/apps/lightcraft/src/main.rs#L839-L846)), and `engine/src/guard.rs#L38` opens it with `create(true).append(true)`, following symlinks.

## Impact
On Linux/FreeBSD multi-user hosts another user can pre-create the file (reading panic messages that contain paths and file names, where `fs.protected_regular=0`) or plant a symlink so panics append to the victim's files (FreeBSD, or `protected_symlinks=0`). macOS and Windows temp dirs are per-user.

## Suggested fix
Use the per-user state/config dir (or `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`); if temp must stay, a `0700` subdirectory and `O_NOFOLLOW`.

title: MCP: render and screenshot PNGs are written to predictable, world-readable names in the shared temp dir
author: PierrunoYT
body:
**Severity:** Low · **Confidence:** Confirmed (code trace) · **Found at:** `31ee2643` · Audit ID LC-23

## Problem
[`crates/mcp/src/tools.rs#L440-L443`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/31ee2643cf208a18cf780b8a63c677e87ab256f7/crates/mcp/src/tools.rs#L440-L443) uses `temp_dir()/lightcraft-mcp-<pid>-<n>-<tag>.png`. Writes are `create_new` + rename (symlink-safe), but the files are `0644`, so on Linux/FreeBSD other users can read rendered photos and screenshots; pre-creating the names makes renders fail.

## Suggested fix
A per-process `0700` temp directory, or return the PNG inline.

title: Network listeners: per-read timeouts let slow clients hold every slot (denoise-serve, control channel); SAM worker exits on one accept error
author: PierrunoYT
body:
**Severity:** Low · **Confidence:** Confirmed (code trace) · **Found at:** `31ee2643` · Audit ID LC-24

## Problem
- `denoise-serve`: 120 s timeout per read and `read_line` over `take(4097)` accept one byte per read, so a few unauthenticated clients dripping bytes hold all 8 slots ([`crates/denoise/src/remote.rs#L156-L161`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/31ee2643cf208a18cf780b8a63c677e87ab256f7/crates/denoise/src/remote.rs#L156-L161), `#L197-L200`). Clients fall back to local denoise. No back-off after wrong tokens.
- Control channel: 16 slots with a 5-minute per-read timeout (`apps/lightcraft/src/control_server.rs#L24,L67`), so any local process can lock out `mcp --connect`.
- SAM 3 worker: one client at a time, 10-minute timeout, no authentication, and `stream.map_err(..)?` ends `serve()` on a single accept error (`crates/segment/src/remote.rs#L188-L206`).

## Suggested fix
A total deadline per header line and a short pre-authentication deadline; back-off per peer; `continue` on accept errors; a token (or `0600` socket) for the SAM worker.

## Related
Previously reported in #2133 and #2134 (closed without a fix; PR #2191 closed unmerged). The control-channel part is new.

title: Geocoding download: `dataset` and `base` command parameters write server-chosen bytes into any directory; unpinned downloads can be truncated silently
author: PierrunoYT
body:
**Severity:** Low · **Confidence:** Confirmed (code trace) · **Found at:** `31ee2643` · Audit ID LC-25

## Problem
- `metadata.downloadPlaceNames` takes `dataset` (any directory) and `base` (any https server) from command params and writes `cities15000.txt`, `admin1CodesASCII.txt` and `countryInfo.txt` there with `std::fs::write` (follows symlinks) ([`crates/engine/src/cmd/geocode.rs#L22-L24`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/31ee2643cf208a18cf780b8a63c677e87ab256f7/crates/engine/src/cmd/geocode.rs#L22-L24), `#L233-L238`). GeoNames data is unpinned by design (`#L192`).
- SAM 3 tokenizer files have `sha256: None` and accept `http://` mirrors (`crates/segment/src/fetch/mod.rs#L20-L21`).
- `BodyMode::Close` treats a TLS EOF without `close_notify` as end of body, so unpinned files can be truncated unnoticed.

## Suggested fix
Ignore `dataset`/`base` from control and MCP (or confine to the config dir) and write atomically; pin the tokenizer hashes and refuse `http://` for unpinned files; treat a missing `close_notify` as an error.

## Related
The tokenizer part was item 5 of #2140 (closed without a fix).

title: Memory gate: `acquire` / `acquire_urgent` add byte counts without overflow checks
author: PierrunoYT
body:
**Severity:** Low · **Confidence:** Confirmed (code trace) · **Found at:** `31ee2643` · Audit ID LC-27

## Problem
[`crates/engine/src/memory.rs#L133-L145`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/31ee2643cf208a18cf780b8a63c677e87ab256f7/crates/engine/src/memory.rs#L133-L145): `g.0 + bytes > g.1`, `g.0 += bytes`, and `self.lock().0 += bytes`. Callers build weights with saturating math (`export.rs#L1797`, `denoise.rs#L933`), so `bytes` can be `usize::MAX`: a debug build panics while holding the mutex; release wraps, admits the job and leaves the accounting wrong until it ends.

## Suggested fix
`saturating_add` in both places (and `saturating_sub` when a `Permit` drops).

## Regression test
`acquire(usize::MAX)` followed by `acquire(1)` doesn't panic and the second waits.

title: GPU denoise workspace pool: `forget()` notifies without the waiter's mutex, so a waiter can miss the wakeup and block forever
author: PierrunoYT
body:
**Severity:** Low · **Confidence:** Plausible · **Found at:** `31ee2643` · Audit ID LC-28

## Problem
In [`crates/gpu/src/nn.rs#L731-L772`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/31ee2643cf208a18cf780b8a63c677e87ab256f7/crates/gpu/src/nn.rs#L731-L772), `take()` checks `made < WORKSPACES` under the `made` mutex, then waits on `wake` with the `free` mutex and no timeout. `forget()` decrements `made` and calls `notify_one` without taking `free`. If the last in-flight tiles fail (e.g. on device loss) between a waiter's check and its wait, the notification is lost and that denoise thread blocks forever; cancel can't reach it. `give()` is fine (it takes `free`).

## Suggested fix
Take `free` in `forget()` (lock order `free` → `made`), or `wait_timeout` and re-check `broken_reason()`.

title: `engine` and `meta` crate roots still lack the mandated `deny(clippy::unwrap_used, …)` attribute
author: PierrunoYT
body:
**Severity:** Low · **Confidence:** Confirmed · **Found at:** `31ee2643` · Audit ID LC-29

## Problem
CLAUDE.md requires every production crate root to carry `#![deny(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic, clippy::unimplemented, clippy::todo, clippy::unreachable)]`. [`crates/engine/src/lib.rs`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/31ee2643cf208a18cf780b8a63c677e87ab256f7/crates/engine/src/lib.rs) and [`crates/meta/src/lib.rs#L12`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/31ee2643cf208a18cf780b8a63c677e87ab256f7/crates/meta/src/lib.rs#L12) have only `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`. No violation is reachable today (`meta/src/xmp.rs#L267,L302,L303,L305` are infallible stack-pops; `meta/src/container.rs#L58` indexes `ifds[0]`), but regressions in the two crates closest to untrusted input wouldn't be caught.

## Suggested fix
Add the attribute; annotate the infallible `expect`s with `#[allow(clippy::expect_used)]` and a reason; optionally have an xtask check verify both attributes on every production crate root.

## Related
Previously reported in #2137 (closed without a fix).

title: Small robustness findings from the 31ee2643 audit (preview cache limits, tile peak memory, spline NaN, i16 offset, history caps, …)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
**Severity:** Info/Low · **Found at:** `31ee2643` · Audit ID 5.M

Grouped minor items; paths at [`31ee2643`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/tree/31ee2643cf208a18cf780b8a63c677e87ab256f7).

1. **Preview cache decode limits** — `crates/preview/src/disk.rs#L432-L446` uses zune defaults (16384², ~0.8 GB) instead of the thumbnail edge; only reachable through a tampered per-user cache. (Was item 6 of #2140.)
2. **Tiled raws peak at ~2× the image** — `crates/raw/src/tiffraw.rs#L104-L112` keeps all tiles plus the output (4–8 GiB at `MAX_SAMPLES`, impossible on wasm32). Lower the per-target cap (e.g. 2²⁸ on wasm32) and copy tiles as decoded.
3. **Spline NaN** — `crates/color/src/spline.rs#L58-L78,L103-L110`: NaN `x` makes `binary_search` return `Err(n)` → `xs[n]` out of bounds; `to_lut(1)` divides 0/0; `Lut1::eval` does `n - 2`. No reachable caller today.
4. **`i16::MIN.abs()`** — `crates/meta/src/datetime.rs#L34,L138`; `DateTime` is `Deserialize` with public fields. Use `unsigned_abs()`.
5. **Focus backfill** — `crates/meta/src/focus_read.rs#L205` allocates a zeroed buffer as large as the file (up to 1 GiB).
6. **TIFF value budget** — `crates/tiff/src/reader.rs#L47-L50` allows 8 × input + 1 MiB of decoded values.
7. **Rational arrays** — `crates/meta/src/tags.rs#L252-L253` formats them unbounded, unlike `list()` (16).
8. **History/versions** — `crates/catalog/src/model.rs#L252,L254` are unbounded on load; `HISTORY_LIMIT = 200` is enforced only by `Op::PushHistory`, not `SetHistory`, snapshot load or `repair`.
9. **Double copy** — `crates/develop/src/lib.rs#L38` clones the whole `Value` in `from_json`.
10. **Panorama memory** — `crates/merge/src/pano/mod.rs#L262-L312` allocates all tiles in parallel without an estimate (~8 GB at the default 512 MP); the `u16::MAX` label sentinel assumes < 65,535 frames.
11. **Windows test failures** — `engine/src/tests_import.rs#L47` and `mcp/src/headless.rs#L224` build expected paths with `/` and fail on Windows.

title: Round 3 integration plan (440 open PRs)
author: francoisgn
body:
cc @aiongg

Draft for a triage issue, prepared by @francoisgn after rounds 1 (#2470, 43 PRs) and 2 (#2515, 85 PRs). Main = `31ee2643c`. Every open PR (440 at dump time, 2026-10-22) is in exactly one bucket; the row-by-row table is `round3-final.tsv`.

## TL;DR

| Bucket | PRs | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| **3a fast lane** | 45 | Green or CI-less-but-safe, clean or docs-only conflicts, tests present, reviewed diffs. Four tracks with disjoint code files. |
| **3b standard** | 133 | Worth merging; each needs a rebase, a CI re-run, or one integrator look. Grouped by area in merge order. |
| **C decision docket** | 130 | Blocked on one ruling (catalog format, Process V3, unsafe, provenance, licence, dependencies, CI policy) or a product call. |
| **D close** | 38 | Duplicate (keeper named), proven on main (commit or file:line), or unreviewable. |
| **E author action** | 94 | One concrete ask each; nothing for the integrator yet. |

Issues that close with 3a: #1624 #1841 #1899 #1944 #2212 #2275 #2308 #2312 #2460 #2500 #2505. With 3b: 40 more (list below).

Three rulings unblock the most PRs: **catalog format numbering** (5 in 3b + ~12 elsewhere), **Process V3** (17), **camera-colour / provenance** (27).

## 3a — fast lane (45)

Conflicts listed as `mech-conflict` are only in `docs/parity-checklist.md`, `docs/whats-new.md`, `docs/gaps.md`, `ROADMAP.md`, locales, `assets/ATTRIBUTION.md` or `contributors/people.toml`; keep both sides. Tracks share no other file (checked against each PR's changed-file list); within a track the order is the merge order. Suggested `next` tracks: r3-t01..t04, `cargo xtask ci` after each track.

title: AI Remove: local generative Remove for LightCraft, and a proposal for a small hook to a local AI service
author: AndrianLeah
body:
Hi! I've been building **[AI Remove](https://github.com/AndrianLeah/ai-remove-lightcraft)**, an unofficial, MIT-licensed companion app that adds **Generative Remove on local models** to LightCraft. It's at [1.5.0](https://github.com/AndrianLeah/ai-remove-lightcraft/releases/tag/v1.5.0), for Windows, macOS and Linux, on NVIDIA, AMD (ROCm), Intel Arc and Apple GPUs. I'd like to share it, tell you what it relies on in LightCraft, and ask whether a small hook would be welcome.

## What it does today, as an external editor

1. **Opening:** in LightCraft, `Photo › Edit In › Open Original in Other Editor` (#1174) opens the photo in AI Remove's own window.
2. **Selecting:** with SAM 3 (one click, or "Describe": type "people" and every person is selected). It reuses the SAM 3 weights LightCraft already downloaded, so there is nothing extra to download.
3. **Removing:** each removal gets variants from a model chosen for the job:
   - **LaMa:** small things on plain backgrounds.
   - **RORem** (the default): people and objects. In our tests it drew no person or odd object back in 12 removals, where SDXL Inpainting did in 11 of 12.
   - **FLUX Fill:** architecture and large areas.
   - **Qwen-Image:** complex backgrounds.
4. **Reflections in glass,** like Lightroom's Remove Reflections, with DAI. On a statue behind a shop window, it finds the reflection where Lightroom does: correlation 0.98 on the face. A whole photo takes about 6 s on an RX 7800 XT. The reflection's light is subtracted from the raw values, with a 0–150 % strength slider.
5. **The result is a raw DNG.** The fills are re-mosaiced into the sensor data with matching sensor noise, so you keep developing it like the original. It is stacked on the original with the same development.
6. **Every removal stays editable** in a project file next to the photo. JPEG, PNG, TIFF, WebP, HEIC and AVIF work too.

## What it relies on in LightCraft (so these can stay stable)

- **Edit In:**
  - the external editor set in Setting…

title: Lightroom Catalog Import Issues
author: rglohre
body:
I'm testing LightCraft as a potential replacement for Lightroom Classic and ultimately need to migrate a library of approximately 125,000 photos.

I've run into what appears to be an issue with larger Lightroom Classic catalog imports where LightCraft reports the import as complete, but a substantial number of photos are missing.

### Main test

I exported a Lightroom Classic catalog containing:

- 45,091 photos
- `.lrcat` size: approximately 641 MB
- Originals remain in their existing locations on an external SSD

LightCraft completed the Lightroom catalog import without reporting an error.

However, after completion:

- Expected: 45,091 photos
- Imported into LightCraft: 16,521 photos
- Missing: 28,570 photos

Restarting LightCraft did not change the counts.

### Controlled test

I identified one folder within that catalog containing 439 JPEG images.

In Lightroom Classic:

- Original/master catalog: 439 photos
- Exported 641 MB `.lrcat`: 439 photos

title: Import a Lightroom catalog backup (.zip) directly
author: francoisgn
body:
### Use case
Someone leaving Lightroom Classic who has already uninstalled it and deleted the live catalog folder. All they
have left is their photos and the catalog backups Lightroom wrote (`<Catalog folder>/Backups/YYYY-MM-DD HHMM/<name>.zip`,
one `.lrcat` inside, plus a small `.lrcat-data/` since Classic 12). LightCraft should take that zip as it is, with
no manual unzip.

### What happens today (main, 0.11.0, macOS, real catalog of 2,740 photos, backups from 2018 to 2023)
- File ▸ Import Lightroom Catalog… only offers `.lrcat` files; `library.importLightroom path=<backup>.zip` fails
  with `invalid SQLite catalog: "invalid SQLite header signature"`.
- Unzipped by hand, every backup (2018 → 2023 schemas) imports fine: 2,740 photos, 96 albums, same as the live
  catalog.
- `--library` / Open Library on a dated backup folder (`Backups/2023-11-07 0900/`) creates a LightCraft library
  inside it; `lightroom_folder.rs` only recognises `Backups/` itself.

### Proposal
1. Accept `.zip` in `library.importLightroom` / `library.inspectLightroom` and in the file picker (and a dated
   backup folder or `Backups/`, taking the newest backup).
2. Extract the single `*.lrcat` entry by streaming (`miniz_oxide` inflate, already a dependency; ZIP64 needed:
   real catalogs pass 4 GB) into a private temp folder, import from it, then delete it — on success, error and
   cancel alike (a guard), and sweep leftovers (`lc-lrbackup-*`) from a crash on the next import. The zip is only
   read. Not the in-memory preset zip reader (256 MB entry cap, no ZIP64).
3. Temp location: the open library's own folder (`<library>/Interop/lc-lrbackup-<pid>/`), so the space is on the
   library's disk and not on a RAM-backed `/tmp` (tmpfs on many Linux distributions); `std::env::temp_dir()`
   (`$TMPDIR` on macOS/Linux, `%TEMP%` on Windows) when the library isn't on disk. A full disk is an actionable
   error, never a panic, and the partial file is deleted at once. (No free-space check before extracting:…

title: Panasonic DC-S5: no colour model, so white balance stays relative and a Lightroom Custom white balance (Kelvin) is kept as shot
author: DWHowes
body:
### setup

- LightCraft `main` at `b3d392b4`, used as a library (`lightcraft-engine`, `lightcraft-develop`, `lightcraft-pipeline`) on Windows 10.
- Panasonic Lumix DC-S5, RW2, landscape timelapse sequences (up to about 1,200 frames each) edited in Lightroom Classic with LRTimelapse, which writes the edits to XMP sidecars.

### what happens

The DC-S5 isn't in the spectral table (`lightcraft_raw::spectral`, 52 bodies from rawtoaces-data; the DC-GX9 is there, the S5 isn't), has no built-in camera profile (`assets/camera-profiles/`) and no Kelvin presets (`kelvin_presets` covers Sony only). So, as `docs/camera-preview-colour.md` describes, its RW2s get **relative** white balance around the as-shot look, and after #510 a sidecar's `crs:WhiteBalance="Custom"` with `crs:Temperature`/`crs:Tint` is kept as shot rather than applied.

For timelapse this loses the white balance entirely. LRTimelapse keyframes `Temperature` in Kelvin across the sequence (for example 5600 K / +27 at one keyframe, ramping to the next), and every frame renders at its camera white instead.

The colour path itself works once the camera has matrices: a DNG of one S5 frame made by Adobe DNG Converter opens in LightCraft with Kelvin white balance (as shot 3544 K / +16) and the sidecar's Custom white applies. So the S5 only needs LightCraft-owned colour data.

### request

Add the DC-S5 so its white balance is in Kelvin, by whichever route LightCraft accepts:

1. **A pooled profile from `lightcraft-cli calibrate`.** The docs list ARW, NEF and RAF as its inputs; does it take RW2? If it does, would a pooled S5 profile also give Kelvin white balance, or does Kelvin still need measured matrices or presets (the docs say "Kelvin WB is missing for fitted cameras without colour matrices")?
2. **Panasonic's white-balance presets, as for Sony.** Do the S5's RW2 maker notes carry the multipliers of its presets at stated temperatures, the way Sony's `SR2SubIFD` does? If so, the `kelvin_presets` route might cover it…

title: DNG from a Panasonic DC-S5 renders darker and bluer than Lightroom Classic with the same settings
author: DWHowes
body:
### setup

- LightCraft `main` at `b3d392b4`, as a library, on Windows 10.
- Panasonic DC-S5 frames given to LightCraft as DNGs carrying the camera's colour matrices, forward matrices and profile tables (`lightcraft_engine::files::load_bytes`). An Adobe DNG Converter DNG of the same frame reads identically (as shot 3544 K / +16, the same black and white levels within 15 of 65,535).
- Compared with Lightroom Classic's renders of the same frames with the same XMP settings (LRTimelapse's visual previews), 15 frames from five sequences, uncropped, mean CIE76 ΔE and ΔL* over the frame.

### what happens

- **Every frame is darker:** ΔL* from 3 to 10 below Lightroom's, in all five sequences. Exposure and the tone controls agree closely when the same frames are rendered with LightCraft's fallback colour model instead (ΔL* within 3 in four of the five sequences), so the darkening comes with the DNG path.
- **A bluish cast** where Lightroom's render is neutral, plainest in one sequence (sky over a park, mean ΔE 23 to 24). A Custom white balance warmer than as shot moves the picture the right way (warmer), but not as far as Lightroom does.
- Mean ΔE over the 15 frames is 16.0; by sequence 5 to 8 at best and 23 to 24 at worst.

### expected

A DNG carrying a camera's matrices and profile tables renders close to Lightroom Classic's rendering of the same DNG with the same settings, in lightness at least.

title: Per-folder stores with a central index: portable folders and Capture One–style sessions at archive scale
author: Lorenzoeffe
body:
## Context

Split out of #2323, as the triage bot asked there (one ticket per problem): this is the session and database model of its section 1. The concrete steps that can be built on their own have their own issues: #2602, #2604 and #2603 (see *Suggested steps*). I read the source at `c66014e` (2026-10-22). Corrections are welcome wherever I've misread it.

**The goal:** LightCraft keeps its own database and never depends on an external DAM. But each folder carries its own independent store of the edits made in it, and the central database is only an **index that points to those folders**. Other programs (DAMs such as digiKam, other raw developers) are served by standard XMP export. They are never required.

---

## The model

1. **Folder store.** Each folder of photos can hold its own store in a subfolder (for example `.lightcraft/`), containing:
   - one record per photo **that has changes**, holding **only what changed**: develop settings, history, flag, rating, label, keywords, metadata;
   - a small **manifest** that works as the folder's "truth table" for detecting changes and conflicts. For each record it lists the photo's identity (file name, size, content hash, capture time, camera serial and frame number where available), plus the record's date and hash at the last read and the last write;
   - the folder's thumbnails and, optionally, its smart previews.

   The store is the source of truth for that folder. Any readable, documented text format works: JSON, like the catalog journal, or YAML.
2. **Central index.** The library lists registered folders and indexes their photos for browsing, search, filters and smart albums.
   - **The index points to the folders. The folders don't point to the index.**
   - Adding a project folder scans its images and its store, and from then on LightCraft reads and writes that store. With *Include subfolders*, every subfolder with photos is registered and keeps its own store.
   - Registered folders appear in the sidebar ne…

title: Library-relative photo paths and volume identity (portable libraries, reconnected disks)
author: Lorenzoeffe
body:
## Context

Part of #2601 (per-folder stores with a central index), and useful on its own: it makes libraries portable and stops photos going missing when a disk is reconnected under another name. It covers section 1.1 of #2323. Source read at `c66014e` (2026-10-22).

## Today

- A photo's location is `Source::File { path: String }` ([`model.rs`][model]). As far as I can tell, it holds the absolute path recorded at import.
- So photos go missing in these cases:
  - a library is moved together with its photos, for example a per-shoot library in `<shoot>/.lightcraft` copied to another disk or computer;
  - a USB disk comes back under another drive letter on Windows;
  - a disk is mounted at another mount point on Linux or macOS.
- *Find Missing Photos* and *Locate Missing Files* fix it (LRC-LIB-MISSING), but by hand, every time.

## Requests

1. **Relative paths inside the library's folder.** When a photo lies inside the folder that contains the library folder (for `<shoot>/.lightcraft`, that's `<shoot>`), store its path relative to that folder and resolve it when the library opens.
2. **Volume identity for everything else.** Next to the absolute path, record the volume's identity (the volume GUID or serial on Windows, the file-system UUID on Linux, the volume UUID on macOS) and the path relative to the volume's root. When the absolute path is missing but the same volume is mounted somewhere else, resolve the photo there automatically.
3. **Existing libraries keep working.** The absolute path stays as a fallback, and the new fields are filled in when a library is opened or a photo is first read.

## Acceptance

- Copying `<shoot>` (with its `.lightcraft/` library) to another disk or computer: the library opens with no missing photos.
- Unplugging a USB disk and plugging it back in under another drive letter: its photos are available without relinking.
- The same on Linux with a different mount point.

[model]: https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/c66014e/crate…

title: Detect sidecar changes made outside LightCraft and resolve conflicts with a chosen policy
author: Lorenzoeffe
body:
## Context

Part of #2601 (per-folder stores with a central index), and useful on its own: today, whichever program writes a sidecar last wins. It also replaces point 2.3 of #2323. Source read at `c66014e` (2026-10-22).

## Today

- As far as I can tell, saving a sidecar doesn't check whether the file changed on disk since LightCraft last read or wrote it: I couldn't find a modification-time or hash check in [`sidecar.rs`][sidecar].
- With auto-write on, a rating or keyword changed by another program is overwritten at LightCraft's next save of that photo.
- *Read Metadata from File* exists, but it's manual (and, since #934, it never writes the sidecar back).

## Requests

1. **Record a fingerprint.** On every read and write of a sidecar, record its size, modification time and content hash, in the library or in the folder's manifest (see #2601).
2. **Check before writing, and on rescan.** If the file on disk no longer matches its fingerprint, treat it as a conflict instead of overwriting it. That includes a sidecar *older* than LightCraft's record, for example one restored from a backup.
3. **A policy chosen in advance** (Preferences, per library):
   - **Ask** (default);
   - **File wins**: re-read the file, keeping LightCraft's changes to fields the file doesn't have;
   - **Library wins**: overwrite;
   - **Newest wins**.

   Whatever the policy, keep a backup of the version being replaced (for example in `.lightcraft/backup/`, timestamped) and log what was done.
4. **Make conflicts visible:**
   - a badge on the thumbnail;
   - a *Metadata conflict* field for filters and smart albums;
   - a review dialog showing the differences field by field (rating, label, keywords, each develop group), with a choice per photo or for all.

   Lightroom Classic has a similar mechanism: it marks such photos and lets you choose which side wins.

## Acceptance

- Change a rating in another program while LightCraft is open, then edit the same photo in LightCraft:
  - with **Ask**, …

title: Sidecar location (none / next to originals / subfolder) and sparse sidecars
author: Lorenzoeffe
body:
## Context

Part of #2601 (per-folder stores with a central index), and useful on its own: it keeps photo folders clean and leaves files written by other programs untouched. It covers sections 2.1, 2.2 and 2.4 of #2323 (2.3, conflicts, is #2603). Related: #92, which made saving merge into sidecars other programs wrote. Source read at `c66014e` (2026-10-22).

## Today

- The sidecar preferences are `auto_write` and `naming` (stem or full) (`XmpPrefs` in [`sidecar.rs`][sidecar]). Sidecars always sit next to the original.
- `lc:settings` holds the complete `DevelopSettings` as JSON. LightCraft's own properties are replaced on every save, and removed when LightCraft has no value ([xmp-interop.md][xmp]).
- With stem naming, LightCraft writes into the same `IMG.xmp` files that other programs wrote. The merge keeps their data byte for byte, but the files still change: their provenance is altered, and incremental backups copy them again.
- With RAW+JPEG, one shot can get two sidecars next to its two originals (issue #1905 rule).

## Requests (all opt-in, defaults unchanged)

1. **Sidecar location:**
   - library only (no sidecars);
   - next to the original (today);
   - in a subfolder of the photo's folder (for example `.lightcraft/xmp/`, with the hidden attribute set on Windows), next to that folder's thumbnails when they're kept per folder.
2. **Sparse sidecars:**
   - write a sidecar only for photos that have changes;
   - in `lc:settings`, store only the fields that differ from the defaults of the photo's process version. The process version is recorded, so the defaults can always be reproduced;

title: Re-importing a moved or backed-up Lightroom catalog adds every collection again
author: francoisgn
body:
### Problem
Collections from a Lightroom Classic import are matched on later imports by `<.lrcat path>:<id_local>` (`Interop/lightroom-index.json`). The same catalog imported again from another path — moved, renamed, copied to another disk, or one of its backups — adds every collection a second time.

Seen on main (0.11.0, macOS) with a real catalog of 2,740 photos and 96 collections: import the live `.lrcat`, then the same catalog unzipped from its backup into the same library → 192 albums. Photos don't duplicate (they are matched by Lightroom's image id and path).

### Fix
The catalog's `Adobe_storeProviderID` (in `Adobe_variablesTable`) is the same in the catalog and in all its backups (checked on backups from Lightroom 7 in 2018 to Classic 13 in 2023, across catalog upgrades). Keying collections on it instead of the file path makes the match stable; the old path keys in existing `lightroom-index.json` files must still be read so libraries imported by earlier releases keep matching.

Split out of #2592 (as ticket-craft suggested). Fixed in #2599, which needs it for backups.

title: Feature request: import a library from the cloud-based Lightroom (Lightroom CC / Desktop), not just Lightroom Classic
author: gstangl
body:
## Problem

LightCraft can import a Lightroom Classic catalog (`.lrcat`, "Import Lightroom Catalog"). It cannot import a library from the current, cloud-based Lightroom (formerly Lightroom CC, now just "Lightroom" or "Lightroom Desktop"). That app does not use an `.lrcat` file, so anyone who works in it has no way to move their library into LightCraft. Albums, ratings, flags, keywords and edits would all have to be rebuilt by hand.

## Desired result

LightCraft offers an import for a Lightroom (cloud) library, next to the existing Lightroom Classic import. After the import, the user finds their photos in LightCraft with the albums, metadata and, where the controls map, the edits they had in Lightroom.

## Observed on one Mac (Lightroom Desktop, macOS)

These are observations from one installation, not a documented format:

- The library lives at `~/Pictures/Lightroom Library.lrlibrary/<catalog-id>/`.
- The catalog is `Managed Catalog.mcat`, a SQLite 3 database (WAL mode). Its tables are `docs`, `labels`, `localDocs`, `revs`, `schemaVersion`.
- Next to it are `originals/`, `previews/`, `proxies/`, `cr_settings/`, `cr_defaults/`, `cr_cameraprofiles/` and `people/`.
- On this machine `originals/` is empty: Lightroom keeps the originals in the cloud only and stores just previews locally. An import can therefore not rely on local originals alone.

## Scope

1. Detect and open a local `Lightroom Library.lrlibrary`.
2. Import photos, albums (including album folders), ratings, flags, keywords, captions and capture metadata.
3. Import develop settings as editable LightCraft adjustments where they map to its controls, as the Classic import already does.
4. When originals are cloud-only: either download them (for example via Adobe's Lightroom API, with the user signing in) or tell the user clearly which photos are missing locally and how to get them (for example by setting Lightroom to "Store a copy of all originals locally").

title: Lightroom catalog import: show Lightroom's previews for photos whose originals are offline
author: francoisgn
body:
### User story
As a photographer moving from Lightroom Classic, I import my live catalog into LightCraft. My originals are on a NAS that is slow, or offline right now. I want to see my photos straight away, as Lightroom showed them, so I can check that the import brought the right ones and start culling (ratings, picks, keywords) before the originals are reachable.

### What happens today (main, 0.11.0, macOS)
A real catalog (2,740 photos, originals on an unmounted volume) imports fine, but the grid and the loupe show "This photo can't be opened" and an empty thumbnail for every photo. The rendered previews Lightroom keeps next to the catalog (`<name> Previews.lrdata`) are ignored.

### Proposal
Part of one transparent step for the user: they import their catalog as today, and the import also brings over what it finds next to it: previews (this issue) and Smart Previews (#2614, handled independently). Nothing new to choose for previews.

title: Lightroom catalog import: reuse Lightroom's Smart Previews, build new ones, or none
author: francoisgn
body:
### User story
As a photographer whose originals live on a NAS that is sometimes slow and sometimes offline, I used Lightroom's Smart Previews to keep editing anyway. When I import my live catalog into LightCraft, I want to keep that: reuse the Smart Previews Lightroom already built, or have LightCraft build its own, or skip them — my choice, since they speed up some workflows but are never required.

### What happens today (main, 0.11.0)
Catalog import ignores `<name> Smart Previews.lrdata`. A photo whose original is offline can't be edited until Build Smart Previews runs with the original online, which is exactly when the NAS isn't there.

### Proposal
Part of the same transparent catalog import as #2613 (previews for display), handled independently.

title: Consistent exposure baseline for DR100 / DR200 / DR400 and D-Range Priority
author: Lorenzoeffe
body:
## Context

Narrowed to one problem, as the triage bot asked. The other parts of the first version are already covered elsewhere:
- reading and showing the film simulation and DR settings: #1203, being implemented in #1209 (I've asked there for the D-Range Priority tags too);
- profiles per film simulation and the starting look: #380 (measured X-T4 looks in #2445).

This is section 5.2 of #2323. Source read at `c66014e` (2026-10-22).

## The problem

DR200 and DR400 expose the sensor about one and two stops lower, and the camera lifts the JPEG with its tone curve to compensate. D-Range Priority (Weak / Strong / Auto, already on the X-H1) works in a similar way. The settings are recorded in the maker note as `DynamicRangeSetting` (`0x1402`), `DevelopmentDynamicRange` (`0x1403`) and `DRangePriority` / `DRangePriorityAuto` / `DRangePriorityFixed` (`0x1443`–`0x1445`), and in the RAF header as `RawExposureBias` (`0x9650`) ([ExifTool][exiftool]). A darktable community Lua script reads `RawExposureBias` and lists −0.72, −1.72 and −2.72 EV for DR100, DR200 and DR400 ([darktable docs][dt-dr]).

[camera-preview-colour.md][colour] already handles the Sony equivalent: it reads the DRO setting (`0xb025`) so that the JPEG's tone operator doesn't leak into the raw's starting look, and notes that "Fujifilm D-Range settings are likely to have the same effect and are not handled yet".

The measurements in #380 found the same effect from the other side: through a fixed look, X-T4 DR200 frames came out a stop dark, and matched as well as DR100 frames once scaled by the raw's dynamic range over 100. Today the per-file fit absorbs this, so it only shows once a profile is fixed.

## Request

Handle these settings like DRO. One difference: DR200/DR400 are a global exposure offset chosen to protect highlights, not a local operator. So the right fix is probably a baseline exposure from the DR setting (DR/100, or `RawExposureBias`) with highlight roll-off, rather than a lowered curve. For D-R…

title: Find Missing Photos can't match the files of a library made on Windows when run on macOS or Linux
author: clydecbrown
body:
### Problem

A library made on Windows records its originals with Windows paths (`C:\Users\me\Photos\a.jpg`). Opened on macOS or Linux, its photos are missing until relinked, and **Find Missing Photos** (`library.findMissing`) is the way to relink them in bulk. Photos imported by LightCraft itself are found by their content (they have a size and a content hash on record). But photos with no hash on record, such as those imported from a Lightroom catalog, can only be found by file name, and none of them are found, even when the searched folder holds every file under the same name: the result is `{"found": [], "missing": 1}`.

`plan_find_missing` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/missing.rs:215`) takes a missing photo's file name with `Path::new(&c.path).file_name()` (`:242`). On macOS and Linux `\` isn't a separator, so the "file name" of `C:\Users\me\Photos\a.jpg` is the whole path, and it never equals `a.jpg`.

The other direction works: on Windows, `/` is a separator too, so a library from a Mac relinks fine.

To reproduce:
1. On Windows, import a Lightroom catalog whose originals are on that computer.

title: view.maskOverlayColor accepts "#+f+f+f" as a colour (parse_rgb misses 80e439f6's hex-digit check)
author: clydecbrown
body:
### Problem

`80e439f6` ("Reject signed hex digits in #rrggbb colour parsing") made `crates/color`, the slideshow's `fadeColor` and the slide settings' `parse_color` require six hex digits. One more parser has the same pattern: `parse_rgb` in `crates/ui-egui/src/menus.rs:340-347`, used by `view.maskOverlayColor` (`menus.rs:1081`). It checks only `h.len() != 6`, then parses each pair with `u8::from_str_radix`, which accepts a leading `+`. So:
- `view.maskOverlayColor {"color": "#+f+f+f"}` sets the overlay to `[15, 15, 15]`;
- `{"color": "+12345"}` sets it to `[1, 35, 69]`;

when both should be refused with the command's `"#rrggbb" or [r, g, b]` error.

No crash: non-ASCII input already fails at `h.get(i..i + 2)`, and a `-` is invalid for `u8`. The bad input becomes a wrong colour.

### Proposed fix

Add the same check as `80e439f6`: `if h.len() != 6 || !h.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_hexdigit())`.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC-1: `view.maskOverlayColor` with `color` set to `"#+f+f+f"`, `"+12345"`, `"#-0-0-0"` or `"##ffffff"` returns an error, and the overlay colour stays as it was.
- [ ] AC-2: `"#2870f0"`, `"2870f0"` and `[r, g, b]` still set the colour; with no params the command still cycles the swatches.
- [ ] AC-3: The new test cases fail on `main` before the change.

title: Detail view: zoom above 100% blurs pixels (linear magnification) instead of showing them
author: radialmonster
body:
Above 100% in detail view, LightCraft smooths the photo instead of showing its pixels, so zoomed-in views look softer than the file is and it's hard to judge focus or sharpening.

**What happens**
The rendered photo is uploaded as a texture with `egui::TextureOptions::LINEAR` (`crates/ui-egui/src/render.rs:914` and `:924` on main). When the view magnifies it (200 %, 400 %, 800 %), the GPU blends neighbouring pixels bilinearly, so each source pixel turns into a soft gradient. On a 24 MP D5600 NEF at 800 %, white aircraft lettering on grey shows blurred edges and blurred rivet dots. Lightroom Classic at 613 % shows the same file as hard pixel blocks (stair-stepped diagonals), so you can see exactly what the raw holds.

The underlying pixels are the same; only the on-screen magnification differs. It matters most for checking focus, sharpening (#757) and noise, which is the main reason to zoom past 100 %.

**Fix**
Magnify with nearest-neighbour whenever a texture holds the photo's own pixels one to one, at every zoom above 100 %, and keep linear everywhere else.

What to build:
- **Choose the filter per texture, from what the texture holds.** When `render.rs` uploads a render (`:914` and `:924` today, both `TextureOptions::LINEAR`), it uses
  ```rust
  egui::TextureOptions { magnification: egui::TextureFilter::Nearest, ..egui::TextureOptions::LINEAR }
  ```
  for a texture whose texels are output pixels of the photo at 100 %. Every other texture keeps `LINEAR`.
  - `Slot::Region` and `Slot::RegionBefore` always qualify. Above 100 % the window is rendered at 100 % and the GPU magnifies it.
  - `Slot::Main` and `Slot::Before` qualify only when the whole-frame render is at the photo's full output size (a small file, or a large texture limit). The render job knows its output size, so the result carries a flag for this, and `render.rs` doesn't need to guess from the texture size.
  - Stand-ins (`Preview`, `ThumbQuick`, `Thumb`, an embedded JPEG preview, a whole-frame render …

title: Nikon D5600: no colour model, so colour is uncalibrated and white balance stays relative (6500 K / 0)
author: radialmonster
body:
The Nikon D5600 has no colour model in LightCraft, so its NEFs render through the generic fallback and their white balance stays relative (shown as 6500 K / 0 = as shot).

**What happens** (main and 0.13.0)
- The D5600 isn't in the spectral table (the D5100 and D5300 are) and has no built-in profile in `assets/camera-profiles/` (`NIKON_D5300.json` is the closest).
- `rawinfo` on a D5600 NEF: `wb [2.098, 1.0, 1.371]` (the camera's as-shot multipliers are read correctly), `matrix_is_fallback true`.
- The catalog stores `as_shot_wb = (6500, 0)`: the relative-scale placeholder, not a Kelvin reading. Lightroom shows As Shot 5500 K / +4 for the same file.
- Colour is close to the camera's own JPEG but not calibrated. On one daylight frame (grey aircraft, white lettering), mean ΔE about 2.3 against the in-camera JPEG, with chroma 7.8 vs 9.1 (slightly desaturated).

**Why it matters**
D5600 owners get uncalibrated colour, and the WB panel can't show or take a Kelvin value, so a Lightroom XMP with a Custom Kelvin white balance won't carry over. Nikon isn't covered by the Kelvin work in #730 / #2527.

**Route**
A LightCraft-owned D5600 colour model, the same way the D5300 got one. Colour-chart shots and varied RAW+JPEG pairs from a D5600 are being requested from the owner who reported this. The D3400, D3500, D7500 and other bodies sharing this sensor generation are worth checking for the same gap.

Part of the softness and colour report that also produced #757 / #762 and #2643 / #2645.

title: Detail view: zoom stops at 800 %; allow 1600 %
author: radialmonster
body:
Detail view zoom stops at 800 %. Going to 1600 % helps when checking single pixels: demosaic artefacts, hot pixels, sharpening haloes.

## Where the 800 % limit is
- `CLICK_ZOOMS` in `crates/ui-egui/src/state.rs` ends at 800.
- The Zoom In steps in `menus.rs` end at 800, and `unwrap_or(800.0)` caps there.
- The pinch zoom clamp in `panels/detail.rs` is 800.
- `view.navigate` in `menus.rs` rejects any zoom percent over 800.
- Docs: `docs/control-protocol.md` and `docs/parity-checklist.md` (LR-VIEW-ZOOM row) say 800.

## Proposal
Add one constant, `MAX_ZOOM = 1600`, and use it for Zoom In, the wheel and pinch limits, and the `view.navigate` check. Add 1600 as the last Zoom In step. Going past 800 % costs nothing more, because the visible window is rendered at 100 % and the GPU magnifies it.

Related: #2643 (zooming past 100 % should show pixels, not a bilinear blur). That is a separate fix, but 1600 % is mostly useful once it lands.

title: lightcraft-cli commands: list commands sorted by id
author: clydecbrown
body:
`lightcraft-cli commands` prints the command registry in the order it was registered: `command_specs()`
(`crates/engine/src/cmd/mod.rs:140`) puts the modules one after another in a hand-written order, each module adds its
commands in source order, and the headless backend appends `app.export` last (`crates/mcp/src/headless.rs:132`).
The CLI prints that order unchanged (`apps/lightcraft-cli/src/main.rs:936`). So the list starts `edit.undo`,
`edit.redo`, `library.source`, `library.filter`, `library.folders`, …. To find a command, or to see what a family
such as `photo.*` offers, you have to search the whole output. And the text output takes two lines per command, so
piping it to `sort` mixes the lines up.

Proposal: `lightcraft-cli commands` lists commands sorted by id, so each family's commands sit together
alphabetically. Only the CLI's output changes. The engine's registry order stays as it is for MCP, the UI and the
control channel.

`lightcraft-cli controls` is not part of this: it lists the develop controls in Develop panel order (`CONTROLS`, "in
panel order"), which is useful as it is.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC-1: `lightcraft-cli commands` prints the commands in ascending order of id (byte order), each with its label,
  shortcut and params line as now.
- [ ] AC-2: `lightcraft-cli commands --json` returns the same array sorted the same way, with the same fields per
  command.
- [ ] AC-3: every command listed before is still listed, `app.export` included (the existing
  `commands_subcommand_lists_registry` test stays green).
- [ ] AC-4: the order of `engine.commands` over MCP and the control channel, and of `lightcraft-cli controls`, does
  not change.

title: Choose what opens at launch: the last library or a list of recent libraries
author: francoisgn
body:
**User story**
As a photographer with several libraries (one per theme: shoots, travel…), I want to choose at launch which library opens, so that I don't open the wrong one and switch afterwards.

**Today (main `23e181283`)**
LightCraft opens `--library`, else `LIGHTCRAFT_LIBRARY`, else the last library opened, else the default location (`apps/lightcraft/src/main.rs`). Recent libraries are only in File ▸ Open Recent Library (last 8, Clear All). A chooser window appears only when the library fails to open (`panels/library_problem.rs`).

**Proposal** (Lightroom Classic offers the same choice in its General preferences)
1. Settings → General → "At launch": *Open the last library* (default, today's behaviour) / *Ask me*.
2. With *Ask me*: a window listing the recent libraries (name, path, last opened; missing ones greyed out), plus Open Another… / New Library… / Quit. Holding a modifier key at launch (e.g. Alt/Option) shows it once even with *Open the last library*.
3. Recent list: remove a single entry (from File ▸ Open Recent Library and from the launch window). This only forgets the path; nothing is deleted on disk.

**Out of scope**: deleting a library folder from disk; backing up a library before removing it from the list (could be a follow-up).

**Acceptance**: the setting persists; `--library` and `LIGHTCRAFT_LIBRARY` still win over it; the window works by keyboard; a missing or locked library in the list shows why and can't be opened; tests for each.

title: Lightroom XMP sidecars: a straightened crop comes in turned the wrong way (crs:CropAngle taken as is)
author: ingolfteetz
body:
Lightroom Classic and LightCraft measure the straighten angle in opposite directions. The catalog import handles this. `catalog_crop` in `crates/engine/src/lightroom_catalog.rs` negates `CropAngle` (except under a mirroring orientation) and maps the crop's corners through the orientation and the rotation. `straightened_catalog_crops_match_lightroom_exports` checks the result against Lightroom's own exports.

The XMP path doesn't do either. `crs::to_partial` (`crates/engine/src/crs.rs`, the `crs:HasCrop` branch) takes `crs:CropAngle` as it is and uses `CropLeft/Top/Right/Bottom` directly as LightCraft's rectangle. It's used for XMP sidecars on import (that's the case I checked) and, as far as I can see, for anything else that goes through `crs::to_partial`. So every straightened photo whose settings come from a sidecar is turned the wrong way, by twice the angle Lightroom fixed, and its crop rectangle is off once the angle isn't 0.

**Example (Leica M11-P DNG, sidecar written by Lightroom Classic):**

```
crs:CropTop="0" crs:CropLeft="0.025221" crs:CropBottom="1" crs:CropRight="0.974779" crs:CropAngle="1.38"
```

- Importing the DNG with that sidecar gives `crop.geometry = {"angle": 1.38, "rect": {"x0": 0.025221, …}}`.
- The catalog import of the same photo gives −1.38° and a rectangle mapped through the rotation.

I checked the direction on another photo that has `CropAngle = 6.06` in Lightroom: rendered with crop angle −6.06 its posts are plumb, and with +6.06 they lean twice as much.

**Suggested fix:** let the XMP path use the same conversion as the catalog, `catalog_crop` with the photo's orientation and stored aspect, so both imports give the same crop. A round-trip test like `straightened_catalog_crops_round_trip` for the XMP path would hold it.

Happy to open a PR for it if that sounds right.
