title: Launch library list (#1290): a re-check started while the list is open does not update its rows
author: francoisgn
body:
A follow-up to #2701 (#1290, choosing the library at launch), found by CodeRabbit and FredApps (review of #2689). Fixed in #2701, part of the integration batch #2689.

### A re-check started while the launch list is open doesn't update its rows
`crates/ui-egui/src/panels/library_problem.rs`: `apply_answers` only updates rows whose `checking` flag is set, and `start_checks` never sets it again. A recent library re-checked while the launch list is up (one not found, every 30 s; the others when the window comes back to the front) gets its new answer in `RecentChecks`, but its row keeps the old one: a drive plugged back in stays "not found" in the list (File ▸ Open Recent Library is right).

**Fix:** when `start_checks` starts a check for a path, set `checking` again on the launch-list row for that path (if the list is up). **Test:** launch list up, a library answered "not found", then the check answers "found": the row becomes openable.

Blast radius: `library_problem.rs` and its tests only.

title: Launch library list (#1290): files waiting for a library are dropped when their import cannot start
author: francoisgn
body:
A follow-up to #2701 (#1290, choosing the library at launch), split out of #2774. Rare and older than the last rounds of #2701, so it gets a small PR of its own once #2689 has landed.

### Files waiting for a library are dropped if their import can't start
Same file, the three places that hand `pending_import` to `import::start_paths` (a library opened from the window, one opened another way, Continue Without Saving): the queue is taken first, and when `start_paths` refuses (an import or a Synchronize Folder is running) the error is only logged, so the files given on the command line or dropped on the window are not imported and not kept.

**Fix:** one helper that takes the queue only once `start_paths` accepted it, and otherwise keeps it and says why in a toast; the three call sites use it. **Test:** queue a file, make `start_paths` refuse (a running import), open a library: the file is still queued and a toast says why; once the import ends it goes in.

Blast radius: `library_problem.rs` and its tests only.

title: Optimize GPU preview rendering and memory usage while preserving cross-platform compatibility
author: draco892
body:
## Goal

Improve rendering responsiveness and memory efficiency on Apple Silicon while preserving compatibility with Windows, Linux, and WebAssembly. Prioritize changes that also benefit Vulkan and DX12.

## Current behavior

The GPU develop pipeline already accelerates most editing stages and caches intermediate results. However, each rendered preview is copied into a staging buffer, read back into CPU memory, converted into an egui image, and uploaded to the UI as a GPU texture.

This introduces allocations, memory traffic, and synchronization even on Apple Silicon’s unified memory architecture. Histograms are also computed on the CPU after readback, and some editing operations require intermediate GPU-to-CPU transfers.

## Planned work

- Establish baseline measurements for interactive latency, GPU readback time, allocations, and peak memory usage.
- Share the rendering device with egui and keep supported previews on the GPU through presentation.
- Compute histograms and result-validation diagnostics on the GPU, returning only small summaries to the CPU.
- Reduce intermediate CPU transfers by adding GPU implementations for remaining operations where measurements justify the work.
- Coordinate memory budgets across caches, rendering work, textures, and AI workloads, with platform-specific memory-pressure handling behind a common interface.

Subsequent work will evaluate tiled rendering for large images, selective reduced-precision intermediates, and directly mappable buffers on suitable unified-memory devices. These optimizations will require separate performance and correctness validation.

## Compatibility requirements

- Keep `wgpu` as the shared GPU abstraction for Metal, Vulkan, and DX12.
- Enable optional GPU features only after checking adapter capabilities.
- Preserve the CPU reference implementation and existing fallback behavior.
- Preserve CPU-readable results for exports, screenshots, headless rendering, and other consumers.
- Keep WebAssembly builds w…

title: Compute preview histograms and result-validation reductions on the GPU
author: draco892
body:
The GPU develop pipeline currently reads the rendered image back into CPU memory to calculate its histogram and detect unwritten pixels or entirely black results.

These full-image CPU passes add memory traffic and synchronization, and must be addressed to support GPU-resident preview presentation.

## Proposed change

Implement GPU reductions that produce histogram bins and compact result-validation summaries. Read back those summaries instead of the complete image when CPU pixels are otherwise unnecessary.

Preserve the existing behavior for incomplete GPU work, device failures, and entirely black results requiring CPU verification.

## Scope and related issues

- Split from the broader optimization proposal in [#2782](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/issues/2782).
- Supports [#1228](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/issues/1228), which already identifies histogram handling as a requirement for GPU-resident previews. This ticket tracks that implementation separately.
- Device sharing and native-texture presentation remain in #1228.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Histogram bins and totals match the CPU reference, including cropped zoom-window output.
- [ ] Diagnostics detect unwritten pixels and preserve the existing entirely-black-result verification behavior.
- [ ] Supported histogram and diagnostic calculations require only compact readbacks.
- [ ] Tests cover normal, black, partially unwritten, and failed GPU results.
- [ ] GPU overhead, readback volume, and CPU time are measured before and after.
- [ ] Metal, Vulkan, and DX12 retain compatible paths; optional capabilities are checked before use.
- [ ] CPU fallback, exports, screenshots, headless rendering, and WASM remain functional.
- [ ] Existing CPU/GPU equivalence checks and `cargo xtask ci` pass.

title: Implement GPU defringe to eliminate its intermediate CPU round trip
author: draco892
body:
## Problem

Defringe currently requires an intermediate image to be downloaded from the GPU, processed on the CPU, and uploaded again before GPU rendering continues.

This transfer interrupts the GPU pipeline and adds memory traffic and synchronization whenever defringe is enabled.

## Proposed change

Implement defringe as a `wgpu` compute operation, preserving the CPU implementation as the reference and fallback.

Match the current algorithm, parameter interpretation, and placement within the develop pipeline. Reuse intermediate buffers where practical and include retained resources in memory accounting.

## Scope and related issues

- Split from [#2782](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/issues/2782), specifically its proposal to reduce intermediate CPU transfers.
- Related to [#1145](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/issues/1145), which addresses repeated mask evaluation and mask-cache accounting. Those changes remain outside this ticket.
- Complements GPU-resident presentation in [#1228](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/issues/1228), but can be implemented independently.
- Spot removal and other CPU-only operations are outside this ticket.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Supported defringe operations execute without downloading the intermediate image to the CPU.
- [ ] Results match the CPU reference within existing equivalence tolerances.
- [ ] Tests cover representative settings, image boundaries, small images, preview and export resolutions, and zoom windows.
- [ ] Resolution independence and stage-cache invalidation remain correct.
- [ ] Unsupported configurations and GPU failures retain a working CPU fallback.
- [ ] Before/after measurements report rendering latency and transfer volume with defringe enabled, plus overhead when disabled.
- [ ] The implementation preserves Metal, Vulkan, DX12, and WASM compatibility and follows the repository’s pure-Rust restrictions.
- [ ] `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: Coordinate cache, UI texture, and AI memory under system memory pressure
author: draco892
body:
LightCraft already budgets several caches and processing activities, but retained image caches, UI textures, and AI model resources do not have a coordinated response to system memory pressure.

These consumers can compete for the same physical memory, particularly on unified-memory systems. Static budgets alone cannot account for changing memory demand from other applications.

## Proposed change

Introduce a common memory-pressure policy that coordinates cache eviction, safe release of inactive UI textures, AI resource retention, and deferral of nonessential background work.

Use platform-specific pressure signals where available, with conservative behavior elsewhere. Preserve explicit user budget settings and prioritize active editing.

Improve memory reporting so retained resources and shared allocations can be understood without double-counting.

## Scope and related issues

- Split from the broader memory-efficiency proposal in [#2782](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/issues/2782).
- **Concurrent GPU render admission, device-memory exhaustion, and OOM retry behavior belong to [#1764](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/issues/1764) and are explicitly excluded.** Integrate with its accounting where appropriate.
- Mask alpha caching and missing chromaticity-plane accounting belong to [#1145](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/issues/1145).
- Coordinate texture ownership and release with [#1228](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/issues/1228); device sharing and presentation remain outside this ticket.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Memory reporting identifies retained cache, UI texture, and AI resources, with accounting limitations documented.
- [ ] Shared resources are counted once, and logical allocation totals are distinguished from measured process memory.
- [ ] Injected pressure signals deterministically trigger documented eviction and retention policies.
- [ ] Active resources remain valid while unused resources are released safely.

title: Sony ILCE-6700 (APS-C): vignetting and lateral CA tables measured, same result as the ILCE-7RM6
author: Enthendor
body:
`docs/sony-ilce7rm6-lens-corrections.md` decides two things for the ILCE-7RM6. Vignetting is read but not applied, because the camera JPEG doesn't compensate it. The lateral CA planes are off, because a warp after demosaic overshoots, and the follow-up is to correct CA on the raw CFA. I measured both on the APS-C ILCE-6700 (the body from #2732). Both decisions hold there too. Numbers only; the photos are private, measured clean room.

**Material:** 30 ARWs (Lossless Compressed, 6192 × 4128 default crop, 11-knot tables):
- Sigma 10–18 mm F2.8 DC DN (9)
- Tamron 17–70 mm F2.8 B070 (13)
- Sony E 70–350 mm G (8)

On all of them `VignettingCorrection`, `LateralChromaticAberration` and `DistortionCorrectionSetting` are Auto (2). Knots as in #2732: crop half diagonal / 10 = 372.09 px.

### Vignetting: not compensated, by JPEG or raw
- **Method:** I compared the camera JPEG with `lightcraft-cli render` with lens corrections on, both in linear luminance and downsampled 8×. A tone curve JPEG ← render is learnt inside 0.3 of the half diagonal. Each ring outside that gives the median log₂(JPEG / curve(render)).
- **Result:** At r ≥ 0.875 the JPEG's gain over our uncorrected render is **median −0.03 EV (p5 −0.15, p95 +0.06)**. Read as `1 + v / 2¹⁴`, the tables would predict **+0.62 EV at the corner (0.34–0.86)**. As alternatives, `v / 2¹³` gives +1.05 and `v / 2¹⁵` gives +0.34. Regressing the measured EV on the predicted one gives a slope of 0.11.
- **Sensitivity:** I applied an artificial radial gain to the render. Predicted +0.69 EV, measured +0.60 EV, so the method would see a compensation of that size.
- **Raw not pre-compensated:**
  - No missing codes: the stored values in the corners are as dense as in the centre (a digital gain before storage would leave gaps).
  - On one ISO 64000 frame, at equal stored level, corner noise divided by centre noise is 0.90–1.01 across levels. The table's gain applied digitally would give about 1.4.

title: AUR: makepkg !lto does not disable Rust ThinLTO inherited from Cargo.toml
author: rwarmstr
body:
Split from #2811 at the triage bot's request. This ticket covers only the downstream AUR packaging behavior; #2811 tracks documentation of the rustc/LLVM SIGILL configuration.

### Problem

In AUR lightcraft 0.13.0-1 (packaging commit 71da1d7), _srcenv() contains:

~~~sh
if check_option lto y; then
    export CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_LTO=thin
    export CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_CODEGEN_UNITS=1
fi
~~~

Upstream Cargo.toml already sets lto = "thin" in [profile.release]. With makepkg's !lto option, the conditional is skipped, but Cargo falls back to the upstream ThinLTO setting. The intended opt-out therefore does not disable Rust LTO. This follows the AUR change faed654 (0.11.0-2), whose stated intent was to follow makepkg options.

### Expected behavior / proposed downstream fix

When makepkg selects !lto, explicitly disable Rust LTO:

~~~sh
if check_option lto y; then
    export CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_LTO=thin
    export CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_CODEGEN_UNITS=1
else
    export CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_LTO=off
fi
~~~

Setting off is deliberate: Cargo's false value may still allow local ThinLTO across codegen units, whereas off disables LTO entirely. Validation should check that the effective rustc invocation has LTO disabled when !lto is selected and still uses ThinLTO when lto is selected.

### Evidence / scope

Explicitly setting CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_LTO=off inside _srcenv() allowed both 0.7.1-1 and 0.13.0-1 to build successfully on the affected system, and both rebuilt CLIs ran. This is a workaround verification, not a test of the exact conditional patch above.

Related #1196 concerns OOM on low-memory builders and was closed after README documentation landed in #1667; the maintainer comment there explicitly leaves PKGBUILD changes to the AUR package. The same need for an effective LTO opt-out applies here, but the SIGILL in #2811 is a different observed failure mode. This ticket is for downstream AUR coordination; no change to the upstream default release profile is requeste…

title: Lightroom import: the archive loses the settings of history steps and snapshots from Lightroom Classic 13 and later
author: clydecbrown
body:
Importing a Lightroom Classic catalog keeps its history steps and snapshots in the import archive, which says they
"remain available for recovery" (`crates/engine/src/lightroom_archive.rs`, module doc). For catalogs written by
Lightroom Classic 13 or later, the archive holds each step and snapshot without its settings: only the name, date
and ids are left, so the edit history can't be recovered from it. Nothing warns about it.

**Cause.** Lightroom 6 stores each history step's settings (`Adobe_libraryImageDevelopHistoryStep.text`) as text.
Lightroom Classic 13 and later store it as a BLOB: a 4-byte big-endian length followed by zlib-compressed Lua, the
same encoding as `Adobe_AdditionalMetadata.xmp`. Upgrading an old catalog in Lightroom Classic 13 converts its steps
too. Checked on catalogs written by Lightroom 6.3, 6.6 and 6.14 (text), and Lightroom Classic 13.0, 15 and 15.3
(compressed, every step).

The catalog reader decodes only the `xmp` BLOB (`Reader::xmp_table`). `Reader::table`, which reads the history-step
and snapshot tables, drops every BLOB value (`SqlValue::Blob(_) => None`, "Opaque Lightroom payloads never become
JSON byte arrays"), so those rows reach the archive with no `text`.

Snapshots (`Adobe_libraryImageDevelopSnapshot.text`) are still stored as text by Lightroom Classic 15.3, so they
are archived whole today; they are read the same way, so one stored compressed would lose its settings too.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC-1: Importing a catalog whose history steps are stored compressed (Lightroom Classic 13 and later) keeps
      each step's decoded settings (`text`) in the import archive, next to its name and date.
- [ ] AC-2: The same for a snapshot stored compressed (Lightroom Classic 15.3 still writes them as text).
- [ ] AC-3: History steps and snapshots stored as text (Lightroom 6) are archived as before.
- [ ] AC-4: A step or snapshot whose BLOB is malformed (short length prefix, bad zlib data, a length that doesn't
      match, more…

title: [Feature Request] Folders panel: option to list only the folders I added (like Lightroom Classic)
author: jkalkstein
body:
## Problem

The Folders section lists every folder from the disk down to the folders that hold photos. A library kept under a
deep path opens on a run of rows that hold no photos and only lead further in, each repeating the same count. The
folder someone is looking for ends up far down the list.

## Lightroom Classic's behaviour

Lightroom Classic's Folders panel lists the folders that were added to the catalog (imported or added as folders), with
their subfolders beneath them. It does not list the folders above them on the disk.

## Proposed behaviour

A new setting, **Show only the folders you added (like Lightroom)**, off by default. When it is on:

- Each folder added in place is a row under its disk, with its subfolders beneath it. A folder is added by an
  import that keeps the files where they are, by **File ▸ Import from Folder…**, or by dropping a folder on the window.
- A folder added inside another added folder stays inside it. It is not a second top-level row.
- Photos imported one at a time, with no added folder above them, are listed under the nearest folder that holds
  photos.
- Counts, choosing a row, dragging photos onto a row, colour labels and the right-click menu work as they do for the
  full tree.
- The **+** in the Folders header runs File ▸ Import from Folder….

When the setting is off, the Folders section is unchanged.

## How to switch it on

Settings ▸ Interface ▸ tick **Show only the folders you added (like Lightroom)**.

## Open questions

- Libraries made before this exists have no record of which folders were added. Should there be a one-time way to
  mark them, or is adding the folder again acceptable?
- Related: #565 asks for the folders that photos were imported from to be listed under Local.

title: Find Missing Photos skips virtual copies whose original uses the same file
author: maxinjapan
body:
## What happens

After importing an old Lightroom Classic catalog whose photos had moved to another volume, Find Missing Photos (`library.findMissing`) relinks each original but leaves its virtual copies missing. The copies stay in Missing Photos with their old path, even though the file they need is on disk and their own original already points to it.

That is how it happened here: the first Find Missing Photos run relinked only the original of each photo, and every virtual copy stayed behind at the old path. Running it again doesn't help, because by then the original "uses" the file. In my library (~80,000 photos imported from Lightroom), 85 virtual copies ("Copy 1", "Copy 2", …) were left missing like this. Many have their own edits, ratings and picks (e.g. ★5 + Pick on a copy whose original is ★0), so deleting them as "duplicates" from Missing Photos would lose real work.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Have a Lightroom catalog with a photo and a virtual copy of it, both referencing `/Volumes/OLD/Photo/a.dng`.
2. Import it with File ▸ Import Lightroom Catalog… while the file is actually at `/Volumes/NEW/Photo/a.dng`.
3. Run Find Missing Photos on `/Volumes/NEW/Photo`.

**Expected:** both the original and its virtual copy point to `/Volumes/NEW/Photo/a.dng`.
**Actual:** only the original is relinked. The virtual copy stays missing and is not listed under `ambiguous` either. Running Find Missing Photos again doesn't relink it.

## Cause

Both stages treat a file that any other photo already uses as unavailable, without allowing for virtual copies, which are meant to share their original's file (`copy_of`):

- `plan_find_missing` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/missing.rs`): `in_use` drops every file that is already some photo's original from the search, and `used` stops a second photo from matching a file another photo just took. So in the first run the original wins the file and its copies get nothing; in later runs the file is already in use.
- `commit_find` (same file): ski…

title: Noise reduction runs only after the colour matrix has amplified the noise: test denoising before it
author: radialmonster
body:
## What happens

At main 38f8d2508700, the standard noise reduction runs only after white balance and the colour matrix have mixed and scaled the sensor noise:

1. **Black subtract** (`crates/raw/src/lib.rs:822-858`).
2. **Demosaic** (`crates/engine/src/files.rs:483`, AHD at full size).
3. **Highlight rebuild.**
4. **`CameraColourModel::apply`** (`files.rs:263-306`, called at `:511`): white balance, the camera or fitted matrix, the hue/saturation table, then a clamp at 0.
5. **Luminance and colour NR,** only now, in the pipeline (`crates/pipeline/src/lib.rs:579`, `local.rs:429-470`), on linear Rec.2020.

Two things already work on the mosaic, and neither is a standard denoise:

- The optional AI Denoise (`files.rs:396`).
- Hot-pixel removal, proposed in #1345 / #1350.

## Evidence

- On #840 (R6 CR3, ISO 1600), the JPEG-fitted matrix's blue row has 2.3× the noise gain of the spectral matrix (our #840 comment).

- Refitting the matrix with a noise budget made ΔE against the camera JPEG worse: 9.1 → 10.0 for the matrix alone (#840). So the gain comes with the matrix the colour fit wants and can't be fitted away.
- After the matrix, the noise of each CFA colour is spread over R, G and B and correlated between them. A per-photosite noise model (variance ≈ a·level + b per CFA colour, as #1345 uses) no longer describes it.

## Hypothesis to measure

Before WB and the matrix, the noise is still independent per photosite and follows one variance model per CFA colour. Denoising there (on the mosaic, or on camera RGB) could remove more of the blue-row-amplified noise than filtering after the matrix, for the same loss of detail. This hasn't been measured yet.

title: Camera look: the fitted shadow toe (log-log slope up to ~3.9) multiplies shadow noise
author: radialmonster
body:
## What happens

At main 38f8d2508700, a raw with a fitted camera look gets its tone curve from the camera JPEG.

- **Where the curve comes from:** `crates/engine/src/camera_preview.rs`, `fit_tone_with_shadows` at `:1074` and `fit_tone` at `:2032`. The toe follows the JPEG's darkest tones (#1307, #1340).
- **Where it's applied:** in the tone map (`crates/pipeline/src/finish.rs:273` → `ToneMap::camera_hdr`, used at `finish.rs:529`). That is after NR and sharpening.
- **No slope limit:** nothing bounds the toe's slope. In log-log terms, relative noise leaves the curve multiplied by the local slope. A toe of slope 3.5 makes shadow noise 3.5× larger relative to the level.

## Evidence

- On the #840 R6 CR3 (ISO 1600), the fitted curve lifts scene 0.022–0.030 to 0.024–0.069. That's a log-log slope of about 3.4 (our local #840 study, round 1). Our #840 comment measured a shadow slope of 3.9.
- AlexChambers on #840: with the colour transform held constant, the fitted curve raises the blue residual 2.4–2.8× over the default raw curve, on three patches.
- Our #840 comment tried capping the toe slope at 2.5 alone. On the blue patches, ΔE against the JPEG went from 7.5 to 6.4. Over the whole frame, it went from 9.1 to 9.7. A plain cap trades accuracy elsewhere, so it isn't a fix as it stands.

## Why it matters

The camera's steep toe goes with its own in-camera noise reduction. Copying the toe onto our less-denoised data multiplies whatever noise is left in the shadows.

Hypothesis to measure: on noisy frames, part of the steepness is fitted from noise. The darkest JPEG levels are paired with noisy sensor values.

## Proposed investigation

1. On every raw whose look is fitted, measure the toe slope (log-log, scene 0.005–0.05) per ISO band.
   - If the slope rises with ISO, the fit is learning noise.
   - If it's steady per camera, it's the camera's real look.
2. Per file, multiply the slope by the flat-block noise at that level, with the matrix held fixed. That gives the noi…

title: Local Moiré / Noise masks blur the rgb/Y ratio, so dark noisy pixels can tint the masked area
author: radialmonster
body:
The local Moiré slider, and the colour part of the local Noise slider, blur the per-pixel chromaticity `rgb / max(Y, 1e-6)`. Blurring that ratio does not keep the area's average colour. Dark, noisy pixels have a tiny or floored Y, so their ratios are huge and dominate the blur. The likely result is tinted or lifted shadows inside masks at high ISO. This is a hypothesis from reading the code; it has not been measured on this path yet.

**Where (main 38f8d250)**
- The ratio: `crates/pipeline/src/masks.rs:638-641` (`chromaticity`, `luminance_2020(c).max(1e-6)`).
- CPU blur of the ratio plane: `crates/pipeline/src/local.rs:612` (`gaussian(&img.map(masks::chromaticity), sg)`).
- Use: `crates/pipeline/src/finish.rs:418-423`. Each pixel's chromaticity moves toward the blurred one by `mt = l_moire + 0.5 * max(l_noise, 0)`. It is then multiplied by the pixel's own Y and clamped with `max(0)`.
- GPU twin: `crates/gpu/src/wgsl/map.wgsl:149` (`chroma_k`), blurred in `crates/gpu/src/render.rs:904-907`.

**Why it matters**
- The weighted mean of `rgb / Y` over a window is not `sum(rgb) / sum(Y)`. In a flat area, pixels whose Y has dropped near zero from noise get ratios far from the true colour, sometimes by a factor of 100 or more. One of those pixels can move the blurred value for its whole neighbourhood.
- Global colour NR has the same structure. PR #2598 (for #840) replaces it there with `blur(rgb) / blur(Y)` and measures the ΔE gain. #2598 does not change this local mask path, so a Noise or Moiré brush on a high-ISO shadow keeps the old behaviour.
- When negative values are allowed through before NR (PR #2278), Y can be ≤ 0. At that point the 1e-6 floor turns into a very large ratio, with the sign carried by rgb.

**Proposed investigation**
1. Change the local plane to blur `[r, g, b, Y]` and divide after the blur (`blur(rgb) / max(blur(Y), eps)`), on CPU and GPU. Same approach as #2598.
2. Paint a full-frame mask with local Noise +100 (and, separately, Moiré +100) on high-I…

title: GPU: renders over ~179 MP fall back to the CPU (one RGB f32 buffer exceeds the 2047 MiB storage-binding limit); tile the render
author: radialmonster
body:
A render whose output is over about 179 MP never runs on the GPU. The whole render is redone on the CPU because the output RGB buffer alone is bigger than the 2047 MiB storage-buffer binding limit. For example, a 200 MP Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra DNG (16320 × 12240) needs a 2287 MiB buffer and falls back. Splitting the render into tiles, or splitting its buffers, would keep these files on the GPU.

Version: main 38f8d2508 (2026-10-24).

## Where it happens

- `crates/gpu/src/render.rs:607`: `render()` checks `gpu.fits(n * 3)` for the planned output (`n = plan.w * plan.h`, three f32 channels). If it doesn't fit, it fails with `FailKind::Limit` ("W×H needs N MiB buffers, over the device's M MiB storage-buffer limit") before any GPU work starts.
- `crates/gpu/src/ctx.rs:381`: `max_buffer = min(max_storage_buffer_binding_size, max_buffer_size)`, logged at start-up as `gpu: … buffers ≤ N MiB`. This is 2047 MiB on an RTX 3090 with DX12, and on an RTX A1000 with Vulkan (from #1764's log).
- `crates/gpu/src/ctx.rs:391`: `Gpu::buffer()` fails the same way for any single buffer over the limit.
- `crates/gpu/src/lib.rs:499-530`: `FailKind::Limit` logs `gpu: rendering on the CPU instead: …` and redoes this render on the CPU. That is correct as a fallback, but on these files it happens on every render (loupe, zoom, export).

The source side already has a way around this: `render.rs:624` samples geometry on the CPU when `src.data.len() * 3` doesn't fit. The output check at line 607 has no such path.

## Buffer maths

One working buffer is `W × H × 3 × 4` bytes (RGB f32), and the limit is 2^31 − 1 bytes:

- largest output that fits: (2^31 − 1) / 12 = 178,956,970 px, about 179 MP
- Galaxy S25 Ultra 200 MP DNG, 16320 × 12240 = 199,756,800 px → 2,397,081,600 B = 2287 MiB (`div_ceil`), over by 240 MiB
- Fujifilm GFX100 class, 11648 × 8736 = 101.8 MP → 1165 MiB, fits
- Sony A7R V/IV, 9504 × 6336 = 60.2 MP → 690 MiB, fits

So today the cliff is at about 179 MP of output on desktop GPUs. O…

title: 16-bit TIFF export with LZW is larger than uncompressed and twice as slow
author: radialmonster
body:
A 16-bit TIFF export with **LZW** compression comes out larger than the same export with no compression, and it takes about twice as long. The export dialog offers LZW next to ZIP with no hint about this, so a user who picks LZW to save space gets the opposite.

Version: main 38f8d2508 (2026-10-24), CLI release build, CPU render (`LIGHTCRAFT_GPU=0`), two runs each (sizes identical across runs, times are the mean).

## Numbers

`lightcraft-cli render <raw> --output out.tif` with `tiffCompression` none / lzw / deflate and 8 or 16 bit, default develop settings. Times are the wall time of the whole render + export:

Nikon D750 NEF, 24 MP
- 16-bit: none 145.9 MB in 1.41 s, LZW 176.0 MB (+21 %) in 3.21 s, ZIP 129.9 MB (−11 %) in 1.85 s
- 8-bit: none 73.0 MB in 1.20 s, LZW 56.0 MB (−23 %) in 1.91 s, ZIP 47.3 MB (−35 %) in 1.44 s

Canon EOS R7 CR3, 32 MP
- 16-bit: none 193.8 MB in 2.14 s, LZW 257.0 MB (+33 %) in 4.95 s, ZIP 186.0 MB (−4 %) in 2.79 s
- 8-bit: none 96.9 MB in 1.99 s, LZW 106.5 MB (+10 %) in 3.06 s, ZIP 80.4 MB (−17 %) in 2.14 s

Nikon Z9 NEF, 45 MP
- 16-bit: none 272.7 MB in 2.68 s, LZW 298.7 MB (+10 %) in 5.61 s, ZIP 226.8 MB (−17 %) in 3.58 s
- 8-bit: none 136.3 MB in 2.36 s, LZW 69.3 MB (−49 %) in 3.73 s, ZIP 71.5 MB (−48 %) in 3.06 s

So at 16 bit LZW was larger than uncompressed on all three files, and at 8 bit on one of three. ZIP (the default) was never larger and was always faster than LZW.

The files are written as the TIFF spec says: Compression (259) = 5 for LZW and 8 for ZIP (the registered Adobe Deflate code, not the old 32946), and Predictor (317) = 2 (horizontal differencing) on both, checked from the IFD of the written files. So this isn't a missing predictor. With 16-bit samples, the low byte of each difference is mostly noise, and LZW's byte-oriented dictionary does worse on it than storing the bytes raw.

## Where

- `crates/codecs/src/encode.rs:217-250`: `TiffCompression` (default `Deflate`) and `encode_tiff`, which sets `Predictor::Horizo…

title: Web: a page should reach the whole control channel (lightcraft.request)
author: hayone1
body:
## What I'd like

Add `lightcraft.request(method, params)` next to `lightcraft.command(id, params)` in the browser version.

## Why

`lightcraft.command` runs engine and UI commands, which is great. But a page can't call the other control methods the desktop control server and MCP have, like `ui.inspect` or `ui.menu.invoke`. VectorCraft (`window.vectorcraft.request`) and FilmCraft already offer those to the page.

With `request`, one AI agent or host app can drive LightCraft, VectorCraft and the others in the same way. We host the craft apps for a small team with an AI assistant on top, and today we patch LightCraft's web build to get this. We'd rather use something built in.

## Proposal

- `lightcraft.request(method, params)`: `params` is an object (or JSON text, like `command`). It resolves to the method's `result` as an object and rejects with an `Error` on failure.
- It uses the same control channel as the desktop app (`with_control`).
- To save memory in the browser, the renderer would not keep CPU copies of photos for it (those are only for headless screenshots).

I have a PR ready for this.

title: White balance: a partial with only Temp or only Tint on the other scale keeps the old field on the new scale
author: radialmonster
body:
On current main (`31ec62cd`), a settings partial that sets only `temp` or only `tint` on the other white balance scale keeps the photo's other field unchanged, but now reads it on the new scale. The result is a different white than either the photo or the partial asked for.

`DevelopSettings::merged` (`crates/develop/src/lib.rs:45`) deep-merges the partial and then takes the scale from it. A partial with no `scale` counts as `Legacy` (relative). So on a raw edited in Kelvin:

```
photo:   wb { temp: 5000, tint: 10, scale: kelvin }
partial: { "wb": { "temp": 5800 } }
result:  wb { temp: 5800, tint: 10, scale: legacy }
```

Tint 10 was a Kelvin-scale tint. It is now read as a shift from the as-shot tint, so the green/magenta balance moves although the partial never touched tint. The other direction is the same: a Kelvin `temp`-only partial on a photo still on the relative scale keeps the relative tint and marks it Kelvin. The existing test at `lib.rs:241` pins the scale change, not the kept field.

Who can hit it: `develop.merge`, `render --settings` and preset JSON written by hand. Presets made from a photo and the crs/Luminar importers always write `temp`, `tint` and `scale` together, so they are not affected. It came up in the review of #2896, which keeps the same behaviour at Amounts below 100 % on purpose so the two paths match.

## Proposal

Resolve white balance partials against the photo before merging, where the as-shot white balance is known:

1. Add `kelvin_to_legacy(temp, tint, as_shot)` in `crates/pipeline/src/local.rs`, the inverse of `legacy_to_kelvin`. It runs the Bradford step of `legacy_white` backwards: cone response × reference / as-shot, then `xy_to_temp_tint`. Add a round-trip test against `legacy_to_kelvin` over the whole slider range.
2. Add one engine-level merge for settings applied to a photo, and use it in every photo-facing caller: preset apply, `develop.merge`, `render --settings`. When the partial's scale differs from the photo's (explic…

title: Windows, Intel iGPU (DX12): GPU renders slower than the CPU; every process waits 2-7 s while 27 kernels compile one after another
author: iluebbe
body:
**What happens**

On a Windows laptop with an Intel iGPU, rendering with the GPU (the default) is slower than with `LIGHTCRAFT_GPU=0`, both for one-shot CLI renders and for batches in one process:

1. **Start-up:** the first GPU render of every process waits for the device and **all 27 compute kernels** to be built (`ctx::Gpu::new`): 1.7–4.0 s per process here (median 2.3 s), **7.2 s** the very first time after the install. `docs/gpu-pipeline.md` budgets this at ~0.3–0.4 s (measured on Apple). The desktop app hides most of it in `gpu::warm_up`, but every `lightcraft-cli render` / `run` / headless MCP session pays it in full.
2. **After start-up** the GPU path is not faster than the CPU for exports either, and varies a lot between runs.

**Machine**

Windows 11 Pro (26300), Intel Core Ultra 7 165U (12 cores / 14 threads), "Intel(R) Graphics" (Meteor Lake iGPU), driver 32.0.101.8425, DX12 (the Windows default since #136, shaders through FXC per #471). LightCraft 0.13.0 (MSI). Sony ILCE-6500 ARW, 24 MP.

**Measured** (LightCraft's own per-command `ms`, so process start and import don't count; 10 ARWs, 5 runs alternating GPU / CPU, median and range)

```
lightcraft-cli run --import a.ARW … (10) app.gpu library.selectAll \
  app.export dir=… longEdge=1600 app.export dir=… longEdge=0 quality=90
```

| | GPU (default) | CPU (`LIGHTCRAFT_GPU=0`) |
|---|---|---|
| `app.gpu` (device + kernels) | **2274 ms** (1694–4029) | – |
| `app.export` 10 × 1600 px | **9516 ms** (3531–12879) | **3653 ms** (3057–6414) |
| `app.export` 10 × full size (6000 × 4000) | 35731 ms (25709–52865) | 34822 ms (26144–43255) |

The machine wasn't idle (other desktop apps open), so the ranges are wide: at 1600 px the GPU was 1.9–3.9× slower in three of the five GPU/CPU pairs, equal in one and 1.8× faster in one; the start-up cost is there every time. One-shot `lightcraft-cli render x.ARW -o x.jpg --size 1600`: median 6.1 s on the GPU against 1.0 s on the CPU.

title: lightcraft-cli: --script rejects a UTF-8 file that starts with a BOM (what Windows PowerShell writes)
author: iluebbe
body:
**What happens**

`lightcraft-cli run --script steps.jsonl` (and `snapshot --script`) fails on the first line when the file starts with a UTF-8 byte order mark:

```
lightcraft-cli: steps.jsonl:1: expected value at line 1 column 1
```

On Windows this is the default: Windows PowerShell 5.1 writes a BOM with `Set-Content -Encoding utf8` and `Out-File -Encoding utf8`, so the obvious way to write a script there produces a file the CLI rejects. The message doesn't hint at the cause (the line looks like valid JSON in any editor).

**Repro** (Windows PowerShell 5.1, LightCraft 0.13.0)

```powershell
'{"command": "library.info", "params": {}}' | Set-Content -Encoding utf8 steps.jsonl
& "C:\Program Files\LightCraft\lightcraft-cli.exe" run --demo --script steps.jsonl
# lightcraft-cli: steps.jsonl:1: expected value at line 1 column 1
```

The same file without the BOM (`[IO.File]::WriteAllLines(path, lines, [Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false))`) runs.

**Cause**

`apps/lightcraft-cli/src/main.rs` reads the script with `read_to_string` and hands each of `text.lines()` to `serde_json::from_str`; the first line still starts with U+FEFF. Same in the `snapshot` script reader.

**Suggestion**

Strip one leading `\u{feff}` from the script text (both readers, and `--script -` from stdin) before splitting into lines.

title: Export: transparent PNG sources lose their alpha (flattened onto white) even when exporting PNG/TIFF/WebP
author: radialmonster
body:
**Version:** LightCraft 0.14.0 (`lightcraft-cli`, Windows 11)

Exporting a photo that has transparency (a PNG with an alpha channel) always flattens it onto white. Exporting to a format that can hold alpha (PNG, TIFF, WebP) drops the transparency, so logos, cut-outs and composites can't round-trip through LightCraft.

### Steps

1. Make a 300×200 RGBA PNG: fully transparent, with an opaque 150×100 rectangle in the middle.
2. Run `lightcraft-cli run --library ./lib --script steps.jsonl` with:

```json
{"command":"library.import","params":{"paths":["src/t.png"]}}
{"command":"library.selectAll","params":{}}
{"command":"app.export","params":{"format":"png","dir":"out"}}
```

### Actual

`out/t.png` is an RGB PNG. The transparent area is pure white (255,255,255), and the alpha channel is gone.

### Expected

When the source has an alpha channel and the export format supports one, the export keeps it. Pixels keep their source alpha, edits apply to the colour channels, and the colour is not composited onto any backdrop. Formats without alpha (JPEG) and opaque sources keep today's behaviour: composited onto white, no alpha channel written. That matches the space-saving point in #1952.

### Proposal

Carry the source alpha through the render as its own plane, untouched by the develop pipeline. Crop, rotate and resize transform it along with the image. Then:
- PNG and WebP write RGBA when the plane has any value below fully opaque;
- TIFF writes an associated alpha plane;
- JPEG keeps compositing onto white.

The grid and loupe already show a backdrop for transparent areas (#1212), so on screen nothing changes.

title: Import ignores Lightroom develop settings embedded in JPEGs (only Read Metadata from File applies them)
author: tinytom21
body:
LightCraft 0.13.0, Linux Mint (Flatpak).

Lightroom (cloud version) stores edits for JPEGs inside the file as an embedded XMP packet (`crs:HasSettings="True"`, process version 11.0 and 15.4 in my files). It writes no sidecar.

**Steps**
1. Export JPEGs from Lightroom with "Original + Settings". The JPEGs contain `crs:` develop settings (exposure, highlights/shadows, tone curve, HSL, crop) and there is no `.xmp` file next to them.
2. Import the folder into LightCraft with Add in place.
3. Select a photo and choose Read Metadata from File.

**Expected:** the photo already has Lightroom's settings after step 2, as it would with a sidecar.

**Actual:** every photo imports with default develop settings. After step 3 the sliders, tone curve, colour mixer and crop all match Lightroom, so the reader from #2042 works. It just isn't used at import time.

For people moving from Lightroom CC this matters: all of their JPEG edits are embedded, so a library import silently drops them unless they know to run Read Metadata from File on everything.

Related: #2042 (embedded JPEG XMP for Read Metadata from File) and #1995 (embedded rating, flag and label on import).

I can attach a sample JPEG with embedded settings if that helps.

title: Ctrl+V (Paste Edit Settings) does nothing on Windows/Linux unless the system clipboard holds text
author: radialmonster
body:
On Windows and Linux, Ctrl+V (Paste Edit Settings) does nothing unless the system clipboard holds text. Ctrl+C (Copy Edit Settings) works, and rebinding Paste Edit Settings to a key without Ctrl (e.g. Shift+V) also works. Reported on v0.14.0 in Develop, both with a slider focused and after clicking a photo.

**Cause**

egui-winit turns Ctrl+V into a clipboard event instead of a key press, and only pushes it when the clipboard has non-empty text:

- egui-winit 0.36.2 (v0.14.0), `lib.rs` around line 1027: on a paste command it reads the clipboard, pushes `Event::Paste(contents)` only if the text is non-empty, then `return`s, so no `Event::Key { V, ctrl }` is sent either.
- egui-winit 0.37.0 (main): same, except that with no text it falls back to `Event::PasteImage` when an image is on the clipboard.

`shortcuts::matches` (crates/ui-egui/src/shortcuts.rs) maps `Event::Paste(_)` back to Ctrl+V, but when the clipboard is empty or holds an image, file or other non-text data, there is no event to map. Copying edit settings with Ctrl+C keeps them inside the app and doesn't write text to the system clipboard, so the usual sequence "Ctrl+C on one photo, Ctrl+V on another" fails whenever the clipboard had no text beforehand. `tests_keymap.rs::clipboard_events_run_the_copy_and_paste_shortcuts` injects `Event::Paste("text")` directly, so it doesn't catch this.

**Proposal**

In our egui fork (storytold/egui, already patched in through `[patch.crates-io]`), change egui-winit's paste branch so that when there's no non-empty text it pushes the normal `Event::Key { key: V, pressed: true, modifiers }` instead of nothing (and keeps `PasteImage` for apps that want it). Then add a keymap test that sends Ctrl+V with an empty clipboard and with an image on it, checking that Paste Edit Settings runs and that Ctrl+Shift+V opens Paste Selected Settings. Text fields aren't affected: they still get `Event::Paste` whenever there is text to paste.

**Workaround until then:** copy any text first …

title: Canon EOS 450D (Rebel XSi): no colour model, so strong reds render darker, dark colours lose saturation and shadows are lifted
author: radialmonster
body:
The Canon EOS 450D (Digital Rebel XSi / Kiss X2) has no colour model in LightCraft. Its CR2s render through the per-photo camera-look fallback, and with default settings strong reds come out darker, dark colours lose about a third to a half of their saturation, and shadows and lower midtones are lifted on some scenes.

**What happens** (main 1a3d9aff; no colour or tone changes since v0.14.0)
- The 450D, Rebel XSi and Kiss X2 aren't in `crates/raw/src/spectral_table.rs` or its alias list.
- Three reporter CR2s (a harbour boat with red paint, a lighthouse against blue sky, a third outdoor scene), each compared with its own embedded camera JPEG after pixel-accurate registration (scale 0.99, 5–8 px offset). The values are 8-bit sRGB, averaged over the same pixels:
  - Bright saturated red (the boat's paint, about 96k pixels): camera 147/15/11, LightCraft 126/11/7. The saturation is the same, but the red is about 14% darker.
  - Medium reds: saturation 0.73 → 0.62. Dark reds: 0.86 → 0.78 and darker.
  - Dark red (the lighthouse top, about 18k pixels): camera 51/33/36 (saturation 0.34), LightCraft 45/35/37 (0.23). It reads as red in the camera JPEG and as near-black in LightCraft.
  - Dark muted blues: 0.35 → 0.20. Deep sky blue: 0.52 → 0.49.
  - Tone (camera luma → LightCraft luma, by camera band): on one photo 40 → 46, 55 → 63, 81 → 88; on another 76 → 86, 111 → 121; on the third within 1–2 levels throughout. Above about 130, all three match.
  - White balance matches: the blue/red ratio of near-grey areas is 1.078 vs 1.082, 1.073 vs 1.067 and 1.087 vs 1.092, and the whole-image means are within about 1 level.
- The reporter's description: "reds become almost black and blues become grey".

The camera JPEG uses Canon's Standard picture style, so it isn't colour truth. But the loss here grows as colours get darker, and the shadow lift varies from scene to scene on the same body, so it isn't just a softer neutral rendering.

title: Sidecars never write lr:hierarchicalSubject: a removed hierarchical keyword comes back on Read Metadata from File
author: xilcmd
body:
A sidecar saved by LightCraft never writes or updates `lr:hierarchicalSubject`. Two things follow from that:

1. **A removed hierarchical keyword comes back.** The stale path stays in the existing sidecar's `lr:hierarchicalSubject`. The next Read Metadata from File (or a re-import) adds it to the photo again.
2. **A new hierarchical keyword is written only as a flat name with pipes.** `dc:subject` gets `Places|Porto` and there is no `lr:hierarchicalSubject`, so Lightroom Classic and other XMP readers see one flat keyword named `Places|Porto`.

Found with auto-write on (`library.xmpPreferences autoWrite=true`) while I replaced a keyword on a few dozen photos; the old keyword reappeared in every sidecar. Reproduced below with `photo.saveMetadataToFile` on a generated file.

### Reproduce (lightcraft-cli 0.14.0, Linux x86_64)

```sh
mkdir -p repro/photos && cd repro
python3 -c "from PIL import Image; Image.new('RGB',(64,48),(120,140,160)).save('photos/test.jpg')"
exiftool -q -o photos/test.xmp '-XMP-dc:Subject=Places|Lisbon' '-XMP-lr:HierarchicalSubject=Places|Lisbon'

lightcraft-cli run --library lib --import photos \
  photo.setMeta '{"ids":[1],"removeKeywords":["Places|Lisbon"],"addKeywords":["Beach"]}' \
  photo.saveMetadataToFile '{"ids":[1]}' photo.inspect id=1     # keywords: ["Beach"]

exiftool -s -XMP-dc:Subject -XMP-lr:HierarchicalSubject photos/test.xmp
#   Subject             : Beach
#   HierarchicalSubject : Places|Lisbon        <- stale

lightcraft-cli run --library lib photo.readMetadataFromFile '{"ids":[1]}' photo.inspect id=1
#   keywords: ["Places|Lisbon", "Beach"]       <- the removed keyword is back
```

On a photo with no sidecar, adding `Places|Porto` and saving writes `dc:subject = Places|Porto` and no `lr:hierarchicalSubject` at all.

### Cause (main 63cb047c)

- `sidecar_packet_with` (`crates/engine/src/sidecar.rs`) sets `keywords: p.meta.keywords.clone()`, which are full paths, and never sets `hierarchical_keywords`. Export does this split alr…

title: Honor the Startup View preference when opening an image from the file manager or CLI
author: chilango74
body:
## Description

The **Startup View → Detail View** preference is ignored when opening an image from a file manager (or passing its path on the command line). LightCraft imports/selects the photo but opens **Photo Grid**, requiring an extra D press or double-click to see the image.

This makes the preference ineffective for users who choose LightCraft as their default image viewer. This report concerns launching with an image path; it does not claim that the preference is ignored on a launch without files.

## Environment

- LightCraft **0.14.0**, official Linux x86_64 DEB (`0.14.0-1`).
- Ubuntu **26.04.1 LTS**, amd64, GNOME/Wayland desktop.
- Isolated native-window reproduction under Xvfb/X11 with a separate HOME, runtime directory, settings and library; software rendering. JPEG and PNG were checked. No headless screenshot fallback was used.
- Desktop entry: `Exec=lightcraft %F`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Set **Settings → General → Startup View → Detail View** and close LightCraft.
2. Open a JPEG or PNG from the file manager using LightCraft, or run `lightcraft /path/to/photo.png`.
3. Wait for the import to finish.

For a deterministic isolated reproduction, the settings were initialized with both `"view": "detail"` and `"settings": {"startupView": "detail"}` before launching with one PNG. `ui.inspect` after import reported:

```json
{
  "ui": {
    "view": "photoGrid",
    "settings": {"startupView": "detail"}
  },
  "active": 1,
  "import": null
}
```

## Expected behavior

Honor **Detail View** when launching with a photo and display the requested photo immediately. An already-catalogued image should also be selected and displayed. **Photo Grid** should remain available for users who explicitly select that startup preference.

## Cause visible in the release source

In [v0.14.0 apps/lightcraft/src/main.rs, lines 1038–1045](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/v0.14.0/apps/lightcraft/src/main.rs#L1038), the launch-files branch calls `import::start_paths` …

I bring up crop again, 'aspect ratio' is still 4x5, but the crop area is still the original image aspect ratio. If I click on the dropdown and reselect 4x5, the crop selection updates to 4x5 (or 5x4) as expected and hitting enter will drop it correctly.
